activities.title: 9th FRIEND-Water Global Conference
activities.priority_area_full: Priority Area 1: Scientific Research and Innovation
activities.output_full: 1.1. International scientific cooperation strengthened and fostered to address unsolved problems in hydrology, improving scientific understanding of hydrological cycles across river basins and aquifers.
activities.description: 9th FRIEND-Water Global Conference held from 25-29 September 2023 at the Université Cheikh Anta Diop in Dakar, Senegal. The conference presented a five-day event under the title “Addressing unsolved problems in hydrology for a water-secure world in a changing environment” and addressed scientific topics such as  Ecohydrology, Climate change and Water Resources Resilience, Bridging the Data-knowledge Gaps in Hydrology,  Spatial Hydrology; Large Rivers Management, and Research Priorities for Young Scientists.
activities.key_activity: 1.1.2. Establishment and maintenance of an exchange scheme among UNESCO water family and partners for research on Unsolved Problems and New, Emerging Topics i n Hydrology.
activities.outcomes:
The Conference included two full days of scientific presentations from researchers from various regions, focusing on topics such as Ecohydrology, Climate Change, Open Hydrology, Data collection, Spatial Hydrology, Artificial Intelligence, and Large Rivers Management.
Further, the attendees were given the opportunity to participate in two hands-on trainings, respectively in ‘Ecohydrology and vulnerability modelling’ and ‘Early Warning Systems for hydrological extremes and hydrometry’. These technical trainings were focused on hands-on applications of hydrological models where participants could learn basic functions, GIS commands and data sources for the use of these tools for water-related research.
Also an IHP-IX Workshop was organized with the goal of realigning the FRIEND-Water activities with the outputs of IHP-IX.

activities.description: Through this activity, UNESCO supported the Water Resource Commission to introduce ecohydrology principles to all Lake Bosomtwe Biosphere Reserve stakeholders. UNESCO also contracted a consultant to conduct comprehensive studies and situational analysis to identify and document significant hydrological, ecological, and socio-cultural changes within the Lake Bosomtwe Biosphere Reserve since its designation as a biosphere reserve by UNESCO in 2016. The information and data gathered by the consultant will serve as a source of knowledge for the elaboration of a project proposal to be used for resource mobilization towards the establishment of the lake as an Ecohydrology Demonstration site.
activities.key_activity: 1.2.4. Application of the ecohydrology approach within UNESCO water related designated sites including biosphere reserves, geoparcs and natural heritage sites for sustainability and resilience; p ublishing, sharing and promotion of the research and innovation at UNESCO designated sites through articles, case studies and a compendium of case studies.
activities.outcomes:
A report on the situational analysis has been produced. A draft project proposal has also been produced.
The capacity of stakeholders, including water professionals have been enhanced on the principles of ecohydrology. Representatives of community members, including owners of hospitality businesses around the Lake Biosphere Reserve have been sensitized on the principles of ecohydrology.

activities.title: The 9th International Conference on Flood Management (ICFM9)
activities.priority_area_full: Priority Area 1: Scientific Research and Innovation
activities.output_full: 1.6. Scientific knowledge, methodologies and tools in addressing water related disasters, such as flood and drought elaborated and/or enhanced towards timely forecasting.
activities.description:
The International Conference on Flood Management (ICFM) is held every three years to discuss various issues related to floods and to achieve significant academic and cross-disciplinary changes. 
ICHARM/PWRI hosted the 9th ICFM (ICFM9) at National Graduate Institute for Policy Studies (GRIPS), and the Tsukuba International Congress Center in Tsukuba, Japan, on February 18-22, 2023 in collaboration with two partner organizations of Japan, the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism and the GRIPS. 
A high-level symposium, “Integrated Water Cycle Management in the PostCOVID-19 Era,” was held on February 18, 2023. Approximately 250 people from 40 countries and regions attended. HM the Emperor of Japan graced the first morning session of the symposium with his presence, listening intently and showing high interest with the lectures.
The 4-day conference in Tsukuba was attended by a total of 394 flood experts from 41 counties and area (212 from Japan, 100 from Asia, 78 from the rest of the world, including four unknown). It was consisted of four plenary sessions and 24 parallel sessions, with 143 oral presentations in the parallel sessions and 48 poster presentations. And five special sessions were also held on cross-cutting themes, and eight companies and organizations participated in the technology exhibition to show their unique services and technologies related to flooding. At the closing ceremony, ICHARM Executive Director KOIKE Toshio presented the draft Statement of ICFM9 to the participants.
activities.key_activity: 1.6.2. Science policy dialogue and capacity building on water management that considers wet and dry extremes (floods and drought), including symposia, workshops, and sessions in related events/fora.
activities.outcomes:
Through the ICFM9, the participants shared the latest scientific findings on the increasing frequency and severity of floods and experiences accumulated in various regions, as well as identified scientific and social issues through exchanges of questions and answers. The results are scheduled to be published online in the Proceedings of the International Association of Hydrological Sciences (PIAHS) and in a special issue of the Journal of Flood Risk Management Science (JFRM). 
The ICFM9 statement was also issued. Advocating the mainstreaming of flood risk management, the statement calls for all stakeholders to take bold, transformative action while recognizing resilience to flood disasters as a prerequisite for achieving sustainable development based on a holistic, quantitative understanding of the impact of floods on human and economic factors, including its changes, and the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic. To achieve this goal, the statement also positively proposes adopting the end-to-end approach to cross-sectionally link the latest science with on-site decision-making and action, strengthening the collection, archiving, and sharing of data and information, improving models to analyze increasingly severe floods and their economic impact, promoting knowledge integration, fostering facilitators, and coordinating flood control measures in consideration of social inequalities and the fundamental rights of indigenous people.
The ICFM9 statement was shared at the occasion of the Sixth UN Special Thematic Session on Water and Disasters (STSWD6) and UN 2023 Water Conference on March 2023.

Outcome 4 – Communication, public awareness, capacity and skills on transboundary aquifers and shared groundwater resources diplomacy enhanced. Related outputs: training seminars on legal and institutional frameworks of TBA cooperation organized with a focus on young professionals and future leaders, communication and awareness raising on groundwater strengthened.

activities.title: Capacity Building Training on Utilization of Advanced Laboratory Equipments in Bahirdar
activities.priority_area_full: Priority Area 1: Scientific Research and Innovation
activities.output_full: 1.8. Development and sharing of knowledge and innovative solutions on impr oving water quality and reducing water pollution by the scientific community supported and communicated to support science based decision making, improve knowledge, services and reduce health related risks.
activities.description: The capacity building training was carried out in Bahir Dar in Abbay Basin Development Office laboratory which is under the Ministry of Water and Energy. The training was conducted between 20 June and 4 July 2022 with the training focusing on enhancing the professional skills, basic knowledge on sample preparation, working principle of high-tech analytical instrument (GC MS/MS, HPLC or LC MS and ICP-OES), instrument software familiarization and troubleshooting for mineral and pesticide analysis.
activities.key_activity: 1.8.2. Promotion of innovative tools and policies and capacity building for water quality management and pollution control, by identifying and disseminating innovative, best technological solutions, nature-based solutions and policies for different stakeholders.
activities.outcomes: Ten (10) technical staff from the Ministry of Water and Energy, two (2) of which women, took part in the 15 days training facilitated by Bless Agro and Food Industry PLC, a first private ISO/IEC 17025 accredited Agri Food & Bev testing laboratory in Ethiopia under the auspices of UNESCO. Staff received specialized training and improved their skills and knowledge on how to use various installed sophisticated laboratory equipment in carrying out various biological and physio-chemical analyses to generate reliable analytical data on inorganic and organic pollutants and other relevant environmental matrices. This contributed to achieving UNESCO’s mandate towards strengthening human and institutional capacity of C2C. Furthermore, providing a platform where joint studies by specialists of different fields can be undertaken and further allow for cooperation, cross exchange of information and identification of synergies among different systems in the understanding of the patterns of water/biota interplays, and their importance for societies.

activities.description: Flood and Drought Monitors were further strengthened and expanded to align them with the needs for reliable climate services at the national level for two pilot countries (Zambia and Botswana).

activities.outcomes: Strengthening and expanding Flood and Drought Monitors in Zambia and Botswana have resulted in enhanced capacity for monitoring hydrological extremes. This initiative signifies an alignment with the needs for reliable climate services at the national level, demonstrating a focus on information to address the unique challenges of each pilot country. The outcomes include improved technologies, increased data sources, and refined monitoring systems, contributing to more accurate and timely information for better-informed decision-making in the face of flood and drought risks. Overall, the strengthened monitors represent a significant step toward bolstering resilience and preparedness at the national level in the context of climate variability.

activities.priority_area_full: Priority Area 1: Scientific Research and Innovation
activities.output_full: 1.6. Scientific knowledge, methodologies and tools in addressing water related disasters, such as flood and drought elaborated and/or enhanced towards timely forecasting.
activities.description:
"This short course provides the necessary tools for the development of the African Drought Atlas through the methodology of Regional Frequency Analysis based on L-Moments. The course begins with the concept of drought and various definitions within the field of hydrology. Following this, basic background information on regional frequency analysis is provided, concluding with the incorporation of L-Moments into the procedure.

The course also includes a practical demonstration of a web application designed to create a Drought Atlas tailored for a specific sector."
activities.key_activity: 1.6.5. Synthesis and publications on knowledge, methodologies and tools on drought/floods; organization of the capitalization of knowledge, results and experience available in the UNESCO Water Family, including the Flagships.
activities.outcomes: Course on  the African Drought Atlas provides participants with understanding of drought concepts and various hydrological definitions. It empowers them with the tools for Regional Frequency Analysis, a methodology crucial for analyzing hydrological events in a regional context. The course ensures participants gain proficiency in applying L-Moments, enhancing their ability to characterize the distribution of hydrological data accurately. Furthermore, the inclusion of a practical demonstration of a web application offers hands-on experience in creating a customized Drought Atlas tailored for specific sectors.

activities.description: UNESCO-IHP supported the development of the 7th edition of the Randolph Glacier Inventory. The RGI is a globally complete inventory of glacier outlines (excluding the ice sheets in Greenland and Antarctica). It is a subset of the database compiled by the Global Land Ice Measurements from Space (GLIMS) initiative.
activities.key_activity: 1.7.3. Continued work on the assessments, case studies and associated education and capacity building on snow glaciers and water resources; sediment monitoring; magnitud e and risks linked to land subsidence from global to local level; coastal aquifers, considering the conservation of ecosystem services and multiple risks, including pollution and saltwater intrusion, with specific emphasis on small island developing states.
activities.outcomes: Focus of the RGI is on achieving global coverage, consistency, and proximity in a specific year. The strength of the RGI lies in its ability to handle large numbers of glaciers simultaneously. This allows, for example, for the estimation of glacier volumes and rates of elevation change at regional and global scales, as well as the simulation of cryospheric responses to climatic forcing.
activities.partners: University of Innsbruck

activities.description: IHP provides insights into the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on implementing SDGs 6, 7, 9, 11, and 17, particularly from a hydrological perspective. The pandemic disrupted traditional scientific and educational practices, leading to setbacks in generating hydrological knowledge and training delivery, hindering progress toward the 2030 Development Agenda. However, it also presents opportunities for virtual learning, fostering inclusivity and equity in hydrological education.
activities.key_activity: 5.1.1. Organizing, co-organizing sessions in intergovernmental meetings, UN platforms and processes, and major international and regional events with relevant tailored messages and science-based governance recommendations.
activities.outcomes: Transformative actions such as the IHP IX Strategic Plan, emphasizing scientific research, education, and inclusive water management are provided. Additionally, the proposal for a Science Based Global Water Assessment that aims to address gaps in meeting water-related SDGs, providing actionable solutions and investment opportunities was presented. Moreover, initiatives like the UN-Water SDG 6 Capacity Development Initiative (CDI) and monitoring of SDG indicator 6.5.2 demonstrate coordinated efforts to accelerate progress and enhance transboundary water cooperation.

activities.title: NATURE-BASED SOLUTIONS IN URBAN DRAINAGE UNDER CLIMATE CHANGE CONDITIONS
activities.priority_area_full: Priority Area 4: Integrated Water Resources Management under conditions of Global Change
activities.output_full: 4.3. Conducting and sharing of research on non conventional Water Resources (NCWRs) such as wastewater reuse, desalination, rainwater harvesting, and the Management of Aquifer Recharge (MAR) by the scientific community, in support of improving Water Cycle Management (WCM), strengthening capacities of local, regional, and national decision makers, and enhanced acceptance of public.
activities.description: One of the priority areas defined by the Strategy IHP-IX is Integrated water resources management under conditions of global change. This includes, among others, activities contributing to disseminating knowledge and raising awareness in nature-based solution. The main webinar’s objective was to promote in the scientific community new methodologies and solutions for informed decision-making based on a scientific rationale of the problem, improving knowledge and services and reducing the risks. Year 2022 we are celebrating 75 years of the Jaroslav Cerni Institute for the Development of Water Resources (JCI), which hosts the Centre for Water for Sustainable Development and Adaptation to Climate Change (WSDAC), the webinar was organized to celebrate this occasion. The goal of the webinar was to present innovative nature-based solutions (NBS) to decision-makers, the scientific community and young professionals, and introduce their application in urban water management. The webinar covered the following topics: (1) strategic and planning frameworks for the implementation of nature‐based solutions in urban hydrotechnical infrastructure, (2) urban water management using green strategy and technology, (3) getting to know with natural, nature‐based technologies and general rules for designing, (4) a practical example of designing and implementing green urban infrastructure systems and, (5) access to higher education in the field of eco‐engineering. The webinar was organized as a hybrid model, in Jaroslav Černi Water Institute and online on the Teams platform.
activities.key_activity: 4.3.4. Dissemination and raising awareness and capacity in nature-based solutions; best practices and public acceptance on safe reuse of wastewater, including community engagements; engagement of young professionals to enhance human capacities in MAR, NCWRs and WCM.
activities.outcomes: The key outputs of the meeting are that it is necessary to change the institutional framework that will enable the legal application of such solutions, then resolve the responsibilities and sources of financing the construction, functioning and maintenance of such systems, increase institutional and human capacities through the connection of science and practice, while increasing knowledge about designing and applications of "green solutions", strengthen public participation in decision-making and continue the implementation of joint activities of various interested groups through similar webinars and workshops.

activities.partners: IRTCUD (International Research and Training Centre on Urban Drainage), JAROSLAV ČERNI WATER INSTITUTE, Belgrade, Republic of Serbia
activities.notes: Full report please find on web-site https://wsdac.jcerni.rs/workshop-nature-based-solutions-in-urban-drainage-under-climate-change-conditions/

activities.output_full: 1.7. activities.description:
https://www.gw-sdg2022.fr/index.php/fr/  (see the page of the conference, with key objectives)
A multi-stakeholder conference, that brought together not only groundwater specialists, but also managers of public and private water services, decision-makers, finance managers, industry, NGOs and representatives of civil society... 40 speakers received financial support from UNESCO or IRD for their participation. 31 Technical Sessions (380 oral presentations and posters), 20 Round Tables, 6 Workshops and 4 Training sessions.
activities.key_activity: 1.7.1. Scientific studies, thematic workshops, and science-based support to policy makers and managers on “Water in the Anthropocene” (e.g. Water Management in Coastal Areas; Water and Land Management in Low Lying River Deltas; Aqui fer Systems; Water management in Urban Environments; Management of Hydrosphere-Cryosphere-Climate Change Nexus).
activities.outcomes:
(see the website of the conference for additional recommandations) 
1. The facts and findings: 
Groundwater is invisible, but it plays a key role in achieving many of the MDG targets by 2030.
Drinking water and hygiene (MDG6): close to consumers (via wells, boreholes), groundwater is often of good quality, with positive effects not only on health, but also on education, gender equality, poverty, the economy and governance (MDGs 1, 3, 4, 5, 8, 10,16).
Food production (MDG2). They already account for almost 50% of irrigated agriculture and are also widely used for livestock production: agricultural development is possible while respecting renewable resources, with water-saving techniques and non-polluting practices;
there is a need for information and education on the overexploitation of groundwater due to agricultural use; agriculture is a major factor in the deterioration of groundwater quality.
The biosphere: ecosystems and biodiversity - Aquatic life (MDG14) and ecosystems (MDG15) are largely dependent on groundwater (groundwater/river links and wetlands).
Clean energy (ODD7): harnessing the heat of the subsoil through groundwater (geothermal energy) provides a link to the energy transition and the circular economy (ODD12).

2 - Knowledge of groundwater develops new knowledge and innovations: Basic concepts and laws of the water cycle, fluid transfer and major cycles such as carbon. New techniques for researching, exploiting and monitoring groundwater.
Principles of shared governance, particularly at basin level: to take better account of the global water cycle, groundwater/surface water connections, the cross-border context, the coastal zone...;
with knowledge and understanding of the issues / stakeholders / local level / vernacular knowledge and common sense.
The development of basic rights and rules, participatory science in environmental monitoring - awareness-raising and water policing - taking into account the socio-anthropological dimension and communities in defining the problems to be solved.

activities.priority_area_full: Priority Area 4: Integrated Water Resources Management under conditions of Global Change
activities.output_full: 4.7. Undertaking assessments and developing and sharing of methods to monitor changes in the cryosphere system (glacier, and permafrost), runoff formation from melting glaciers erosion and sediment transport, glacier fed reservoirs such as mountain lakes, and aquifers, by the scientific community supported for improved understanding of their potential use to inform decision makers at all levels
activities.description:
- Complex observations of cryosphere dynamics were organized and successfully carried out in the basis of three high-altitude year-round monitoring stations in the Northern Tien Shan - glaciological “Tuiyksu Glacier” in Kishi Almaty River basin (base station at an altitude of 3500 m), hydrophysical “Big Almaty Lake” (2500 m ) and geocryological “Zhusaly-Kezen” (3400 m) in Ulken Almaty River basin. The key elements of the observation complex are monitoring the mass balance of Tuiyksu glacier with the submission of annual report to the World Glacier Monitoring Service WGMS - Switzerland (duration of continuous series of monitoring data since 1958), monitoring the dynamics of the temperature regime of permafrost in 32 wells the Ulken Almaty river basin (since 1973).
- Scientific research in the frames of mentioned programs has been successfully completed.
activities.key_activity: 4.7.3. Focused research and knowledge generation and dissemination, including International symposium on the scientific understanding on current and future water availability and the risks from highly glacierized basins; IHP position paper to guide forthcoming research.

activities.title: Transboundary water cooperation under SDG indicator 6.5.2: disaggregating data to provide additional insights at the aquifer level
activities.priority_area_full: Priority Area 3: Bridging the data knowledge gap
activities.output_full: 3.1. Development and use of scientific research methods by the scientific community supported to correctly collect, analyze interpret and exchange data.
activities.description:
The acceleration of transboundary water cooperation is essential to support water security and ensure mutual benefits of sustainable development. The way existing Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) monitoring data is used to raise its importance further up political agendas and inform future reporting rounds is therefore crucial to acceleration. Using data extracted from national country reports of SDG indicator 6.5.2 on transboundary water cooperation, we showcase the level of cooperation, as reported, per aquifer to compliment the national approach currently followed by the official SDG framework. Our analysis uncovers a variety of insights and challenges to transboundary aquifer (TBA) cooperation that otherwise might be difficult to visualize through official national reports. Reported aquifer cooperation is often not harmonized across international
borders. A lack of groundwater data and information is a major contributing factor to  uncoordinated reporting, highlighting the importance of a sound scientific baseline. However, harmonization issues are also interlinked to a national focused reporting process where Member States have the right to disagree over the status of their joint cooperation. These results can assist in improving future indicator coverage, both as an awareness raising tool for co-custodian agencies and by countries through direct interventions and coordination with neighbours.
activities.key_activity: 3.1.3. Compilation and harmonization of knowledge products across sources and custodians of data and monitoring systems from collection, validation, analysis, assessment and reporting perspectives, in partnership with WMO; and engagement with the scientific community on the associated needs and the-state-of-the-art to stimulate research and enhance data services.
activities.outcomes: Scientific publication
activities.partners: UNESCO
activities.cross_cutting_wg: ["Groundwater and Human Settlements"]

activities.title: Students’ Scientific Conference under the topic "Water – A Key to development”
activities.priority_area_full: Priority Area 2: Water Education in the Fourth Industrial Revolution including Sustainability
activities.output_full: 2.1. Public s awareness at all levels raised towards better understanding their contribution to the import ant multi functions of water in domestic life, ecosystems and productive development
activities.description:
On March 22, 2023, commemorating World Water Day, the Mongolian National Commission for UNESCO collaborated with the Ministry of Environment and Tourism, the Water Authority, a governmental implementing agency, the Millennium Challenge Corporation in Mongolia, and the National University of Mongolia to convene a Students’ Scientific Conference in Ulaanbaatar. The conference, themed "Water – A Key to Development," took place at the National University of Mongolia. 

As part of the World Water Day 2023 celebrations, the Mongolian National Commission for UNESCO undertook the translation of the United Nations World Water Development Report (WWDR) 2023 from English into Mongolian. During the event, Mr. S.Boldsaikhan, Secretary-General of the Mongolian National Commission of UNESCO, unveiled and presented the WWDR to representatives of pertinent organizations. Additionally, a message from Ms. Irina Bokova, Director-General of UNESCO, in honor of World Water Day was also conveyed.
activities.key_activity: 2.1.1. Country level awareness raising using special days and observances such as World Water Day World Wetlands Day and World Toilet Day, engaging mass media specialists for proper messaging towards target audiences; possibly a dedicated prize (if sponsored by a Member State), among others.
activities.outcomes:
The event aimed to spotlight the highlighted issues and enhance higher education students' awareness of water-related concerns. Its objectives included fostering the exchange of ideas, experiences, and best practices associated with Integrated Water Resources Management (IWRM). Over 100 students and youths from diverse universities actively engaged in the event.

Elevating awareness about water management issues, consumption patterns, and wastewater treatment stands as a critical endeavor for Mongolia's sustainable future, particularly among younger generations. Given that today's university students are tomorrow's leaders, their ideas and innovations will shape Mongolia's approach to addressing developmental challenges in the foreseeable future.

activities.title: International Conference on Ancestral Hydrotechnologies as a Response to Climate, Health and Food Emergencies
activities.priority_area_full: Priority Area 4: Integrated Water Resources Management under conditions of Global Change
activities.output_full: 4.4. Development and sharing of knowledge on using the source to sea and nexus approaches by the scientific c ommunity supported, and capacities strengthened to improve integrated water resources management for all watersheds, including transboundary ones
activities.description:
Throughout history, ancestral civilizations designed and built sophisticated water systems based on the natural hydrological cycle. These "Hydrotechnologies" provided an adaptive response to cope with issues such as water conservation, irrigation or flood and drought control, but also with biodiversity conservation and local/regional sustainable development. Good examples of this type of systems, some of them still in use today, can be found all over the world: the Zenú Channels or "camellones" in Colombia, the Incas Hydraulic Wonders in Peru and the Persian Qanat in Iran, to name a few. These ancestral Hydro-technologies can be analyzed from a present-day viewpoint to assess their viability as appropriate technologies in a global climate, health and food emergency context. If properly managed, these technologies could become an effective solution for adaptation and inclusion as multifunctional tools for diffuse pollution management, food and health security, flood and drought control, ecosystem services, biodiversity conservation and economic development, among others.
The conference was hosted by the UNESCO Chair on Sustainability of the Polytechnical University of Catalonia (UPC) and co-convened by the Intergovernmental Hydrological Programme (IHP) of UNESCO and the Global Network of Water Museums (a flagship Initiative of UNESCO-IHP). It was supported by the Ministry for Ecological Transition and Demographic Challenge (MITERD) of Spain, the Dept. of External Action of the Generalitat de Catalunya, the Barcelona City Council and MedCites.
activities.key_activity: 4.4.3. Research on synergies and tradeoffs among the societal goals related to water management (e.g. water-environment-energy-food-health); and compilation and dissemination, including through conferences/symposia/workshops, of best nexus practices, including wastewater reuse and byproducts (nutrients, energy) in a circular economy context.
activities.outcomes: 50 specialists from 21 countries and different fields of knowledge, met in Barcelona, from 16 to 17 February 2023, in the International Conference "Ancestral Hydro-technologies as a Response to Climate, Health and Food Emergencies. Good Practices in the Mediterranean and in Latin America and the Caribbean”. 29 good practices were presented on the hybrid conference (virtual and in person, at Campus Nord UPC, Barcelona), that brought together water professionals, water institutions, national and local authorities and academia to discuss the potential of ancestral hydro-technologies as integrated solutions for adaptation and transformation of the territories.

activities.partners: Intergovernmental Hydrological Programme of UNESCO (UNESCO-IHP), Global Network of Water Museums (a flagship Initiative of UNESCO-IHP), UNESCO Chair ‘Water, Heritage and Sustainable Development’ (Ca’ Foscari Univ. of Venice),

activities.title: DETERMINACION A LA VULNERABLIDAD A  LA SEQUIA EN EL PERU
activities.priority_area_full: Priority Area 5: Water Governance based on Science Mitigation, Adaptation and Resilience
activities.output_full: 5.3. Sciences based assessment and development of guidelines, for strengthening water related content in Nationally Determined Contributions and National Adaptation Plans, conducted to strengthen water based climate policy action nexus for adaptation and mitig ation.
activities.description: El presente estudio tuvo por objetivo determinar áreas vulnerables a la sequía en el Perú desde un enfoque multidimensional, utilizando indicadores sociales, económicos y ambientales. La metodología consistió en nueve pasos: desde identificación de la zona de estudio, selección de indicadores disponibles, y procesamiento de la información (Paso 1, 2 y 3), posteriormente se realiza el análisis de pesos, normalización de indicadores y ajuste a la función de distribución de probabilidad “Beta” (pasos 4, 5, 6 y 7), finalmente se realiza la clasificación de grado de vulnerabilidad y mapeo (paso 8 y 9).
activities.key_activity: 5.3.3. Development of a science-based framework and guidelines for the assessment and inclusion of surface and groundwater related and ecohydrology related content s in NDCs and NAPs.
activities.outcomes: Producto; INFORME TECNICO, cuyo resultados muestran que, los departamentos de La Libertad y Ancash presentaron los mayores porcentajes de distritos con "Alta" vulnerabilidad, registrando un 31.33 % y 35.54 %, respectivamente. En la región sierra, todos los departamentos exhiben más del 30 % de sus distritos con "Alta" y "Muy Alta" vulnerabilidad. Igualmente, en la selva peruana, Amazonas, San Martín y Madre de Dios, se identifica un preocupante de 40.48 %, 40.26 %, y 63.64 % de distritos clasificados como "Alta" vulnerabilidad

activities.title: Be Resilient South Africa Project -  Citizen Sciences Component. The implemented activities forms part of the Be Resilient South Africa Project which aims to address climate risk and build adaptive capacity in SA's Biosphere Reserves.
activities.priority_area_full: Priority Area 1: Scientific Research and Innovation
activities.output_full: 1.10. Conducting and sharing of research on integrating citizen science in the hydrological discipline by the scient ific community and other stakeholders supported, to improve understanding of the water cycle enabling science based decision making
activities.description:
Citizen Sciences Component of the Be Resilient South Africa Project aims to strengthen data and knowledge management, research, capacity building with communities, and partnerships. 

The main activity under this component is the River Monitoring in 4 South African Biosphere Reserves
The activities include the following:
-Joint contextualization of the water quality and quantity problems in biosphere reserves involving youth, interested in Environmental Science 
-Co-creation of river monitoring programmes for the Eerste, Luvuvhu, Sand, Blyde and Marico catchments with the youth and biosphere reserves leads. 
-Training and capacity building for monitoring of water indicators including – miniSASS, pH, Dissolved Oxygen, E-coli, Electric Conductivity, Temperature, Turbidity, and stream flow. 
- Development, training, and use of a Smartphone Data Collection Application to capture citizen science data
- Development of understanding of catchment dynamics to enable a comprehensive mapping of causes of decline in water quality and availability. 
-Development of partnerships
activities.key_activity: 1.10.4. Continued Research and Development and capacity building work, including development of a citizen science toolbox, its promotion through training programmes and in cooperation with non-governmental organizations as catalysts.
activities.outcomes:
Outputs
Citizen Science Data Collection and Visualization Platform: A mobile smartphone application specifically designed for citizen science data collection and visualization. This tool includes features for monitoring various water indicators such as miniSASS, pH, Dissolved Oxygen, E-coli, Electric Conductivity, Temperature, Turbidity, and stream flow.
Training, and Capacity Building Materials and Reports- Development and dissemination of training materials aimed at building the capacity of both the youth and biosphere reserve leads in monitoring water indicators. This includes the use of the training of various water indicators, smartphone applications, and Participatory Catchment Mapping Programmes
Partnerships - The establishment of partnerships among various stakeholders involved in the project, fostering collaboration and shared responsibility for effective river monitoring and environmental management.
Outcomes:
Strengthened Data and Knowledge Management through improved data collection, management, and knowledge dissemination related to water quality in the Biosphere Reserves.
Enhanced research and data collection - The project contributes to scientific research by providing valuable data on water indicators and catchment dynamics, helping to identify causes of decline in water quality. 
Capacity building through increased knowledge and skills among youth and biosphere reserve leads in environmental science and river monitoring, contributing to the development of local expertise.

activities.title: IHP Training Course in Kyoto
activities.priority_area_full: Priority Area 2: Water Education in the Fourth Industrial Revolution including Sustainability
activities.output_full: 2.4. Development and sharing of methods and tools based on new practices by the scientific community supported to translate scientific information into a format facilitating education, decision making and policy formulation.
activities.description:
The 32nd and 33rd IHP Training Course (IHP TC) on integrated basin management under changing climate was organized in 2022 and 2023 at Disaster Prevention Research Institute (DPRI), Kyoto University. This training course is organized by Kyoto University in cooperation with the UNESCO Jakarta Office under the objectives of IHP-9, and is also part of the educational activities of the Kyoto University UNESCO Chair WENDI. The TC aims to present various aspects of water resources and water-related disasters under climate change for participants from Asia-Pacific regions as a part of Japanese contribution to the UNESCO IHP-IX. The TC consists of a series of lectures, exercises including self-paced practicing of various software and a field visit for the target river basin. 
   The online training course is oriented to the study of integrated basin management: hydrological extreme analysis, hydrological measurements, assessing the impacts of climate change, rainfall-runoff-inundation modelling, reservoir sustainability, optimum operation and management, as well as knowledge of the interrelationship with river ecosystem and environment. Development of resilient society has become an inevitable issue under the recent climate change that is increasing the frequency of extreme phenomena such as unprecedented floods and severe droughts. In order to make our society more resilient for such unprecedented extremes, social adaptation and countermeasure are required based on technologies for prediction and vulnerability assessments to meet the requirements of future water availability under changing climate.
activities.key_activity: 2.4.2. Capacity building modules, training material, and communications tools on ensuring stakeholder trust and engagement in water management.
activities.outcomes: The TCs gave an opportunity for participants: 1) to acquire the latest knowledge on climate change impacts on water resources, water and weather-related disasters, hydrological measurements of large river basins and ecosystem services, 2) to make a practice on rainfall-runoff-inundation analysis at river basin scale, and 3) to discuss effective strategies of integrated basin management based on scientific knowledge to realize a resilient society under climate change.
activities.institution: Water Resources Research Center, Disaster Prevention Research Institute, Kyoto University
activities.partners: UNESCO Chair (WENDI)

activities.description:
The Regional Center for Water Security under the auspices of UNESCO and the Water Network of the National Autonomous University of Mexico, in collaboration with the Coordination of the Open University, Educational Innovation and Distance Education (CUAIEED), designed the Massive Open Online Course on Water Security available on Coursera. The main objective of this course is to analyze the elements of the concept of water security to promote its adoption across plans and implementation strategies currently developed by different stakeholders, at different scales.
Over five weeks, participants will explore the definition of water security, as well as the challenges and opportunities to move towards more sustainable water management. The course is organized into five modules: 1) Definition of Water Security; 2) Challenges for Universal access to water and sanitation services; 3) Water as a key element for sustainable development and economic growth; 4) Ecohydrology; and 5) Water-related disasters.

This course was designed with the objective of helping participants identify the elements that make up the comprehensive approach to hydro-smart cities and learn about their challenges and possibilities in various contexts. It was developed by the UNAM, through the Water Network and the Coordination of the Open University, Educational Innovation and Distance Education (CUAIEED), in collaboration with the Regional Center for Water Security under the auspices of UNESCO (CERSHI) and Agua Capital, aims to respond to such challenges through innovation in the digital age.

It has the participation of experts from the sector, who share their knowledge from various areas, such as government, private initiative, civil society and academia.

activities.title: Strengthening sustainable water resources management of Subak Bengkel as best practices to support Subak system sustainability in Tabanan Regency in dealing with the challenges of climate change impacts
activities.priority_area_full: Priority Area 4: Integrated Water Resources Management under conditions of Global Change
activities.output_full: 4.6. Undertaking and sharing assessment of ecosystem services and environmental flows in ecohydrology pilot sites by the scientific community supported, to improve integrated water resources management.
activities.description: Historically, Subak is a community organization specializing in the irrigation system used in rice farming in Bali Island, Indonesia. In 2012, Subak was declared as a Cultural Landscape World Heritage Site by UNESCO, based on the fulfillment of three outstanding values consisting of: a long and excellent cultural history; a concept of Tri Hita Karana still in place; and a good governance of Subak management. This designation is an effort to protect this important heritage from extinction in the future. Subak's strength lies in its shared dependence on irrigation water and is also united by culture in the manifestation of the Subak Temple binding together physical, cultural, and spiritual interests. Subak, nowadays, has severe challenges among others: the use of chemicals affecting soil fertility; tourism activities encouraging land conversion; upstream development declining water quality; the potential for natural disasters; and climate change triggering rainfall fluctuation. To manage a section of the Subak System, it was designed to culturally perform structures, which are classified as utilization of water. The subak system emerged with the philosophy of Tri Hita Karana (three happiness) consisting of palemahan (environment, rice fields, flora, and fauna), pawongan (farmers), and Narayanan (subak culture) contained as wisdom. The assumed tangible material and ecological effects are: (1) Reduce water pollution and sedimentation; (2) Mitigate water discharge fluctuation; and (3) Minimize crop failure inside Subak.
activities.key_activity: 4.6.2. Development/dissemination of case studies from current ecohydrology sites to improve the understanding of water ecosystem human interactions and highlight ecohydrology-NBS synergies.
activities.outcomes:
Multiple Ecohydrological Nature-based Solutions (Ecohydrological biotechnologies) have been implemented, including household waste segregation, waste and sediment trapping, bioremediation, natural predators and refugia plants for pests’ eradication, organic fertilizer uses, and cultural ceremony in water management.
•	Household waste segregation. Household waste is segregated into organic and inorganic waste. Organic waste will be processed into organic fertilizer for agricultural activities. While inorganic waste will be traded in different ways depending on compounding materials such as plastic, glasses, cans etc.
•	Waste and sediment trapping. Waste and sediment traps installed in secondary or tertiary irrigation waterways can screen, slow down and remove waste, sediment, and pollutants from water as well as improve water quality in catchments. 
•	Bioremediation. Bioremediation using of aquatic plants such as Water Hyacinth (Eichhornia Crassipes) proven to reduce contaminants, pollutants, and toxins from water, and other environments. 
•	Natural predators and refugia plants for pests’ eradication. Utilization of natural predators such as Owl (Tyto alba) and Refugia plants such as red rose balsam (Impatient balsamina) permit to reduce pests’ problems and chemical pesticides application.
•	Organic fertilizer. Changing habits to organic fertilizer applications are beneficial for different aspect such as soil microorganisms’ revival, soil structure and fertility maintenance, water-soil preservation, plants nutrient provision, and land productivity improvement.
•	Water cultural ceremony. During land preparations, the farmers will conduct Magpag Toya ceremony (picking water ceremony) at the water source of subak (located at the river, water division, or water spring). These activities present the farmer respect to the water (irrigation water).

activities.title: Second Forum on DRR – Water related disasters
activities.priority_area_full: Priority Area 5: Water Governance based on Science Mitigation, Adaptation and Resilience
activities.output_full: 5.5. Capacities of the scientific community and decision makers strengthened on new frameworks and tools, to underpin water governance and build resilience.
activities.description:
Sudan remains a large, protracted humanitarian and protection crisis country, and the severity and scale of needs are far reaching. Conflicts, food insecurity, and Climate Change have further exacerbated situation, with Sudan being one of the most vulnerable countries to the impact of Climate Change considering that more than 80% of the agriculture is rain fed and urbanization is not based on appropriate water management systems. Thus, it is becoming annually impacted by floods that have claimed many lives and property. Furthermore, drought is one of the causes of conflict in Darfur and in Red Sea State where water scarcity contributed to escalation of civil unrest and clashes. Therefore, the National Council of Civil Defense is developing Early Warning System for Natural Disasters, where this project shall contribute toward building collaboration with all potential partners for Early Warning System and disaster risk reduction for Floods and Droughts being a priority that have had devastating impact on Sudan for years.

Thus, UNESCO Khartoum office collaborated with the National Council of Civil Defence in Sudan in strengthening Early Warning Systems for Floods and Drought that included several coordination efforts including the organization of the second Forum on DRR – Water related disasters from 13-14 February 2023 with over 100 participants.
activities.key_activity: 5.5.1. Engagement with the science community and decision makers for state-of-the-art research, publications and capacity building on new and emerging frameworks and tools to support water governance and build resilience, including support to accelerate the Agenda 2063 of the African Union.
activities.outcomes:
The forum provided an opportunity for experts, policymakers, and community members to come together and share their experiences and knowledge about water-related disasters. It highlighted the importance of community engagement in disaster preparedness and response and the need for coordinated action at the local, national, and international levels. The strategies developed during the breakout session will serve as a valuable resource for communities seeking to address water-related disasters in the future.
In conclusion, the forum for water-related disasters was a success and provided valuable insights and strategies for mitigating the impact of these disasters on communities. The questionnaire and evaluation results were an important part of this process, providing valuable feedback on the effectiveness of disaster preparedness and management efforts in Sudan.

activities.title: Développement de scénarios de changement climatique et analyse d’impact à Ntoumanalyse Ntoum
activities.priority_area_full: Priority Area 5: Water Governance based on Science Mitigation, Adaptation and Resilience
activities.output_full: 5.2. Integration of sound science in water governance instruments improved reflecting adaptation to climate change and IWRM, integrating surface and groundwater fo r their uptake by decision makers.
activities.description: L'UNESCO, en collaboration avec l'Institut Deltares, a mené une étude visant à évaluer la vulnérabilité de la production d'eau potable face au changement climatique à Libreville et ses environs. L'approche utilisée, la méthodologie CRIDA, implique une analyse participative ascendante pour identifier les risques actuels et futurs pour la sécurité de l'eau. Les objectifs du projet comprennent l'analyse des effets du changement climatique sur les ressources en eau dans le bassin de la Nzémé et le développement d'une stratégie d'adaptation. Une chaîne de modélisation a été mise en place pour évaluer la résilience du système face aux développements futurs, en utilisant un générateur de données météorologiques pour simuler différentes conditions climatiques.
activities.key_activity: 5.2.1. Publication and dissemination of case studies on science-informed water governance for management of surface and groundwater, in IWRM context and for climate change adaptation, also linking with experimental research basins and the UNESCO Water Family.
activities.outcomes:
Key Outputs:

- Analyse des effets du changement climatique sur les ressources en eau dans le bassin de la Nzémé, en amont de l'usine d'eau potable de Ntoum.
- Développement d'une stratégie d'adaptation pour maintenir ou améliorer la sécurité de l'eau dans le futur.
- Renforcement des capacités sur l'usage des tests de stress climatique pour le développement de stratégies d'adaptation.

Key Outcomes:

- Identification des risques potentiels pour la sécurité de l'eau dans les conditions climatiques actuelles et futures.
- Amélioration de la gestion des ressources en eau pour garantir des débits nécessaires et améliorer la desserte en eau des différents quartiers de Libreville et ses environs.
- Développement de capacités locales pour évaluer et répondre aux défis posés par le changement climatique sur la disponibilité de l'eau.
activities.institution: Ministère de l'Energie et des Ressources Hydrauliques
activities.partners: Ministère de l'Energie et des Ressources Hydrauliques et le Ministre des Eaux, des Forêts, de la Mer, de l’Environnement, Chargé du Plan Climat, et du Plan d’Affectation des Terres

De plus, elle est en cohérence avec l'Activité Clé 5.2.4, qui met l'accent sur le renforcement des capacités des parties prenantes dans la mise en œuvre d'une gouvernance de l'eau solide et adaptative.

activities.title: RENFORCEMENT DES CAPACITES DES RESSOURCES HUMAINES DU SECTEUR DE L’EAU ET DE L’ASSAINISSEMENT AU GABON
activities.priority_area_full: Priority Area 2: Water Education in the Fourth Industrial Revolution including Sustainability
activities.output_full: 2.6. Capacities of decision makers, and water managers and key water sector institutions strengthened allowing them to take advantage of new technologies and resea rch to enhance better decisions, design and implementation of integrated and efficient water policies
activities.description: Ce projet vise à renforcer les capacités dans le secteur de l'eau potable, de l'assainissement et de la gestion intégrée des ressources en eau au Gabon, en réponse aux défis d'accès insuffisant aux services d'eau potable, à la nécessité d'améliorer la Gestion Intégrée des Ressources en Eau (GIRE) et au déficit global de capacités. Initié par l'UNESCO en collaboration avec des ministères partenaires gabonais, le programme de formation cible des professionnels de cinq entités clés du secteur. Les objectifs comprennent le développement de compétences en gestion durable de l'eau, l'utilisation de données de télédétection pour la gestion des ressources en eau, le renforcement des capacités institutionnelles et la promotion de stratégies pour une gestion durable de l'eau face au changement climatique. Les formations, dispensées de manière virtuelle en raison de la pandémie de Covid-19, ont abouti au renforcement des compétences des participants dans divers domaines liés à la gestion de l'eau.
activities.key_activity: 2.6.2. Building capacity to mainstream research recommendations and relevant technology including nature-based solutions/ecohydrology in decision making for middle/ upper-level civil servants, water managers, and professionals.
activities.outcomes:
Outputs:

- Renforcement des compétences des professionnels du secteur de l'eau potable, de l'assainissement et de la gestion intégrée des ressources en eau.
- Utilisation accrue de données de télédétection et de systèmes d'information pour la gestion des ressources en eau.
- Développement de capacités institutionnelles et humaines pour favoriser la réglementation et la gestion durable de l'eau.
- Promotion de stratégies pour une gestion durable de l'eau face aux défis du changement climatique.

Outcomes:

- Amélioration de la gestion durable de la ressource en eau à l'échelle locale et nationale.
- Capacité accrue à faire face aux problèmes liés à l'eau en utilisant des outils de télédétection et des systèmes d'information.
- Renforcement des compétences dans l'évaluation des ressources en eau, tant pour le petit que pour le grand cycle de l'eau.
- Capacité à élaborer des stratégies pour une gestion intelligente et durable de l'eau.

activities.title: Integrated Water Resource Management for Bhutan’s Future Water Security for Cities and Climate Resilient Development
activities.priority_area_full: Priority Area 4: Integrated Water Resources Management under conditions of Global Change
activities.output_full: 4.5. Understanding and knowledge on pollutants sources, fate and transp ort in freshwater systems, including surface waters (rivers, lakes, wetlands) and groundwater improved by the scientific community and UNESCO Water Family to prevent and reduce water pollution and underpin water resources management strategies.
activities.description: The project supported the government of Bhutan to strengthen capacity to monitor water quality by installing 4 pilot ambient water quality monitoring sensors at the Thimphu and Paru Rivers. These sensors for the first time in Bhutan are providing real-time data on pH, dissolved oxygen, conductivity, turbidity, total dissolved solids, salinity, and temperature. This was followed by the capacity building workshops to train 20 participants to learn approaches to optimizing river monitoring; and interpretation of data and understanding different monitoring protocols. Further 30 technicians were trained in troubleshooting and equipment maintenance including software applications used for data management and visualization.
activities.key_activity: 4.5.2. Knowledge generation and research on global change impacts on water quality (e.g. linking to relevant projects).
activities.outcomes: The project supported the government of Bhutan to strengthen capacity to monitor river water quality. The installed sensors for the first time in Bhutan are providing real-time data on pH, dissolved oxygen, conductivity, turbidity, total dissolved solids, salinity, and temperature. The project trained 20 government officials to learn approaches to optimizing river monitoring; and interpretation of data and understanding different monitoring protocols. Further 30 technicians were trained in troubleshooting and equipment maintenance including software applications used for data management and visualization.

The 15th session of the Arab Ministerial Council on Water (Riyadh, 19-23 Nov, 2023)  adopted the outcome of the UNESCO meeting and asked LAS and ACSAD to incorporate the outcome in the implementation plan of the Arab Strategy for water Security.

activities.title: Strengthening UNESCO Water Family in the Arab Region
activities.priority_area_full: Priority Area 5: Water Governance based on Science Mitigation, Adaptation and Resilience
activities.output_full: 5.1. Awareness raising of decision makers at all levels on the importance of science based water governance by the UNESCO Water Family supported, to enhance the overall resi lience of communities to effects of global change.
activities.description:
CAI/HYD successfully organized The 19th Regional Meeting of the IHP NATCOMs in the Arab Countries (Cairo, Egypt; 14-16 November 2023) with the participation of 13 Arab counties. The meeting discussed the possible action plan to activate the involvement of the Arab IHP national committees in the operational workplan of IHP-9 in the Arab region and to strengthen the IHP-9 program presence at the national and regional levels. It also reviewed national research activities, programs and projects related to water in the relevant member states, the main axes of the program, and the role of committees and members in cooperation and interoperability in the implementation of activities. The countries presentations showed the significant effort of the Arab counties in the sustainable management of water resources in the Arab region through climate change adaption and promoting non-conventional water resources management. It was suggested that UNESCO Cairo will lead the organization of number of webinars in key areas such as wastewater treatment and desalination, climate change adaptation, Artificial intelligence application in water management and transboundary rivers, drought, rain and floods forecasting maps.   
The UNESCO Regional Office in Cairo and the UNESCO Office in Baghdad participated in the Third Baghdad Water Conference, where UCO/HYD gave a presentation on capacity-building programs in the field of water carried out by UNESCO including website for open learning.
activities.key_activity: 5.1.1. Organizing, co-organizing sessions in intergovernmental meetings, UN platforms and processes, and major international and regional events with relevant tailored messages and science-based governance recommendations.
activities.outcomes: A major achievement of UCO/HYD is the partnership with the IHP secretariat, the UNESCO Climate Taskforce and UCO/ADM on organizing UNESCO presence at the COP27, held in Sharm Elsheikh (Nov 8-17, 2022). UCO/HYD also represented the IHP secretariat in sessions organized by IAEA (Wetlands) and the Government of Egypt (Water Day- Green Water), along with supporting the Secretariat in curating the IHP/ESCWA curated thematic during COP27.

activities.title: National Youth Water Award 2022
activities.priority_area_full: Priority Area 4: Integrated Water Resources Management under conditions of Global Change
activities.output_full: 4.1. Conducting and sharing of research on inclusive and participatory approaches by the scientific community, to ensu re open, active, meaningful gender responsive engagement of youth, local and indigenous communities supported to enable all stakeholders to be part of the water management process.
activities.description: Mexico's National Youth Water Prize (PNJA) funnels students aged 15-20 into the Stockholm Junior Water Prize, organized by the Stockholm International Water Institute (SIWI). PNJA aims to spark student interest in water research, cultivate future water leaders, and encourage solutions to local, regional, and global water challenges – all through teamwork and interdisciplinary approaches.
activities.key_activity: 4.1.1. Conducting and sharing scientific research in inclusive and participatory water management with gender emphasis and engagement of youth, local and indigenous communities, e.g. in selected demonstration sites (such as Ecohydrology demosites, CRIDA applications and UNESCO designated sites); studies and country level pilots including stock take on stakeholder participation in water management at all levels, and a country pilot showcasing modalities and benefits of engagement.
activities.outcomes: The 2022 edition of the PNJA witnessed remarkable participation with 309 submitted projects. Following a rigorous selection process, eight regional representatives were chosen to compete at the national level. Ultimately, Alonso Hernández emerged as the winner of the national phase, earning the honor of representing Mexico at the Stockholm Junior Water Prize.
activities.institution: CERSHI, National Autonomous University of Mexico and Embassy of Sweden in Mexico
activities.partners: yes
activities.notes: The representative of Mexico, Alonso Hernández, presented his project "Discovery of thermostable PET degrading enzymes from metagenomes" during World Water Week in Stockholm. In addition, he was awarded a six-month scholarship to improve his project with the help of a specialist from the National Autonomous University of Mexico.

Finally, in the closing session, an analysis on water security in the context of the 2030 Agenda was provided.

activities.title: 2025 International Year of Glaciers Preservation
activities.priority_area_full: Priority Area 4: Integrated Water Resources Management under conditions of Global Change
activities.output_full: 4.7. Undertaking assessments and developing and sharing of methods to monitor changes in the cryosphere system (glacier, and permafrost), runoff formation from melting glaciers erosion and sediment transport, glacier fed reservoirs such as mountain lakes, and aquifers, by the scientific community supported for improved understanding of their potential use to inform decision makers at all levels
activities.description: In December 2022, the UNGA adopted the resolution (UNGA Resolution 77/443) to declare 2025 as the UN International Year of Glaciers’ Preservation (IYGP25), accompanied by the proclamation of March 21st of each year as the World Day for Glaciers starting in 2025. UNESCO and WMO were invited to facilitate the implementation of the International Year and observance of the World Day for Glaciers
activities.key_activity: 4.7.1. Assessment of snow, glaciers permafrost and surface and groundwater resources in selected regions; supported by compilation of an inventory of mountain related water hazards Early Warning Systems, including for Glacial Lake Outburst Floods (GLOFS)
activities.outcomes:
UNESCO and WMO  co-organized a brainstorming session with 100+ partners from 16 countries from research organizations, international and UN organizations, NGOs and other stakeholders in July 2023 in UNESCO headquarters, Paris and co-developed a roadmap for the implementation, along with a list of representative activities that could be carried out towards and during the IYGP25. Several outreach activities including the during the 42nd UNESCO General conference partnership hub, One Polar summit and COP 28 were organized.   Terms of Reference for Task Teams have been developed to lead specific topics, as well as Terms of Reference for an Advisory Board (to be co-led by WMO and UNESCO, with leaders of the Task Teams and other partner organizations), to oversee the implementation of the IYGP25 and the World Day for Glaciers 2025.

Following the concept note and identified activities and interests, a “Call for Expression of Interest for the IYGP 2025 Task Forces” was launched in December 2023. A kick-off meeting for the Task Forces was held online on 24 January 2024 where the results of the call were presented and draft workplans for the Task Forces were introduced to interested organizations. 

Based on the expression of interest received the four Task Forces have been established as follows:
·	TF-1: Global Campaign for International Year of Glaciers' Preservation 2025
·	TF-2: International Conference on Glaciers' Preservation, Regional Workshops and Capacity Building
·	TF-3: Research and Monitoring Initiatives
·	TF-4: Policy Advocacy, Partnerships and Resource Mobilization
The advisory board will be established by UNESCO and WMO, which will include the task Force leads.

activities.title: Titicaca Aqua Watch: Indigenous Empowerment for Environmental Justice
activities.priority_area_full: Priority Area 1: Scientific Research and Innovation
activities.output_full: 1.5. Undertaking and sharing assessments on the interaction between humans and water, in line with socio hydrology by the scientific community supported to develop adaptive pathways, scenarios and strategies for water management
activities.description:
The project is focused on water quality citizen science in the indigenous communities of Chojasivi, situated along the shores of Lake Titicaca in Bolivia. Our initiative aims to empower Aymara indigenous communities to monitor the pollution affecting their environment effectively.
In collaboration with four indigenous communities in Chojasivi, we are undertaking a comprehensive effort to assess and understand the water quality challenges facing Lake Titicaca. Through the application of citizen science methodologies, community members are  actively involved in data collection, analysis, and interpretation.
By providing training, resources, and support, the project seeks to foster a sense of ownership and responsibility among indigenous community members towards the local environment. Through their participation in monitoring activities, these communities gain valuable insights into the trends of contamination in Lake Titicaca, enabling informed advocacy efforts for environmental justice.
The approach prioritizes collaboration, scientific attention, and respect for indigenous knowledge systems. By working hand in hand with the communities of Chojasivi, we aim to contribute to a more holistic understanding of water quality issues in Lake Titicaca and support the empowerment of indigenous peoples in advocating for their environmental rights.
activities.key_activity: 1.5.3. Conducting and supporting scientific research to assess the interaction between humans, environment and water, in line with socio-hydrology within an urban rural setting and develop adaptive pathways, scenarios and strategies for water management.
activities.outcomes:
1. Community-Generated Data: a dataset on water quality indicators in Lake Titicaca is being compiled. This data, collected using citizen science methodologies, serves as a foundation for understanding pollution dynamics impacting the local ecosystem and Lake Titicaca.
2. Capacity Building: Indigenous communities participating in the project are equipped with the necessary training and resources to monitor and analyze water quality parameters. This enhances the communities' technical skills and contemporary environmental literacy.
3. Local Environmental Awareness: community members gain firsthand insights into the trends of contamination in their own community and Lake Titicaca. This reinforced awareness enables advocating for environmental justice.
4. Holistic Understanding: More comprehensive understanding of water quality issues in Lake Titicaca. By integrating indigenous knowledge systems with scientific methodologies, we attempt to develop a perspective that acknowledges the complexities of environmental challenges in the region.
5. Empowerment and Advocacy: Our project support the empowerment of indigenous peoples by amplifying their voices in advocating for their environmental rights. By actively involving community members in monitoring activities we aim to empower them to promote the sustainable management of Lake Titicaca's water resources.

activities.title: Groundwater Research
activities.priority_area_full: Priority Area 2: Water Education in the Fourth Industrial Revolution including Sustainability
activities.output_full: 2.5. Capacities of skilled professionals and techn icians at water related tertiary and vocational education strengthened to identify the main gaps for sustainable water management towards providing appropriate tools to governments and societies to address those gaps and the Agenda 2030 targets.
activities.description:
1. With ESGUSA Project, UWC managed to implement on activities that focused on groundwater recharge activities such as focussed recharge, groundwater modeling, groundwater development when 4 boreholes were drilled for research. Groundwater geophysics and groundwater monitorung activities were carried out in the Limpopo Province of South Africa
2. With MARSA Project, UWC focussed on managed aquifer recharge in the WestCoast of South Africa where geophysics, monitoring, modeling activities were carried out to inform the developmebt of groundwater managed aquifer recharge for augmenting the drinking water supply.
3. With CSIR, the UWC implemented standardised methodlogy for aquifer characterisation of aquifer study in the 3 transboundary aquifer basins, namely, the Zambezi, Limpopo and the Orange-Vaal-Sengu basins where groundwater governance in addition to modeling, hydraulics, geophysics activities among others were implemented
4. With DWS, UWC implemented refinement of the methodology for groundwater resources directed measures (GRDM) and updated software methodology for GRDM in the Berg and Heuningnes catchments in Western Cape of South Africa in addition to generating groundwater information to improve the protection of groundwater resources in the studied catchment and beyond
5. With NRF, The UWC implemented water education project in selected schools in Limpopo province of South Africa with various activities on stalkholder engagement with communities
6. With WRC, UWC implemented Groundwater Discharge with a focus on springs activities and GW-SW Interaction study in the Cape Agulhas Area in the Western Cape of South Africa. Groundwater management and governance activities and Citizen science activities were implemented.
activities.key_activity: 2.5.3. Capacity building to bridge education policy gaps in water and sustainable development by equipping professionals and technicians with relevant tools and knowledge.
activities.outcomes:
With ESGUSA and MARSA, UWC produced project reports, thesis reports, journal papers, conference presentations, trained Masters and Postdoctoral scholars. Developed human capacity and strengthened research collaboration with Denmark, DWS, IWMI, local communities among others. The impact on communities and researchers and practitioners was visible.
 
 With CSIR, the UWC developed a  standardised methodology for carrying out aquifer characterisation of aquifer in transboundary water resources areas;  developed legal aspects and established legal precedents through formal dispute mechanisms in the water governance. Improved collaboration on research and water education and human strengtheing initiatives among staff members from the education institutions[University of the Western Cape], research institution [CSIR] and government institutions[DWS]

With DWS, UWC  refined the methodology for groundwater resources directed measures (GRDM) and updated software methodology for GRDM. step-by-step tarining manuals were developed. Trainings were carried on the use of the updated methodology and software. The impact in the water sector on the use of updated methodology and software for improved groundwater protection activities were anticipated to spread in all South Africa catchment and beyond.

With NRF, UWC improved the water education teaching approach in the selected schools in Limpopo province of South Africa. This approach is anticipated to influence curriculum modification on water education. The impact on such activities are long life among the learners.

With WRC, UWC produced project reports, published journal papers, trained Masters and Doctoral students via capacity building initiatives, improved citizen science, science engagement and stalkholder engagement among via community meetings.

activities.output_full: 1.7. Development and sharing of knowledge base on the impacts of global change and human usage on river and lake basins, aquifer systems, coastal areas, and cryosphere and human settlements by the scientific community supported so as to embed it in water resources and services management plans.
activities.description: This course provided theoretical and practical concepts for sediment management to prevent erosion and sediment transport to water bodies, determine impacts, understand the importance of sediment in pollutant transport and its relationship to water quality, assess the ecological integrity of freshwater aquaculture systems, understand the social implications, and determine what needs to be regulated to conserve and rehabilitate water bodies.
activities.key_activity: 1.7.3. Continued work on the assessments, case studies and associated education and capacity building on snow glaciers and water resources; sediment monitoring; magnitud e and risks linked to land subsidence from global to local level; coastal aquifers, considering the conservation of ecosystem services and multiple risks, including pollution and saltwater intrusion, with specific emphasis on small island developing states.
activities.outcomes: Increased knowledge of participants on theoretical and practical concepts for sediment management.

activities.title: Science-based Governance meeting for implementation of Output 5.2
activities.priority_area_full: Priority Area 5: Water Governance based on Science Mitigation, Adaptation and Resilience
activities.output_full: 5.2. Integration of sound science in water governance instruments improved reflecting adaptation to climate change and IWRM, integrating surface and groundwater fo r their uptake by decision makers.
activities.description: Meeting to compare practice on ensuring that governance of basins is properly informed by locally-relevant science. Participants from the UNESCO Water Family contributed their experience of linking governance and science.
activities.key_activity: 5.2.1. Publication and dissemination of case studies on science-informed water governance for management of surface and groundwater, in IWRM context and for climate change adaptation, also linking with experimental research basins and the UNESCO Water Family.
activities.outcomes: Production of key issues that affect the relationship between science and governance in c.15 basins across scales, based on experience globally. Details of how these issues have been addressed and how successfully. Impact through comparison of experience, to be crystallised in a publication in 2025.
activities.institution: Centre for Water Law, Policy and Science
activities.partners: No
activities.notes: The meeting brought together more than 30 people (15 presentations overall) to discuss practice in linking governance with science. Examples were presented from every continent except Antarctica. The role of stakeholders in this process was discussed in depth. The key themes and findings will be distributed to participants for discussion and development of a publication that will outline best practice. This will detail the issues and factors that influence the effective relationship between science and governance, and how these can be addressed in practice.
activities.cross_cutting_wg: ["Groundwater and Human Settlements","Ecohydrology and Water Quality","Hydrological Systems, Rivers, Climate Risk and Water-Food-Energy Nexus"]
