activities.title: the Workshop on Water Dynamics Under Climate Change: Gender-Responsive And Innovative Measures For Risk Reduction
activities.priority_area_full: Priority Area 4: Integrated Water Resources Management under conditions of Global Change
activities.output_full: 4.4. Development and sharing of knowledge on using the source to sea and nexus approaches by the scientific c ommunity supported, and capacities strengthened to improve integrated water resources management for all watersheds, including transboundary ones
activities.description:
the Workshop on Water Dynamics Under Climate Change: Gender-Responsive And Innovative Measures For Risk Reduction was organized on 18 October 2024 in Hanoi, Viet Nam by IMHEN  in collaboration with the Vietnam Association of Science Women, as part of the 2024 action plan. The event aimed to promote the integration of gender in the creative research of the IHP program and share new solutions for water management and climate change adaptation.

Key topics discussed included flood management and water safety, such as identifying large floods and proposing solutions to enhance flood prevention effectiveness, as well as water resource management and gender, with a focus on the role of women in smart water usage and ensuring gender equality. The workshop emphasized the crucial participation of women in developing more sustainable solutions, helping communities respond effectively to water-related risks. Integrating gender into research and activities will help create comprehensive solutions, enhancing community resilience in water resource management and climate change adaptation.
activities.key_activity: 4.4.2. Promotion of source-to-sea and nexus approaches in water quality, quantity, ecosystems and biodiversity and resilience interlinkages; development of science-based guidance.
activities.outcomes:
The workshop on "Water Dynamics in the Context of Climate Change, Creative Solutions, and Gender Integration for Risk Reduction" held on October 18, 2024, achieved several key outputs and outcomes. It provided a platform for scientific exchange on water dynamics, emphasizing the integration of gender issues in water management and climate adaptation. Key presentations included identifying large floods, smart water usage, and assessing flood risks in urban areas such as Hanoi. Additionally, the role of women in water resource management was highlighted, focusing on gender equality.

The discussions contributed to raising awareness on the need for inclusive, sustainable solutions in water resource management, promoting gender-sensitive policies, and enhancing decision-making processes. Furthermore, creative solutions were proposed for improving flood prevention and mitigation, such as enhancing operational systems for large-scale flood events. The workshop successfully fostered collaboration between experts and stakeholders, ensuring that gender considerations are embedded in climate change and water management strategies.

activities.institution: WENDI, Water Resources Research Center, Kyoto University
activities.partners: Kyoto University
activities.notes:
The 34th IHP Training Course (IHP TC) on integrated basin management under changing climate was organized in 2024 at Disaster Prevention Research Institute (DPRI), Kyoto University. This training course is organized by Kyoto University in cooperation with the UNESCO Jakarta Office under the objectives of IHP-9, and is also part of the educational activities of the Kyoto University UNESCO Chair WENDI. The TC aims to present various aspects of water resources and water-related disasters under climate change for participants from Asia-Pacific regions as a part of Japanese contribution to the UNESCO IHP-IX. The TC consists of a series of lectures, exercises including self-paced practicing of various software and a field visit for the target river basin. 

The online training course is oriented to the study of integrated basin management: hydrological extreme analysis, hydrological measurements, assessing the impacts of climate change, rainfall-runoff-inundation modelling, reservoir sustainability, optimum operation and management, as well as knowledge of the interrelationship with river ecosystem and environment. Development of resilient society has become an inevitable issue under the recent climate change that is increasing the frequency of extreme phenomena such as unprecedented floods and severe droughts. In order to make our society more resilient for such unprecedented extremes, social adaptation and countermeasure are required based on technologies for prediction and vulnerability assessments to meet the requirements of future water availability under changing climate.

The TCs gave an opportunity for participants: 1) to acquire the latest knowledge on climate change impacts on water resources, water and weather-related disasters, hydrological measurements of large river basins and ecosystem services, 2) to make a practice on rainfall-runoff-inundation analysis at river basin scale, and 3) to discuss effective strategies of integrated basin management based on scientific knowledge to realize a resilient society under climate change.


The IHP-TC was held from November 18 to 28, 2024. The event took place online, 42 participants from 20 countries were selected from a number of applicants. During the course, the chosen participants attended lectures on hydrology and water resources. They also engaged in practical exercises related to hydrological modeling and climate change data analysis. The program concluded with successful completion, including final presentations by the participants. This training played a crucial role in equipping them with the necessary skills and knowledge for managing water resources in the context of climate change.

activities.title: Publication: Agro-Physiological and Morphological Responses of Pearl Millet to Varying Water Regimes in Semi-Arid Conditions of Namibia
activities.priority_area_full: Priority Area 1: Scientific Research and Innovation
activities.output_full: 1.1. International scientific cooperation strengthened and fostered to address unsolved problems in hydrology, improving scientific understanding of hydrological cycles across river basins and aquifers.
activities.description:
Abstract
Pearl millet (Pennisetum glaucum (L.) R. BR.) is a C4 plant adapted to semi-arid climates and is one of the primary staple foods in Sub-Saharan Africa, including in Namibia. The decline in yields associated with water scarcity over the years has been a national concern in the country. An experimental field trial was conducted at the Mannheim Crop Research Station, Namibia, during the 2023 and 2024 cropping seasons to investigate the response of two local pearl millet cultivars (Kangara and Okashana 2) to different water regimes (100%, 75%, and 50% crop evapotranspiration [ETc]) according to morpho-physiological and yield parameters. Pearl millet was planted in a split-plot factorial design with four rows per plot under the three water regimes, and the genotypes were planted in subplots. The results revealed that the water regime had a significant effect on plant height, number of leaves, tillers, chlorophyll content, stomatal conductance, leaf temperature, stem thickness, number of productive tillers, panicle diameter, panicle length, dry panicle weight, biomass, grain weight, and 1000-seed weight of the two pearl millet cultivars (p < 0.001). At 50% ETc, the water regime significantly reduced the growth and yield parameters compared with the 75% ETc and 100% ETc water regimes, highlighting the significance of water in plant development and growth. The findings highlighted that both cultivars responded similarly to water stress. Seventy-five percent of ETc is recommended to be applied in pearl millet systems in semi-arid conditions. This research has significant implications for the planning and producing of pearl millet under water-limited environments under changing climatic conditions.

activities.title: Sustainability of Flood Plains Supported Livelihoods in the Face of Climate Change in East Africa (Kenya and Rwanda)
activities.priority_area_full: Priority Area 5: Water Governance based on Science Mitigation, Adaptation and Resilience
activities.output_full: 5.5. Capacities of the scientific community and decision makers strengthened on new frameworks and tools, to underpin water governance and build resilience.
activities.description:
The proposal outlines a collaborative research project aimed at enhancing climate resilience and
sustainable livelihoods in floodplain regions of East Africa. It represents a cooperation between
institutions in Rwanda, Kenya, and Austria, focusing on climate-smart agriculture, water resource

management, and the integration of gender and diversity perspectives. The proposal is well-
crafted, providing a comprehensive understanding of the issues at hand and offering scientifically

sound strategies to address them.
The project's design and scientific quality are sound, with clear objectives, good methodologies,
and a well-structured work plan. It integrates climate-smart agriculture with water resource
management, aiming for significant, sustainable improvements in agricultural productivity and
resilience to climate change. The partnership and collaboration strategy outlined in the proposal
are robust, ensuring a multidisciplinary approach and strong institutional support, essential for the
project's success.
The project shows a strong commitment to gender and diversity through its inclusion of women
and diverse groups at various levels, from project management to implementation. The use of the
Abbreviated Women’s Empowerment in Agriculture Index (A-WEAI) to measure empowerment
and gender parity is a notable strength. Further details on how the project plans to address and
monitor gender disparities in participation and benefits throughout its lifecycle could strengthen
the project.
The proposal also demonstrates a thoughtful approach to risk management and budget allocation,
emphasizing cost-effectiveness and strategic resource utilization. However, it could benefit from a
more detailed quantitative risk assessment and a more comprehensive justification of the budget
items to enhance efficiency.
activities.key_activity: 5.5.4. Development and implementation of projects to strengthen efficiency, effectiveness, and stakeholder confidence and engagement, around frameworks and objectives such as IWRM, nexus, source-to-sea, resilience to shocks, disasters, and climate change.
activities.outcomes:
The proposal outlines a set of expected results that are highly relevant to the project's objectives,
including the establishment of research partnerships and networks, and the creation of a
documentary and policy briefs focused on climate-smart agriculture and water resources
management. The proposal could be strengthened by specifying the publication channels and
dissemination efforts, such as specifications of target audience reach or expected outcomes from
stakeholder engagement activities.
The project lays a good foundation for sustainability through its focus on building partnerships,
enhancing local capacity, and developing actionable policy recommendations. While the proposal
mentions developing policy briefs, a more detailed strategy for engaging with policymakers and
influencing policy could further enhance the project's sustainability.

activities.title: WEI + as an Indicator of Water Scarcity and Ecological Demand Issue
activities.priority_area_full: Priority Area 1: Scientific Research and Innovation
activities.output_full: 1.5. Undertaking and sharing assessments on the interaction between humans and water, in line with socio hydrology by the scientific community supported to develop adaptive pathways, scenarios and strategies for water management
activities.description:
Different types of droughts, with a great number of indices which try to explain/categories
them, exist in literature. Certain regions do not necessarily have the same drought pattern
changes for different types of droughts. The socio-economic drought index WEI + of one
country/region or catchment area is defined as a quotient of water abstraction and water
sources availability (after deducting ecological demand), both with calculated returns.
Water demand (or water use/abstraction) can be expressed as the total water demand (usually)
or water demand for a certain purpose (water supply, irrigation, or industry). Both
water demand and water availability can be examined at different time levels: mean annual,
maximum (minimum) monthly, max (min) daily, etc. The reasons why these indices differ
over time and across one region are different. Four larger and twenty smaller catchment
areas in central Serbia were analyzed, the results of which are presented. River flows
on hydrological stations (monthly basis data) have been used as water source availability.
Available data for the 60-year period (1957–2016) has been included in the analyses. They
have been split into two 30-year periods and differences between them have been considered.
The adopted time levels are: 1) mean annual, and 2) 97%monthly flow which corresponds
with maximum monthly demand. It has been shown that annual WEI + is still low,
while 97%monthly is often higher than 0.5. An excessively high WEI + points to potential
Environmental hazards, so Ecological demand must be considered. Due to climate change,
and the increase in water demand, Ecological demand issues have become very debatable
in dry areas worldwide. After presenting the methodology and results, the paper discusses
all these issues.
activities.key_activity: 1.5.3. Conducting and supporting scientific research to assess the interaction between humans, environment and water, in line with socio-hydrology within an urban rural setting and develop adaptive pathways, scenarios and strategies for water management.
activities.outcomes:
The question is how Qefq should be adopted for the goal of achieving a (good) compromise
between ecological and human demand. Another question whether it should be
uniform, or whether it should adopt different rules depending on different river conditions
(mean annual flow, quotient of mean flow and certain adopted low flow levels, existence of
upstream reservoirs and other possible factors). This paper does not pretend to implicitly
propose such rules, but it claims that the number of months during which Qef
is higher than Qimon will increase in the watersheds that were analyzed here, to the point that in
many small and medium sized rivers, no water will be available for human demand during
several dry months or, in the event that ecological flow is not respected, some riverbeds
will become empty during periods of drought. The New Serbian Law/Rule regarding Qef
presents an additional challenge. Compared with Serbia, many sub-arid regions around the
world could expect water scarcity conditions that are much more severe.

Demand Issue, Water Resources Management, Published online 24 July 2024, Springer

activities.title: National Water and Women Camp (KAWK) 2025
activities.priority_area_full: Priority Area 2: Water Education in the Fourth Industrial Revolution including Sustainability
activities.output_full: 2.1. Public s awareness at all levels raised towards better understanding their contribution to the import ant multi functions of water in domestic life, ecosystems and productive development
activities.description:
The first camp was conducted on January 19, 2025, in Kota Samarahan, Sarawak, in collaboration with Universiti Malaysia Sarawak (UNIMAS). A total of 35 participants, including homemakers and students, attended the program. The sessions focused on the importance of water conservation at home and the production of soap using used cooking oil.
The second series was held on February 14, 2025, at Upcycle Park, Seberang Perai, Penang, with the support of Universiti Sains Malaysia (USM). This session saw a significant turnout of 104 participants from Puspanita MBSP and their children. Four modules were conducted, covering water conservation at home, the use of mud balls for water purification, water filtration techniques, and the H2O exercise.
The final series took place on February 21, 2025, at Tasik UniSHAMS, Kedah, in partnership with Universiti Islam Antarabangsa Sultan Abdul Halim Mu'adzam Shah (UniSHAMS), Universiti Utara Malaysia (UUM), and Universiti Sains Malaysia. This session gathered 35 women, comprising students, lecturers, and their children. The modules introduced included water filtration methods, bioindicators, compost fertilizers, and the H2O exercise.
activities.key_activity: 2.1.3. Mainstreaming water’s importance in broader awareness raising events (such as sustainable development, environment, climate change, desertification, cities, responses to public health issues, pandemics etc., at global, regional and national levels.
activities.outcomes:
Output: The program successfully raised awareness among participants, which included students, homemakers, educators, and government personnel, about sustainable water management practices. A total of three camps were conducted in Sarawak, Penang, and Kedah, drawing 174 participants. Educational modules covering topics such as water filtration, soap production from used cooking oil, mud ball usage, and bioindicators were effectively delivered. The program also resulted in the creation of learning materials and practical guides on sustainable water management. Collaboration between institutions like UNIMAS, USM, UniSHAMS, UUM, NGOs, and government agencies was strengthened, providing a valuable platform for networking and knowledge sharing among women from diverse backgrounds.

Outcome: This initiative empowered women to become active agents of change in water management and environmental sustainability within their communities. It enhanced their leadership roles in decision-making processes related to water resources, both at community and institutional levels. The knowledge gained from the camps led to improved sustainable water practices among families, communities, and organizations. Furthermore, the program significantly contributed to achieving SDG 5: Gender Equality and Women’s Empowerment. It fostered the formation of a motivated and knowledgeable community of women committed to environmental sustainability. Additionally, it strengthened partnerships among educational institutions, government agencies, and NGOs, driving collaborative efforts towards sustainable water management.

activities.title: Young Leaders Camp
activities.priority_area_full: Priority Area 2: Water Education in the Fourth Industrial Revolution including Sustainability
activities.output_full: 2.1. Public s awareness at all levels raised towards better understanding their contribution to the import ant multi functions of water in domestic life, ecosystems and productive development
activities.description:
The Young Leaders Camp (Borneo Zone) 2024 was held from May 22 to May 24, 2024, at Hidden Paradise Resort, Papar, Sabah. This camp was jointly organized by UNESCO-International Hydrological Programme (UNESCO-IHP) Malaysia, the Department of Irrigation and Drainage, and Universiti Malaysia Sabah. The program involved 62 participants consisting of students from public universities (IPTA) and secondary schools.

The theme of this camp was “Water for Peace.” The activities were designed to benefit the participants, with various agencies involved in educating them about the role of water resource management, aligned with the main objectives of UNESCO-IHP Malaysia's partner agencies.

The program was conducted through basic presentations on the roles of each agency, supervised by instructors and facilitators. It also included an integrated water resource management module featuring lectures and fieldwork related to hydrology, water, rivers, and their importance in human and environmental life. This year's program comprised 11 modules, contributed by 11 partner agencies from across Malaysia. Participants’ understanding of the program was evaluated through interactive methods (such as quizzes) recorded in logbooks and group presentations assessed by a special jury panel.
activities.key_activity: 2.1.3. Mainstreaming water’s importance in broader awareness raising events (such as sustainable development, environment, climate change, desertification, cities, responses to public health issues, pandemics etc., at global, regional and national levels.
activities.outcomes:
Output
This program achieved several significant outcomes. A total of 11 training modules were successfully implemented, providing participants with intensive training in integrated water resource management. Various engaging activities such as lectures, fieldwork, interactive quizzes, and group presentations were conducted to ensure a deep understanding among the participants. Additionally, participants recorded their learning in logbooks, serving as comprehensive documentation of the program.

The program's success was further strengthened by the collaboration of 11 strategic partner agencies, which contributed modules as well as instructors and facilitators. The camp concluded with a closing ceremony featuring creative presentations and sketches based on the modules learned, showcasing the participants’ enhanced understanding and creativity regarding the topics discussed throughout the program. As a result of this program, participants were introduced to responsibilities in water management, fostering an early awareness of the importance of preserving water resources for human life and the environment.     

Outcome                                                       
The program generated meaningful long-term outcomes, leaving a lasting impact on its participants and the community. It successfully fostered increased awareness among the younger generation about the importance of sustainable water resource management for the future. The participants emerged as agents of change within their families, peers, and local communities, actively sharing and applying the knowledge they gained. The program also contributed to advancing the goals of Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) 6, ensuring the availability and sustainable management of water and sanitation for all.

Additionally, the camp nurtured young leaders with broad knowledge, visionary outlooks, and creative problem-solving skills, equipping them to tackle water-related challenges dynamically. Follow-up sessions conducted three months after the camp assessed the program's long-term impact on the participants' lives and their communities. The feedback gathered emphasized the program's effectiveness and the participants’ ability to apply their learnings to address real-world issues. With strategic improvements in planning and execution, such as addressing location and weather challenges, this program can continue to deliver impactful outcomes for all involved parties and the environment

activities.title: Advancing Water Reuse Technologies and Practices
activities.priority_area_full: Priority Area 4: Integrated Water Resources Management under conditions of Global Change
activities.output_full: 4.3. Conducting and sharing of research on non conventional Water Resources (NCWRs) such as wastewater reuse, desalination, rainwater harvesting, and the Management of Aquifer Recharge (MAR) by the scientific community, in support of improving Water Cycle Management (WCM), strengthening capacities of local, regional, and national decision makers, and enhanced acceptance of public.
activities.description: The UNESCO Chair on Water Reuse at the University of Tehran advanced water security by promoting research, education, and policies on water reuse, especially wastewater recycling for urban, agricultural, and industrial use. In 2024-25, it held workshops, seminars, and international collaborations focusing on sustainable water management, circular economy in water reuse, AI integration, and ecohydrology. The Chair actively engaged in global forums, policy dialogues, and capacity building to enhance water reuse technologies and governance, including industrial wastewater treatment and glacier protection initiatives. It also contributed to national and international knowledge exchange and legislative efforts for water transparency and sustainability.
activities.key_activity: 4.3.1. Research projects, including collaborative actions (private sector, NGOs, civil society) and compilation of the state of the art in NCRWs and circular economies to improve WCM and to enhance efficiency and effectiveness of public and private investments, also in urban and peri-urban settlements, and also in alignment with MAWAC (Megacities, Water & Climate).
activities.outcomes: The implemented activity resulted in enhanced water reuse policies and frameworks for urban, agricultural, and industrial sectors, including a closed-loop water system for industries and greywater reuse strategies for cities. It fostered national and international collaboration, capacity building through workshops and seminars, and contributed to global water security dialogues. The activity also advanced ecohydrology site registration, integrated AI in water management, and raised awareness on water transparency and sustainability, strengthening Iran’s role in UNESCO water programs.
activities.institution: UNESCO Chair on Water Reuse, University of Tehran
activities.partners: Iranian National Commission for UNESCO
activities.stakeholder_group_type: Research and Academic Institutions (universities and research institutions studying water issues, scientists and researchers specializing in hydrology and water management.)
activities.notes:
Key Highlights
International Engagement: Active participation in UNESCO forums, including contributions to the International Hydrological Programme (IHP) and collaborations with global partners on initiatives related to water scarcity and climate change.

National Impact: Engagement with government bodies to promote policies for water reuse in urban, agricultural, and industrial sectors, advocating for a circular economy approach and water transparency.

Educational Initiatives: Organization of workshops and seminars on topics such as membrane autopsy, wastewater reuse, and water productivity improvement, targeting experts and students.

Research and Innovation: Contributions to scientific literature with publications on water reuse technologies, including the integration of AI in water management.

Ecohydrology Focus: Spearheading the registration of Iran's first ecohydrology site in collaboration with UNESCO, emphasizing nature-based solutions for water management.

Glacier Preservation: Launching initiatives to protect the Koohrang Glacier, a vital freshwater source, as part of UNESCO’s World Water Day program

National Workshops and Seminars
Hosted workshops on membrane autopsy to enhance sustainable water production.

Organized workshops on wastewater reuse based on a circular economy approach.

Conducted webinars on monitoring and managing water consumption in the industrial sector.

Policy and Advocacy

Advocated for policies promoting water reuse and transparency in industrial water management.

Engaged with government bodies to implement closed-loop water systems in industries.

The UNESCO Chair on Water Reuse at the University of Tehran has demonstrated a strong commitment to advancing water security through multifaceted activities. This report underscores the Chair's pivotal role in fostering sustainable water management practices and contributing to global dialogues on water-related challenges. The Chair's proactive engagement with UNESCO, national stakeholders, and international partners positions it as a key player in shaping the future of water resource management.

The activity also advanced ecohydrology site registration, integrated AI in water management, and raised awareness on water transparency and sustainability, strengthening Iran’s role in UNESCO water programs.

activities.partners: Iranian National Commission for UNESCO
activities.stakeholder_group_type: Research and Academic Institutions (universities and research institutions studying water issues, scientists and researchers specializing in hydrology and water management.)
activities.notes:
International Engagement: Active participation in UNESCO forums, including contributions to the International Hydrological Programme (IHP) and collaborations with global partners on initiatives related to water scarcity and climate change.

National Impact: Engagement with government bodies to promote policies for water reuse in urban, agricultural, and industrial sectors, advocating for a circular economy approach and water transparency.

Educational Initiatives: Organization of workshops and seminars on topics such as membrane autopsy, wastewater reuse, and water productivity improvement, targeting experts and students.

Research and Innovation: Contributions to scientific literature with publications on water reuse technologies, including the integration of AI in water management.

Ecohydrology Focus: Spearheading the registration of Iran's first ecohydrology site in collaboration with UNESCO, emphasizing nature-based solutions for water management.

Glacier Preservation: Launching initiatives to protect the Koohrang Glacier, a vital freshwater source, as part of UNESCO’s World Water Day program

National Workshops and Seminars
Hosted workshops on membrane autopsy to enhance sustainable water production.

Organized workshops on wastewater reuse based on a circular economy approach.

Conducted webinars on monitoring and managing water consumption in the industrial sector.

Policy and Advocacy

Advocated for policies promoting water reuse and transparency in industrial water management.

Engaged with government bodies to implement closed-loop water systems in industries.

The UNESCO Chair on Water Reuse at the University of Tehran has demonstrated a strong commitment to advancing water security through multifaceted activities. This report underscores the Chair's pivotal role in fostering sustainable water management practices and contributing to global dialogues on water-related challenges. The Chair's proactive engagement with UNESCO, national stakeholders, and international partners positions it as a key player in shaping the future of water resource management.

activities.priority_area_full: Priority Area 2: Water Education in the Fourth Industrial Revolution including Sustainability

activities.description: The online Open Learning course on Flood Hazard and Exposure Mapping, developed in collaboration with Antea Group Belgium, equipped participants with the knowledge and practical skills to map flood hazards and exposure using openLISEM and GIS software packages.  The content includes fundamental concepts of flood hazards, hydrology, and the impact of climate change on flooding. Participants learn to use GIS techniques, explore various data sources for flood modeling, and delve into flood modeling techniques, including hydrodynamic modeling.
activities.key_activity: 2.4.4. Integration/synthesis of e-learning on water topics (e.g. in UNESCO Open Learning, Open Water Network and others).
activities.outcomes: Online training course on Flood Hazard and Exposure Mapping available in the Open Learning platform. 406 active participants from 93 different countries. The course highlighted the value of open education in addressing global hydro-climatic risks. By promoting open-source tools and integrating them with real data from vulnerable regions, the course supports countries in building technical resilience to climate-related disasters, while reflecting our commitment to open science and equitable access to knowledge. Given the success of this run, the course is now continuously available on the Open Learning platform in a self-paced format as part of our Open Hydrology strategy and the new IHP Water Information Network System (IHP-WINS), aiming to expand open access to training opportunities to a wide audience.

activities.title: Workshop APPLICATION OF NEW TECHNOLOGIES FOR FLOOD FORECASTING AND DATA SCIENCE
activities.priority_area_full: Priority Area 1: Scientific Research and Innovation
activities.output_full: 1.9. Development and sharing of new technologies using earth observation, Artificial Intelligence and Internet of Things by the scientific community and service providers are communicated to and/or used for capacity strengthening of water stakeholders to increase their use in hydrological planning and assessment as well as monitoring and distribution networks.
activities.description:
The year 2025 marks the 50th anniversary of the Intergovernmental Hydrological Programme (IHP) and 60 years of UNESCO’s commitment to water sciences. To mark this significant jubilee, WSDAC organized a workshop aimed at exchanging knowledge and experiences and exploring cutting-edge technological applications in water management, including innovations within the water–energy–ecology nexus.The workshop focused on the application of innovative solutions for flood risk reduction, including the development of Flood Early Warning Systems (FEWS), as well as the synergistic application of AI and IoT in the fields of water management and energy. The workshop address the following topics, all related with flood protection:
1. Development of early warning systems for flood protection (FEWS)
2. Application of Artificial Intelligence in FEWS data acquisition and management
3. Artificial Intelligence (AI) methods and the Internet of Things (IoT) for FEWS
4. Enhancing infrastructure resilience through AI
activities.key_activity: 1.9.1. Facilitation of the development, and promotion, of tools and methodologies based on earth observations, Artificial Intelligence (AI) Machine Learning (ML) and Internet of Things (IoT) for water resources assessment and monitoring and promote use of software applications such as rainwater harvesting, observation and as well as flood and drought monitoring.
activities.outcomes: The main outcomes of the workshop included the exchange of experiences in applying AI and IoT in hydrological practice; presentation of innovative FEWS solutions implemented in the Public Water Management Company Srbijavode; sharing of experiences and best practices in the use of Open Data; identification of potential directions for further development and application of AI and IoT in the fields of water management and energy; training of students from technical faculties and young engineers in the application of innovative technologies; and the expansion of scientific cooperation between institutions.
activities.institution: WSDAC - Center for Water for Sustainable Development and Adaptation to Climate Change
activities.partners: Jaroslav Cerni Water Institute (co-organizator)
activities.knowledge_product_type_other: Presentations of best practices (7 PowerPoint presentations) summarizing project results, lessons learned, or recommendations for stakeholders, scientific community and young researchers.

activities.notes:
In addition to national research and scientific institutions, a student from Brazil, who was on an international internship, attended the workshop. For this reason, both Serbia and Brazil were included in the field for countries. All ppt presentations and photoes from events are available at the WSDAC web page https://wsdac.jcerni.rs/application-of-new-technologies-for-flood-forecasting-and-data-science/

activities.title: Urban water security in a changing climate: Water management in human settlements in the Balkans and global megacities
activities.priority_area_full: Priority Area 5: Water Governance based on Science Mitigation, Adaptation and Resilience
activities.output_full: 5.4. Conducting and sharing of research on novel approaches of adaptive water management by the scientific community supported and capacities of Member States strengthened to enhance sound water govern ance.
activities.description: Organized as part of the celebrations of IHP 50th anniversary, the event will share findings from initiatives and projects implemented by UNESCO IHP and partners. In particular, key findings of the UNESCO Project “Strengthening capacities for water management in human settlements in Balkan countries”. Designed as part of the UNESCO objective to support human settlements to achieve water security, the project supports three South-eastern Europe countries—Albania, Bosnia and Herzegovina, and Montenegro—in achieving SDG 6 targets. Implemented in collaboration with UNESCO cat 2 centres CIMWRM (Greece) and IRTCUD (Serbia), the project's 1st phase gathered valuable information on capacity gaps and needs in water management and infrastructure in urban and rural human settlements in the three Balkan countries. The project's 2nd phase focuses on capacity building through a comprehensive training programme, based on findings of the capacity gaps and needs assessment. Lessons learnt from the project offer insights on challenges related to urban water management and may serve as a showcase for countries with similar problems in other parts of the world.
activities.key_activity: 5.4.1. Supporting and facilitating the research on novel approaches to adaptive water management, including adaptive urban water management; dissemination of the research results; training and refresher programs for related public officials, water managers, professionals and water operators.
activities.outcomes: The event will offer actionable insights and practical recommendations for achieving urban water security and supporting cities in developing and implementing strategies for climate adaptation and resilience. Through the findings of UNESCO IHP projects and initiatives on urban water, the event highlights the need to identify and address country-specific policy and knowledge gaps for the development of education and training programmes for water professionals, researchers, educators and policy makers. activities.title: Workshop APPLICATION OF NEW TECHNOLOGIES FOR FLOOD FORECASTING AND DATA SCIENCE
activities.priority_area_full: Priority Area 1: Scientific Research and Innovation
activities.output_full: 1.9. Development and sharing of new technologies using earth observation, Artificial Intelligence and Internet of Things by the scientific community and service providers are communicated to and/or used for capacity strengthening of water stakeholders to increase their use in hydrological planning and assessment as well as monitoring and distribution networks.
activities.description:
The year 2025 marks 50th anniversary of the Intergovernmental Hydrological Programme (IHP) and 60 years of UNESCOs commitment to water science. To mark this significant jubilee WSDAC organized a workshop aimed at exchanging knowledge and experiences and exploring cutting-edge technical application in water management, including inovations within the water-energy-ecology nexus. The workshop  focused on the application of innovative solutions for flood risk reduction, including the development of Flood Early Warning Systems (FEWS), as well as the synergistic application of AI and IoT in the fields of water management and energy. The workshop address the following topics, all related with flood protection:
1.	Development of early warning systems for flood protection (FEWS)
2.	Application of Artificial Intelligence in FEWS data acquisition and management 
3.	Artificial Intelligence (AI) methods and the Internet of Things (IoT) for FEWS
4.	Enhancing infrastructure resilience through AI
activities.key_activity: 1.9.1. Facilitation of the development, and promotion, of tools and methodologies based on earth observations, Artificial Intelligence (AI) Machine Learning (ML) and Internet of Things (IoT) for water resources assessment and monitoring and promote use of software applications such as rainwater harvesting, observation and as well as flood and drought monitoring.
activities.outcomes: The main outcomes of the workshop included the exchange of experiences in applying AI and IoT in hydrological practice; presentation of inovative FEWS solutions implemented In the Public Water Management Company Srbijavode; sharing of expirience and best practicies in the use of Open Data; identification of potential directions for futher developmenet and application of AI and IoT in the fields of water management and energy; training of students from technical faculties and young engineers in the application of innovative technologies and the expansion of scientific cooperation between institutions.
activities.institution: WSDAC - Center for Water for Sustainable Development and Adaptation to Climate Change
activities.partners: Jaroslav Černi Water Institute
activities.knowledge_product_type_other: Presentations of best practicies ( 7 PowerPoint presentations summarizing project results, lessons learned and recommendations for stakeholders etc.
activities.stakeholder_group_type: Research and Academic Institutions (universities and research institutions studying water issues, scientists and researchers specializing in hydrology and water management.)
activities.notes: In addition to national research and scientific institutions, a student from Brazil, who was on an international intership attended the workshop. For this reason, both Serbia and Brazil were included in the field for countries. All ppt presentations and photoes from event are available at the WSDAC web page https://wsdac.jcerni.rs/application-of-new-technologies-for-flood-forecasting-and-data-science/. The workshop is reported also on offical linkedin profiles of the Jaroslav Cerni Water Institute https://www.linkedin.com/posts/jaroslav-cerni-water-institute_fews-sustainablewatermanagement-climatechangeadaptation-activity-7364333050370973698-3x3i?utm_source=share&utm_medium=member_desktop&rcm=ACoAADV-9YsBUsLxNr8cn-F5DM_CxUlqkZOnjAM, and Voden Kragujevac https://www.linkedin.com/posts/vodena-rs_ai-floodprevention-watermanagement-activity-7361652807596158977-vh6Q?utm_source=share&utm_medium=member_desktop&rcm=ACoAADV-9YsBUsLxNr8cn-F5DM_CxUlqkZOnjAM
activities.cross_cutting_wg: ["Hydrological Systems, Rivers, Climate Risk and Water-Food-Energy Nexus"]

activities.title: DeepTech & Innovation Online School Sustainable Product Design in a Digital Age Monday, 3rd to Friday, 7th November 2025
activities.priority_area_full: Priority Area 1: Scientific Research and Innovation
activities.output_full: 1.9. Development and sharing of new technologies using earth observation, Artificial Intelligence and Internet of Things by the scientific community and service providers are communicated to and/or used for capacity strengthening of water stakeholders to increase their use in hydrological planning and assessment as well as monitoring and distribution networks.
activities.description:
Our Centre had the honour of delivering the lecture “The Role of WSDAC, a UNESCO Category 2 Centre, in Promoting New Technologies in the Water Sector.” Dr. Brankica Majkić-Dursun emphasized that climate change profoundly affects water resources management by altering precipitation regimes, increasing the frequency of floods and droughts, and reducing the predictability of water availability. These challenges demand adaptive, data-driven approaches for monitoring, forecasting, and decision-making.  She highlighted that Artificial Intelligence (AI) can play a transformative role by enhancing hydrological modelling, optimizing reservoir operations, improving early warning systems, and supporting integrated water resources management through real-time data analysis and predictive analytics.  The presentation focused on IHP-IX Priority Area 1 – Scientific Research and Innovation, as well as the activities of the WSDAC Centre and the Jaroslav Černi Water Institute in contributing to the Sustainable Development Goals through the integration of new technologies (AI, ML, IoT, Digital Twin) in the water sector.
The online school provided an excellent opportunity for participants from different sectors to share experiences and strengthen collaboration between science and industry.
activities.key_activity: 1.9.1. Facilitation of the development, and promotion, of tools and methodologies based on earth observations, Artificial Intelligence (AI) Machine Learning (ML) and Internet of Things (IoT) for water resources assessment and monitoring and promote use of software applications such as rainwater harvesting, observation and as well as flood and drought monitoring.
activities.outcomes: The online school provided an excellent opportunity for participants from different sectors to share experiences and strengthen collaboration between science and industry. During the five-day programme, more than 900 registered participants from multiple countries followed the lectures and exchanged ideas on DeepTech, artificial intelligence, and sustainability.
activities.partners: Vodena Serbia, University of Tourus France, University of Ioannina Greece, Modragon Unibersitatea Spain, University of East Sarajevo  Bosnia and Herzegovina, University of Bergamo Italy, Gebze Technical University Turkey, John von Neumann University Hungary

activities.title: Participation in the Panel II : How to Best Utilize Hydropower Potential Under Current Climate Change Conditions
activities.priority_area_full: Priority Area 4: Integrated Water Resources Management under conditions of Global Change
activities.output_full: 4.2. Research on upstream downstream river uses for hydropower, navigation, fishery, leisure activities, water supply, drought risk management and flood ri sk management conducted and shared by the scientific community and UNESCO Water Family to minimize socio economic and ecological consequences.
activities.description:
A panel discussion on “How to Best Utilize Hydropower Potential Under Current Climate Change Conditions” was held at the Chamber of Commerce and Industry of Serbia, within the International Expert Conference “Hydropower Plants – An Important Link in the Energy Transition.”
The conference gathered representatives of key institutions from the energy sector and governmental bodies from Serbia and the region — including the Ministry of Mining and Energy of the Republic of Serbia and the Republic of Srpska, Electric Power Industry of Serbia (EPS), Electric Power Industry of Montenegro (EPCG), Power Plants of North Macedonia (ESM), as well as representatives of Energoprojekt and the Republic Hydrometeorological Service of Serbia.
Panel participant Miodrag Milovanović, Advisor at the Jaroslav Černi Water Institute and a member of the WSDAC Centre team, emphasized the need for developing reservoir storage that would enable redistribution of water from the wetter to the drier periods of the year. His presentation focused on the necessity of strategic and integrated water resources management under pronounced climate change conditions, with particular attention to the role of reservoirs as a key instrument for reallocating water from periods of surplus to periods of deficit.
activities.key_activity: 4.2.1. Identification, sharing, publishing and building capacity on good inclusive practices in upstream-downstream river uses for hydropower, irrigation, navigation, fishery, leisure activities, water supply and water related risk management.
activities.outcomes: The modernization and revitalization of existing reservoirs, along with clearly defined management models for future infrastructure, were highlighted as crucial steps toward building a more resilient and efficient water system. The multifunctional role of hydropower reservoirs — in flood protection, inflow regulation, and water management — confirms their strategic importance in the energy transition and in addressing climate challenges.

activities.title: Scientific Paper:  Impact of Different Factors on Changes in Water Resources Availability
activities.priority_area_full: Priority Area 1: Scientific Research and Innovation
activities.output_full: 1.3. Research on uncertainty in climatic scenarios, hydrological projections and water use scenarios conducted and recommendations communicated to decision makers and the general public to elaborate adaptive water management strategies
activities.description: Authors Dejan Dimkić, Boris Pokorni, Zoran Simić published scientific paper Impact of Different Factors on Changes in Water Resources Availability in the Journal Water Resources Management, under the support of WSDAC Center
activities.key_activity: 1.3.2. Research and preparation of state-of-the-art publications on uncertainty in climatic scenarios, hydrological projections and water use scenarios and intersectoral consultations among research teams (including publication and dissemination of Water Outlook).
activities.outcomes: When considering trends in hydrological changes (HC) for one region, two questions arise: (1) Are they simply variations of one parameter (coincidence), or have they been initiated with certain causes; and (2) If they are not random, how do various significant environmental changes impact these trends, and how do they vary across the region. The most important environmental changes which could impact HC are changes in Temperature (T), Precipitation (P), Forest Cover (FC) and Human Use of water (HU). This paper sheds light on these questions for central Serbia (CS) based on a series (analyzed period 1949–2023) for 24 hydrological stations in CS, and 26 T stations and 38 P stations across the whole of Serbia. Estimation of FC changes and changes in HU are based on the available data for three larger regions, which cover the whole of central Serbia (western, central and eastern part). The results indicate that temperature is generally the most significant factor for the observed decrease in HC in central and especially eastern CS (impact slightly greater than 50%), while in the western part of CS, P and T the impacts on HC are about the same (both slightly lower than 50%). Other environmental changes (ΔFC and ΔHU) generally exhibit a lower impact. The methodology offered for evaluating the impact of different factors on HC could also be applied to the other parts of the world where decreasing HC is observed. After presenting the methodology and results, the paper discusses the confidence of the results and cites some results from different Mediterranean and other countries/regions.

activities.title: Conference paper: Advanced Hydrogeological Modelling Tools for Metro - Groundwater Interaction Studies
activities.priority_area_full: Priority Area 1: Scientific Research and Innovation
activities.output_full: 1.7. Development and sharing of knowledge base on the impacts of global change and human usage on river and lake basins, aquifer systems, coastal areas, and cryosphere and human settlements by the scientific community supported so as to embed it in water resources and services management plans.
activities.description: Authors Vladimir Lukić, Vesna Tripković and Milenko Pušić published in Conference proceedings of Southeastern Europe Tunnelling Conference (SETC-2025) titled Advanced Hydrogeological Modelling Tools for Metro - Groundwater Interaction Studies under support of WSDAC
activities.key_activity: 1.7.1. Scientific studies, thematic workshops, and science-based support to policy makers and managers on “Water in the Anthropocene” (e.g. Water Management in Coastal Areas; Water and Land Management in Low Lying River Deltas; Aqui fer Systems; Water management in Urban Environments; Management of Hydrosphere-Cryosphere-Climate Change Nexus).
activities.outcomes: This paper presents experiences in the development and application of software systems designed for the preparation, analysis, and interpretation of hydrogeological data; execution of a large number of parallel numerical simulations, including simulation of the tunnel lining within the schematized layers of the mathematical model; automatic generation of results and reports; and data archiving. The importance of these tools is emphasized in the analysis of complex hydrogeological systems, particularly in the context of hydrodynamic modelling of spatially heterogeneous aquifers and the simulation of various exploitation or contamination scenarios.The application of modern software platforms in the field of hydrodynamic groundwater flow analysis represents an indispensable tool for achieving sustainable management of this valuable resource, as well as for further advancement of professional practice and scientific research in this domain.

activities.title: Connecting knowledge for water security: The launch of the new IHP-WINS
activities.priority_area_full: Priority Area 3: Bridging the data knowledge gap
activities.output_full: 3.3. Comparing and validating open access data on water quantity, quality and use and their sharing by the scientific community supported for sustainable water management.
activities.description: The IHP-WINS Launch Webinar officially introduced UNESCO’s IHP Water Information Network System as a global digital platform to bridge the water data-knowledge gap under IHP-IX. The event combined live demonstrations of the platform’s core components with practical use cases presented by members of the UNESCO Water Family, including the UNESCO Regional Office for Eastern Africa, the IHP-ROK National Committee, the Vrije Universiteit Brussel UNESCO Chair on Open Water Science and Education, and the Category 2 Centre ICWRGC. These examples illustrated how IHP-WINS supports regional coordination, national reporting, open science, and data-driven water management.
activities.key_activity: 3.3.1. Enhancement of the capabilities and user friendliness of IHP-WINS, including the extension of IHP-WINS with new members, new data and new contributions from members.
activities.outcomes: The webinar successfully launched IHP-WINS to a global audience and showcased real-world implementation pathways through diverse institutional use cases. It strengthened awareness, technical understanding, and ownership among Field Offices, National Committees, UNESCO Chairs, and Category 2 Centres. The activity fostered collaboration within the Water Family, encouraged data contributions and platform adoption, and reinforced IHP-WINS as a key digital infrastructure supporting open science, SDG monitoring, and evidence-based water governance under IHP-IX.
activities.partners: Regional Office for Eastern Africa, IHP-ROK, VUB, ICWRGC
activities.notes: The recording, presentation and Webinar recording can be found here: https://ihp-wins.unesco.org/dataset/ihp-wins-platform-launch-materials-28-april-2025

activities.title: IHP-WINS Launch during side-event on Open Hydrology
activities.priority_area_full: Priority Area 3: Bridging the data knowledge gap
activities.output_full: 3.3. Comparing and validating open access data on water quantity, quality and use and their sharing by the scientific community supported for sustainable water management.
activities.description: The IHP-WINS live launch was held as a hybrid event during the 50th Anniversary celebration of the Intergovernmental Hydrological Programme (IHP), within the pre-event on Open Hydrology at UNESCO Headquarters. The event officially introduced IHP-WINS as UNESCO’s global open science infrastructure for hydrology and water data integration. Through high-level presentations and institutional use cases (Regional Office for Eastern Africa – GaFa MIS, IHP-ROK National Committee, ICWRGC/GEMS Water, and the UNESCO Chair on Open Water Science and Education), the launch demonstrated real-time data sharing, interoperability standards (OGC, ISO, INSPIRE), citizen science integration, and open hydrological data workflows supporting research, operational hydrology, and evidence-based governance.
activities.key_activity: 3.3.1. Enhancement of the capabilities and user friendliness of IHP-WINS, including the extension of IHP-WINS with new members, new data and new contributions from members.
activities.outcomes:
Official global launch of IHP-WINS as UNESCO’s digital water data infrastructure.

Demonstration of interoperability pathways linking research data, operational hydrology (e.g., WHOS), and open science standards.

Showcased real-time hydrometeorological data integration (IHP-ROK), transboundary groundwater cooperation (GaFa Horn of Africa), global water quality metadata harmonization (ICWRGC/GEMS Water), and citizen science & low-cost sensing applications (VUB UNESCO Chair).

Strengthened collaboration across Member States, Category 2 Centres, UNESCO Chairs, and Regional Offices.

Established momentum for the IHP-WINS Task Force and broader institutional adoption.

Reinforced UNESCO’s role as a bridge between research hydrology, operational monitoring systems, and global data governance.

activities.title: UNESCO International Symposium on Coastal Aquifers, Sustainable Futures
activities.priority_area_full: Priority Area 1: Scientific Research and Innovation
activities.output_full: 1.1. International scientific cooperation strengthened and fostered to address unsolved problems in hydrology, improving scientific understanding of hydrological cycles across river basins and aquifers.
activities.description:
On 10 and 11 February 2026, UNESCO hosted the International Symposium on Coastal Aquifers, Sustainable Futures, which brought together experts and decision-makers to advance the sustainable management of coastal aquifers.  
The symposium builds on 5 years of work under the UNEP/GEF MedProgramme, where UNESCO leads the component on Management of Coastal Aquifers and Related Ecosystems of Child Project 2.1. as executing partner.
activities.key_activity: 1.1.1. Coordination of UNESCO scientific efforts on Unsolved Problems in Hydrology, including hydrogeology/geo hydrology, in partnership with IAHS, IAH and other water related scientific associations, including o rganization of the capitalisation of knowledge, res ults and experience available in the UNESCO Water Family, incl. the Flagships, into published syntheses.
activities.outcomes:
More than 110 participants gathered to discuss opportunities and challenges of sustainable management of coastal aquifers, achievements from the project and the way forward.  

Experts presented case studies from across the Mediterranean. From the Rhiss-Nekkor aquifer in Morocco to Ras Jebel in Tunisia, from Libya’s Jifarrah Plain to Lebanon’s Damour aquifer, and the Buna–Bojana coastal aquifer shared between Albania and Montenegro, each site tells a different story. Governance contexts and local pressures vary, but all highlight the fragile balance between land and sea. 

Discussions focused on the interactions between freshwater and marine systems, including vulnerability assessments, seawater intrusion, submarine groundwater discharge, and groundwater-dependent ecosystems. Participants also explored integrated and inclusive approaches to coastal aquifer management, such as coastal aquifer management plans,  decision-support tools, and stakeholder engagement.  

Cooperation emerged as a central theme. Some coastal aquifers cross national borders. Others span institutional boundaries, linking water, agriculture, environment, and urban planning authorities that do not always work together. Overall, the discussions held were a demonstration of the effectiveness of the Conjunctive Surface and Groundwater Management approach, with practical examples from UNESCO’s work under the MedProgramme.

activities.title: UNESCO Chair in Water Sciences, University of Birmingham, UK
activities.priority_area_full: Priority Area 1: Scientific Research and Innovation
activities.output_full: 1.2. Ecohydrology research and innovation at UNESCO designated sites conducted and shared by the scientific community and UNESCO Water Family, communicated to assess the impact of ecohydrological and nature based solutions on water cycles and include such solutions in Integrated Water Resource Management ( and services at all scales and in Sites management.
activities.description: Understanding how global change affects water in the environment is crucial to provide reliable information on water resources and hazards, and to develop sustainable water policies and adaptation strategies. The UNESCO Chair in Water Science aims to develop a transformative approach to tackle ‘wicked water problems’ - multifaceted, interconnected problems that are very difficult to solve due to lack of data and changing human needs. The Chair delivers new insights into water cycle processes, assessing impacts on ecosystems and communities, leveraging novel sensor technologies, and engaging citizen scientists. The Chair was established in 2016 and is led by Professor David M. Hannah.
activities.key_activity: 1.2.6. Scientific support, capacity building, and promotion for coordinated implementation of ecohydrology principles including e cohydrological multidimensional enhancement of catchment sustainability potential WBSR+CE UNSC SEEA ecosystem valuation, IUCN NBS Global Standard, FAO/TNC and World Bank guidelines.
activities.outcomes: With chair oversight, the University of Birmingham (UoB) has produced more than 50 interdisciplinary, high-impact, peer-reviewed publications on ecohydrology in collaboration with partner institutions across the Global North and South. Research has addressed diverse themes including: (i) freshwater ecological responses to hydrological dynamics; (ii) early warning systems to enhance flood resilience; (iii) socio-hydrological dynamics linking human and water systems; and (iv) freshwater microplastic pollution. Complementing these outputs, UoB has secured more than £10M in ecohydrology-focused research funding. Since 2018, UoB has also hosted the UK’s largest UN World Water Day events, including major online and hybrid gatherings in 2024 and 2025 themed “Leveraging Water for Peace” and “Glacier Preservation.” In 2025, UoB successfully led an application within UNESCO’s International Hydrological Programme to recognise the regional Upper Tame basin as an Ecohydrological Demonstration Site, titled the “Birmingham Urban Ecohydrological Observatory.” At postgraduate and postdoctoral levels, since 2021 UoB has hosted the internationally recognised annual Catchment Science Summer School. In 2024, Prof. Hannah was listed among the inaugural Highly Ranked Scholars by ScholarGPS and was invited by the President of the American Geophysical Union to serve as a member of the Robert E. Horton Medal Committee. In 2025, Prof. David Hannah received recognition as a long-standing contributor to the International Hydrological Programme during the 50th anniversary of IHP and 60 years of UNESCO’s leadership in water sciences. Additional service roles include participation in the World Meteorological Organization Hydrological Coordination Panel and International Glossary of Hydrology, advisory involvement with the UNESCO Ecohydrology Youth Network, and contributions to the UNESCO toolbox on partnerships in water resources research and policy.

activities.description: UNESCO developed and integrated a Water-Related Post-Disaster Viewer within the IHP-WINS platform to support hydrological disaster assessment and recovery planning under IHP-IX. The tool provides a standardized, reusable digital workflow for compiling and visualizing water-related impacts of disasters (flooding, droughts, landslides, infrastructure damage, water quality, hydrological change, ...) and recovery outputs from following projects. Embedded in IHP-WINS, the Rapid Response page enables Member States and UNESCO partners to rapidly assemble post-disaster information through interactive story maps, geospatial datasets, timelines, and impact assessments, strengthening science-based emergency response and recovery processes. A demonstrative use case showcased the platform’s capacity to integrate diverse datasets and present coherent narratives for decision-makers, supporting UNESCO’s Open Hydrology and disaster risk reduction agenda.

Development of a reusable template architecture allowing rapid activation of future disaster pages, including event overview, hydrological impact assessment, interactive story maps and response/recovery activities.
Integration of multi-source datasets (flood extent, water levels, infrastructure damage, and water quality indicators) into a unified digital assessment environment.
Strengthened IHP-WINS functionality as an operational decision-support tool, linking open hydrological data with disaster preparedness, response, and recovery planning.
Enhanced capacity for Member States, Regional Offices, and the UNESCO Water Family to conduct post-disaster water assessments, promote evidence-based recovery strategies, and support climate resilience and disaster risk reduction under IHP-IX.

activities.priority_area_full: Priority Area 3: Bridging the data knowledge gap
activities.output_full: 3.3. Comparing and validating open access data on water quantity, quality and use and their sharing by the scientific community supported for sustainable water management.
activities.description: UNESCO developed and integrated a Data Stories feature within the IHP-WINS platform to transform complex water datasets into accessible, article-style narrative knowledge products supporting IHP-IX implementation. The tool enables researchers and practitioners to combine structured storytelling with interactive geospatial visualizations, linking scientific datasets directly to interpretive content. Data Stories follow a publication workflow similar to scientific articles, including contributor attribution, structured sections, persistent identifiers (DOIs), and correctly formatted citations and references. Each story is explicitly linked to underlying datasets, which are themselves assigned DOIs, ensuring traceability, reproducibility, and compliance with Open Science principles. Embedded in IHP-WINS, Data Stories provide a standardized mechanism for Member States and the UNESCO Water Family to publish evidence-based water narratives that bridge data, research, education, and policy-relevant communication.

Establishment of structured publication workflows (draft, review, approval, publication) ensuring quality-controlled storytelling across the Water Family.
Integration of interactive Terria-based maps within stories, allowing users to explore spatial data alongside scientific interpretation.
Introduction of dataset linking, contributor attribution (including ORCID), versioning, and analytics, strengthening transparency and reproducibility of published content.
Confirmed alignment with UNESCO Open Science principles through improved DOI handling and citation export, facilitating reuse and attribution of data and stories.

During the First Regional IHP Meeting for the Maghreb (Tunis, September 2025), a strategic presentation of the IHP Water Information Network System (IHP-WINS) was delivered to national focal points, IHP National Committees, UNESCO Chairs, Category 2 Centres, and water experts from Algeria, Libya, Mauritania, Morocco, and Tunisia. The session provided a comprehensive overview of IHP-WINS as a core digital infrastructure supporting the implementation of the IHP-IX Strategic Plan in the region.

The presentation demonstrated how IHP-WINS operationalizes Priority Area 3 (Bridging the Data-Knowledge Gap) through its data catalogue, DOI-enabled datasets, geospatial viewer (Terria), data stories, rapid response tools, and Water Family Hub. Particular emphasis was placed on how Member States in the Maghreb region can use the platform to publish national datasets, strengthen interoperability, enhance visibility of research outputs, support ecohydrology site documentation, and facilitate science-based water governance aligned with SDG 6, the Sendai Framework, and climate adaptation priorities.

The session evolved into an interactive regional dialogue, exploring pathways for establishing or strengthening IHP National Committees, connecting regional datasets to IHP-WINS, fostering cross-border cooperation, and supporting the development of a Maghreb regional IHP roadmap.

activities.description: UNESCO integrated NASA Surface Water and Ocean Topography (SWOT) satellite products into the IHP-WINS platform to support near real-time monitoring of river dynamics in Ukraine, with a focus on the Dnipro River basin. The activity transformed raw SWOT satellite observations into actionable hydrological information by establishing an automated data pipeline for acquisition, processing, cataloguing, and visualization within IHP-WINS. SWOT products were operationalized and linked directly to the geospatial viewer, enabling interactive exploration of water surface elevation and discharge through time. Embedded in IHP-WINS, this implementation demonstrates how Earth observation data can be translated into decision-ready insights for water management, climate impact assessment, and disaster risk reduction, directly supporting IHP-IX priorities on data-knowledge integration and science-based governance.
activities.key_activity: 3.3.1. Enhancement of the capabilities and user friendliness of IHP-WINS, including the extension of IHP-WINS with new members, new data and new contributions from members.

Operational integration of NASA SWOT Level-2 river products for Ukraine into IHP-WINS, enabling satellite-based monitoring of water levels and discharge along the Dnipro River.
Establishment of an automated workflow for regular data acquisition, processing, metadata enrichment, and upload, ensuring continuous updates without manual intervention.
Deployment SWOT Products capturing point-based and segment-averaged river characteristics, providing complementary hydrological perspectives.
Configuration of tailored TerriaJS visualizations, including time-enabled layers, color-scaled water surface elevation maps, and animated temporal playback, transforming satellite measurements into intuitive, decision-support visuals.
Integration of these datasets into the IHP-WINS geospatial viewer, allowing users to combine SWOT-derived information with other hydrometeorological and contextual layers.
Strengthened capacity for Ukrainian stakeholders and UNESCO partners to assess river dynamics remotely, supporting climate resilience, flood and drought analysis, and evidence-based recovery planning.

activities.title: IHP-WINS Water Quality Feature through a Raster-Based Time-Series Processing Pipeline
activities.priority_area_full: Priority Area 3: Bridging the data knowledge gap
activities.output_full: 3.3. Comparing and validating open access data on water quantity, quality and use and their sharing by the scientific community supported for sustainable water management.
activities.description:
IHP developed and integrated an innovative Water Quality feature within the IHP-WINS platform by establishing a state-of-the-art data processing pipeline based on xcube, enabling on-the-fly extraction of time series from satellite raster products. This activity transforms large Earth observation datasets into actionable point-based water quality information directly accessible through the IHP-WINS geospatial viewer.

The pipeline allows users to click anywhere on a water body and instantly generate time series for key water quality indicators such as turbidity, chlorophyll-a, suspended particulate matter, and related variables. By serving harmonized datasets through scalable cloud infrastructure and exposing them via TerriaJS, the system bridges advanced remote sensing analytics with user-friendly visualization for decision-makers.

Implemented initially through pilot case studies (Ukraine Copernicus Lake Water Quality products and satellite-based monitoring of Lake Andraikiba in Madagascar), the feature establishes the technical foundation for a dedicated Water Quality Portal within IHP-WINS. Beyond water quality, this architecture is designed to be reusable across other thematic domains (e.g. drought, floods, groundwater, ecosystems), providing a modular framework for future expansion under IHP-IX.
activities.key_activity: 3.3.1. Enhancement of the capabilities and user friendliness of IHP-WINS, including the extension of IHP-WINS with new members, new data and new contributions from members.
activities.outcomes:
Development of a scalable xcube-based processing pipeline enabling interactive time-series extraction from raster water quality datasets directly within IHP-WINS .
Successful integration of Copernicus Lake Water Quality products into the IHP-WINS geospatial viewer, including server-side styling and thematic visualization.
Deployment of a working pilot Water Quality Viewer supporting point-based analysis, temporal playback, and basic statistical aggregation of satellite-derived indicators.
Demonstration of acceptable performance and technical viability for regional deployments, validating the architecture for operational use.
Implementation of a Ukraine pilot and Lake Andraikiba (Madagascar) case study showcasing satellite-based monitoring of turbidity, chlorophyll-a, and suspended matter in data-scarce contexts .
Creation of the technical foundation for a future IHP-WINS Water Quality Portal, supporting expansion to additional regions and thematic applications.
Strengthened capacity for Member States and UNESCO partners to access near-real-time water quality insights for climate resilience, ecosystem protection, and evidence-based water governance.
Demonstrated how advanced Earth observation analytics can be operationalized through IHP-WINS into practical decision-support tools aligned with Open Science and IHP-IX priorities.

activities.title: National Water Quality Monitoring Program (Pakistan)
activities.priority_area_full: Priority Area 4: Integrated Water Resources Management under conditions of Global Change
activities.output_full: 4.5. activities.description: Pakistan Council of Research in Water Resources (PCRWR) continues to conduct research and national-level water quality monitoring. Under its National Water Quality Monitoring Program (2025–2026), PCRWR conducted a comprehensive assessment of drinking water quality in 70 major cities across Pakistan. The findings based on 2205 water sources indicated that 59% of the tested drinking water sources were found unsafe for human consumption due to microbiological contamination. Trend analysis since 2015 shows gradual improvement possibly due to installation of filtration plants and improved awareness; however, the overall proportion of safe drinking-water sources has consistently remained below 50%.
activities.key_activity: 4.5.2. Knowledge generation and research on global change impacts on water quality (e.g. linking to relevant projects).
activities.outcomes:
Key Outputs: Assessed 2,205 water sources in 70 cities (2025–26); 59% unsafe due to microbiological contamination. Trend since 2015 shows gradual improvement, yet safe sources remain below 50%.

Indicator: % of safe drinking-water sources nationwide.

activities.title: Global Water Security Issues Series Publication
activities.priority_area_full: Priority Area 4: Integrated Water Resources Management under conditions of Global Change
activities.output_full: 4.2. Research on upstream downstream river uses for hydropower, navigation, fishery, leisure activities, water supply, drought risk management and flood ri sk management conducted and shared by the scientific community and UNESCO Water Family to minimize socio economic and ecological consequences.
activities.description: The Global Water Security Issues (GWSI) Series is an official UNESCO publication co-published under the framework of the UNESCO Intergovernmental Hydrological Programme (IHP), in cooperation with the International Water Resources Association (IWRA). The series aims to contribute to the achievement of the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) by sharing international best practices and policy- and technology-related experiences in the field of water security. GWSI is a regular publication series with a target of ten thematic issues. Each issue is developed through consultation with UNESCO to reflect globally relevant and timely water security agendas and is structured around field-based case studies from different countries. Through this approach, the series provides an integrated perspective linking water management with environmental, social, and institutional dimensions, while promoting international cooperation and knowledge sharing in the water sector. GWSI has addressed major water security themes, including water reuse (2020), groundwater management (2021), urban water management (2023–2024), and climate change (2024). In 2025, the series focuses on biodiversity (Issue 6) and water and gender (Issue 7). Issue 6 is aligned with SDG 6.6 (protection and restoration of water-related ecosystems) and aims to highlight interactions between water management and ecosystem change, while exploring sustainable water management responses to ecosystem degradation and climate change. Issue 7 is aligned with SDGs 5.4 and 5.5 and seeks to address gender-related disparities and vulnerabilities in water access, use, and management processes, particularly in developing countries, while fostering more inclusive water governance discussions.
activities.key_activity: 4.2.1. Identification, sharing, publishing and building capacity on good inclusive practices in upstream-downstream river uses for hydropower, irrigation, navigation, fishery, leisure activities, water supply and water related risk management.
activities.outcomes: In 2025, i-WSSM promoted the dissemination of GWSI as a thematic platform for advancing global water security agendas through a total of three outreach activities, including one domestic and two international events. At the national level, i-WSSM co-organized a thematic session with the UNESCO IHP National Committee of the Republic of Korea at the Korea Water Resources Association Annual Conference held in Yeosu in May 2025. The session introduced the background and objectives of the GWSI Series and discussed its contributions to the SDGs with domestic academic and professional communities. At the international level, i-WSSM participated in the UNESCO IHP 50th Anniversary and 60th Anniversary of Water Sciences event held in Paris in June 2025, where it presented data-driven urban water management cases and shared research and practical experiences related to global water management agendas. Subsequently, at the 19th World Water Congress (WWC) held in Marrakech, Morocco, in December 2025, i-WSSM co-organized special sessions with UNESCO IHP and IWRA to introduce the objectives and publication directions of GWSI Issue 6 (Water and Biodiversity) and Issue 7 (Water and Gender), thereby expanding related discussions at the international level. In particular, Issue 7 was presented in connection with the theme of WWDR 2026, “Water for People,” to encourage broader attention to water and gender issues.Through these outreach activities, i-WSSM effectively delivered the key messages of the GWSI Series to a wide range of stakeholders, including academia, international organizations, and policy and practice communities. These efforts contributed to raising awareness of global water security agendas and strengthening international cooperation platforms related to water, biodiversity, and gender.
activities.institution: International Centre for Water Security and Sustainable Management(i-WSSM) under the auspices of UNESCO
