activities.title: Dissemination of the World Water Development Report 2025: Mountains and Glaciers – Water Towers
activities.priority_area_full: Priority Area 1: Scientific Research and Innovation
activities.output_full: 1.7. Development and sharing of knowledge base on the impacts of global change and human usage on river and lake basins, aquifer systems, coastal areas, and cryosphere and human settlements by the scientific community supported so as to embed it in water resources and services management plans.
activities.description: This project aims to disseminate the key messages of the World Water Development Report (WWDR), UN-Water’s annual report published on World Water Day (22 March), and to enhance understanding of global water security issues within Korea. In February 2017, UNESCO’s World Water Assessment Programme (WWAP) requested i-WSSM to prepare a Korean-language executive summary of the WWDR. Subsequently, with UNESCO’s approval,  i-WSSM has continued publishing the Korean executive summary and audiobook in Korean in addition to the six official UN languages, which is a rare case for a non-official UN language. In particular, as the United Nations designated 2025 as the International Year of Glaciers’ Preservation, established 21 March as World Glaciers Day, and set the official theme of WWDR 2025 as “Mountains and Glaciers: Water Towers,” i-WSSM published the Korean executive summary and audiobook of WWDR 2025 to raise awareness of the importance of mountain and cryospheric water resources for water security.
activities.key_activity: 1.7.1. Scientific studies, thematic workshops, and science-based support to policy makers and managers on “Water in the Anthropocene” (e.g. Water Management in Coastal Areas; Water and Land Management in Low Lying River Deltas; Aqui fer Systems; Water management in Urban Environments; Management of Hydrosphere-Cryosphere-Climate Change Nexus).
activities.outcomes: Following publication, i-WSSM actively promoted and disseminated the Korean executive summary and audiobook of WWDR 2025 through major domestic academic events. In particular, i-WSSM organized a thematic session at the Korea Water Resources Association Annual Conference, held in Yeosu on 23 May 2025, to share the key messages of the report. The session featured expert presentations and panel discussions on the downstream ecological impacts of soil erosion and human activities, the use of satellite and geophysical observations to understand changes in mountain water resources and management directions, and the implications of winter snow dynamics for water circulation and disaster risks such as wildfires.. In addition, promotional booths were operated to distribute the publications, enabling the key messages of WWDR 2025 to reach a wide range of stakeholders, including policymakers, researchers, and practitioners.

activities.description: The Mekong River is a transboundary basin shared by multiple countries and plays an important role in regional stability and global water security. Since then, the Laos Office has functioned as a regional hub for capacity development in water resources and urban water management. In 2025, in response to the increasing risk of urban flooding caused by heavy rainfall in Laos, i-WSSM implemented a capacity development programme and field investigation focusing on stormwater management, with the aim of strengthening understanding of urban water management challenges and contributing to water security in the Mekong River Basin.
activities.key_activity: 2.5.3. Capacity building to bridge education policy gaps in water and sustainable development by equipping professionals and technicians with relevant tools and knowledge.

On-site Diagnosis with technical experts enabled a clearer understanding of urban flood vulnerabilities and water management infrastructure conditions in Vientiane, leading to the identification of short-, medium, and long-term improvement pathways. In addition, sharing the programme outcomes through a high-level meeting with the Vice Minister of MONRE enhanced the visibility of i-WSSM and the Laos Office at the governmental level, while confirming opportunities for sustained cooperation and high-level engagement in future activities.

activities.description: i-WSSM has accumulated expertise in nexus approaches through research on interactions among water, energy, food, and ecosystems (WEFE), and has applied these approaches to urban water cycle systems through phased research since 2020. This research has been guided by the nexus approach as a core analytical framework for understanding urban water management challenges as interconnected systems rather than isolated components. Building on these achievements, this project aimed to structure accumulated nexus research outputs and expert networks into educational content, strengthen i-WSSM’’s expertise in nexus-based urban water management, and apply these outcomes to its education and research activities. In addition, the project sought to enhance linkages with global water agendas and UNESCO’s International Hydrological Programme (IHP) flagship initiatives.
activities.key_activity: 4.4.3. Research on synergies and tradeoffs among the societal goals related to water management (e.g. water-environment-energy-food-health); and compilation and dissemination, including through conferences/symposia/workshops, of best nexus practices, including wastewater reuse and byproducts (nutrients, energy) in a circular economy context.
activities.outcomes: Through this project, i-WSSM gained external recognition for its research by applying the WEFE nexus approach. In particular, a presentation entitled “Assessment of Water Quality and Aquatic Ecosystem Impacts Based on a WEFE Nexus Approach” received a Best Paper Award at the Summer Conference of the Korean Society of Limnology in August, enhancing i- WSSM’S academic credibility and expertise in nexus-based water and environmental research. In addition, participation in various academic events, including Conference of the Korean Sociey fo Climate change, contributed to disseminating nexus-related issues and expanding exchanges with domestic and international experts and stakeholders. The urban water management training module developed by i-WSSM further enhanced its leadership and visibility in the field of urban water management content.

Tajikistan is transitioning from river-based management to basin-based integrated water management and shifting from manual data management to scientific, information-based system operations. This program was designed to provide theoretical knowledge and practical experience in IWRM concepts, policies, technologies, and operational best practices, enabling participants to apply these learnings to their national context.
activities.key_activity: 2.5.3. Capacity building to bridge education policy gaps in water and sustainable development by equipping professionals and technicians with relevant tools and knowledge.
activities.outcomes: The program successfully delivered practical, field-oriented case studies that can inform Tajikistan's integrated water management policy development. Participants gained technical knowledge in water resources allocation, dam operations, and flow meter calibration through hands-on training. The program fostered shared recognition of the need for river and basin-level integrated management approaches. Tajikistan currently manages water resources by river and agency, and participants explored the potential for introducing basin-centered collaborative frameworks, starting with pilot management in selected areas before scaling up. The program also identified policy-linked water resource education needs, including requests for training on water demand modeling in response to climate change and population growth, customized WIS operational training for practitioners, and capacity building in diplomatic skills for transboundary water management.

activities.description: The IHP Flagship Initiative HELP (Hydrology for the Environment, Life and Policy) was introduced as a collaborative framework for scientists, policy makers and lawyers to tackle water resource management issues at the basin-scale. By 2014 the HELP network totaled 91 basins spanning 67 countries before entering a period of comparative decline. The continued relevance of HELP to the UNESCO Water Family by ‘promoting development through good water governance’ was recognized during IHP-IX’s strategic review of Flagships. To this end a kick-off meeting of HELP 2.0 was organized at the 10th World Water Forum 2024 focusing on “Re-Invigorating the Hydrology for the Environment, Life and Policy (HELP) River Basin Network for Water Security”. The 2nd Meeting of HELP was organized during the 26th Session of the IHP Council “Renewing the IHP-HELP Flagship Initiative”. activities.key_activity: 3.2.1. activities.title: Water Education and Capacity Development to support SDG 6 achievement
activities.priority_area_full: Priority Area 2: Water Education in the Fourth Industrial Revolution including Sustainability
activities.output_full: 2.5. Capacities of skilled professionals and techn icians at water related tertiary and vocational education strengthened to identify the main gaps for sustainable water management towards providing appropriate tools to governments and societies to address those gaps and the Agenda 2030 targets.
activities.description: SDG 6 is alarmingly off-track, as highlighted in the recent SDG 6 status report published by UN-Water. This means that all efforts undertaken globally to improve the management of water resources and services are not producing the desired and needed results. It has been recognized at high political level specifically in the Global Acceleration Framework that Capacity Development is one of the main factors that will produce an “acceleration” in achieving SDG 6. Moreover, Water Education was identified as one of the key priority areas within the UNESCO IHP-IX strategy. These initiatives target in particular water sector institutions, strengthening their capacity to support real and substantial changes across scales, and will contribute to address both existing and emerging issues in a rapidly changing world requiring quick adaptation of capacities in institutions.
activities.key_activity: 2.5.4. Establishment of a UNESCO water family educational platform open to the Member States and partners to enhance learning opportunities and sharing of good practices and lessons learned, also valorizing Ecohydrology Demosites, MAB Biosphere Reserves and other UNESCO designated sites.
activities.outcomes:
1. Provided a better understanding of the role and the impact pathways generated by Education and Capacity Development to achieve SDG 6, and in particular will showcase the main large initiatives and “game changers” that are contributing to upscale capacity development efforts at a global scale, with a focus on developing countries. 
2. Provided inputs to the global capacity development within the UNESCO water family and Member States on the future of water education and capacity development to support the water sector especially in developing countries to develop capacities to accelerate implementation of water related SDG’s. 
3. Offered a modern perspective and scaled up efforts to deliver Capacity Development products and services to carry out institutional changes that will deliver ultimately impact to SDG 6 achievement. 
4. Raised awareness among the UNESCO water family and especially member states from especially countries that lag behind implementation of SDG 6 and water related targets, advocating the importance of education and capacity development as an essential enabler for SDG 6.

activities.title: Workshop on Citizen Science for Water Resilience with Youth in Ghana
activities.priority_area_full: Priority Area 1: Scientific Research and Innovation
activities.output_full: 1.10. Conducting and sharing of research on integrating citizen science in the hydrological discipline by the scient ific community and other stakeholders supported, to improve understanding of the water cycle enabling science based decision making
activities.description: Ghana faces increasing challenges from water-related disasters such as floods and droughts, exacerbated by climate change. Youth, as key agents of change, are often underrepresented in disaster risk reduction (DRR) and climate adaptation efforts. UNESCO, through the project “Strengthening resilience on water-related disaster under climate change for a sustainable society in Ghana”, funded by the Government of Japan, is working with national stakeholders in Ghana to enhance resilience against water-related hazards by leveraging digital technologies. As part of this initiative, a hands-on training workshop for youth on citizen science for river flow monitoring was organized in Accra, Ghana. The workshop engaged youth from local communities and trained them with practical skills in river flow monitoring, data collection, and analysis using the UNESCO Citizen Science Toolbox.
activities.key_activity: 1.10.1. Citizen science pilot studies in different regions for water resources monitoring and crowdsourced assessments by local stakeholders, including validation of data quality to ensure adequate accuracy.
activities.outcomes:
Youth trained in the use of the UNESCO Citizen Science toolbox integrated in IHP WINS
Capacity-building of youth and local communities in river flow monitoring for informed flood and drought management
Youth engagement in water-related DRR and climate adaptation through hands-on fieldwork
Establishment of a network of your facilitator to scale up citizen science river flow monitoring across Ghana
activities.partners: UNESCO Accra Office, Youth Bridge Foundation, Groundtruth

activities.title: AI Capacity Building for Water Resources Stakeholders
activities.priority_area_full: Priority Area 1: Scientific Research and Innovation
activities.output_full: 1.9. Development and sharing of new technologies using earth observation, Artificial Intelligence and Internet of Things by the scientific community and service providers are communicated to and/or used for capacity strengthening of water stakeholders to increase their use in hydrological planning and assessment as well as monitoring and distribution networks.
activities.description: In the era of data, the expansion of the digital water industry has highlighted the growing need for the application of artificial intelligence (AI) and machine-learning technologies. There is an increasing demand to refine scientific knowledge and methodologies for addressing water-related disasters, as well as to explore strategies for developing water resources planning technologies that utilize AI and the Internet of Things (IoT). Despite the recognized necessity of AI adoption, the level of understanding of AI-related knowledge among domestic and international stakeholders remains relatively low, according to the results of the second-year study. Accordingly, there is a clear need to develop and operate online AI educational content for entry-level professionals in the water resources field. To achieve the objective of the UNESCO-IHP Phase IX overarching theme (1)—“to enhance the knowledge base of Member States and stakeholders in water practice and research and to strengthen their capacity to manage related risks”—this research project aims to develop and provide online educational content to strengthen AI capacity among domestic and international stakeholders in the water resources sector.
activities.key_activity: 1.9.1. Facilitation of the development, and promotion, of tools and methodologies based on earth observations, Artificial Intelligence (AI) Machine Learning (ML) and Internet of Things (IoT) for water resources assessment and monitoring and promote use of software applications such as rainwater harvesting, observation and as well as flood and drought monitoring.
activities.outcomes:
In the present research project, the study is conducted based on the following four specific objectives:
▪Reconstruction of the AI–water resources education curriculum and governance framework based on the research outcomes from Years 1–3 of the UNESCO Phase-IV programme
▪Development of educational content structured around three themes: theoretical foundations, expert interviews, and hands-on practice and applications
▪Editing and expert review of AI education content in both Korean and English versions
▪Uploading the educational content to the IHP Korea National Committee and the IHP Open Learning platform, and collecting feedback

activities.title: Study on the Riparian Zone Management System for Improving Watershed Water Environment(Ⅰ)
activities.priority_area_full: Priority Area 1: Scientific Research and Innovation
activities.output_full: 1.8. Development and sharing of knowledge and innovative solutions on impr oving water quality and reducing water pollution by the scientific community supported and communicated to support science based decision making, improve knowledge, services and reduce health related risks.
activities.description: This study presents policy directions for redefining riparian zones beyond their traditional water quality–focused role, positioning them as integrated watershed management areas that encompass water quantity regulation, habitat functions, and carbon sequestration. To this end, it reviews domestic and international riparian management systems and comprehensively evaluates the multifunctional roles of riparian zones.
activities.key_activity: 1.8.1. Thematic assessments of water quality at the basin, city, national, regional and global scales to identify key water quality and pollution challenges.
activities.outcomes: This study confirms that riparian zones provide multifunctional benefits across water quality improvement, water quantity regulation, habitat support, and carbon sequestration. Domestic literature demonstrates that adequately vegetated riparian buffers significantly reduce nonpoint-source pollution, attenuate peak runoff, stabilize baseflow, and enhance aquatic and terrestrial habitats. In addition, riparian vegetation and wetlands contribute meaningfully to climate mitigation through carbon sequestration, accounting for a substantial share of national LULUCF absorption. These findings highlight riparian zones as essential nature-based infrastructure for integrated watershed management rather than narrowly defined regulatory spaces.

activities.title: Ecohydrology and Nature-Based Solutions for Water Management Workshop
activities.priority_area_full: Priority Area 1: Scientific Research and Innovation
activities.output_full: 1.2. Ecohydrology research and innovation at UNESCO designated sites conducted and shared by the scientific community and UNESCO Water Family, communicated to assess the impact of ecohydrological and nature based solutions on water cycles and include such solutions in Integrated Water Resource Management ( and services at all scales and in Sites management.
activities.description:
PERMATIL (Permaculture Timor-Leste), in collaboration with the UNESCO Regional Office in Jakarta, convened a two-day workshop titled “Ecohydrology and Nature-Based Solutions for Water Management” in Dili. Participants included national institutions responsible for water, environment, and forestry; the UNESCO National Commission; NGOs; international partners; and regional experts.
The workshop aimed to:
•	Build technical capacity in understanding and applying NBS for water and ecosystem management in the Timor-Leste context.
•	Highlight the importance of integrating local and indigenous knowledge, strongly championed by PERMATIL and local communities, as a complement to scientific methods for climate adaptation.
•	Initiate discussion toward establishing an Ecohydrology Demonstration Site in Timor-Leste, building on existing restoration initiatives.
•	Strengthen regional cooperation and stakeholder networks to support sustainable, nature-based water management.
activities.key_activity: 1.2.2. Expansion of UNES CO ecohydrology sites to demonstrate ecohydrology and nature based solutions as the sustainable way of water resources management, including in urban areas, in partnership with IAHS IAHR and ISEH
activities.outcomes: Gaps identified during the workshop: Recognition of Governance and Policy Gaps, Data and Technical Challenges, Lack of wastewater treatment, limited research. Strengths Identified: Strong cultural importance of springs and water governance traditions, Existing NBS initiatives already implemented by local actors, A broad and active network of engaged community members, Solutions rooted in deep local knowledge and cultural understanding.

activities.title: E-Flows implementation in Ramganga river at Hareoli Barrage
activities.priority_area_full: Priority Area 1: Scientific Research and Innovation
activities.output_full: 1.2. Ecohydrology research and innovation at UNESCO designated sites conducted and shared by the scientific community and UNESCO Water Family, communicated to assess the impact of ecohydrological and nature based solutions on water cycles and include such solutions in Integrated Water Resource Management ( and services at all scales and in Sites management.
activities.description: Ramganga E-Flows Assessment and Trade-offs Analysis was conducted during 2013-2018. From 2018 to 2021, policy engagement with the departmental and dam authorities continued and in March 2021 an Office Order was issued, notifying lean season E-Flows releases into the River from Hareoli Barrage by the authorities (UPI&WRD). Since 2022, WWF India team and UPI&WRD team are jointly monitoring the flows in the river to assess the E-Flows releases in the river. Besides this, the monitroring on 3 other aspects is being conducted, i.e. (i) improvement in river health (channel depth, width, longitudinal connectivity, flow velocity, general physico-chemical parameters, like DO etc.); (ii) improvement in hydraulic habitat conditions for the aquatic life in the river; (iii) fish surveys to understand the changes in fish diversity and catch-per-unit-effort to understand if improved habitat conditions are aiding bouncing back of diversity and presence of fishes in the impacted river stretch of Ramganga. This is done from October/November to May/June since 2022.
activities.key_activity: 1.2.1. Development and operationalization of a world leading network/hub for transdisciplinary ecohydrological research, education and dialogue on ecohydrology and nature-based solutions for enhancement of WBRS+CE catchment sustainability potential (biodiversity, resilience to anthropogenic climate change, ecosystem services and culture and education) and promotion of Ecohydrology Web Platform (http://ecohydrology ihp.org/demosites/).
activities.outcomes:
The team now plan to come out with a joint publication documenting the findings/resuts of the monitoring and impact assessment of maintaining E-Flows in the Ramganga during the most critical period in a year, i.e. the lean season. The is report is expected before end of 2026. 

The other key output from this work and other experiences is to come up with a guide-paper on restoring E-Flows in the rivers, while capturing real-life case studies from many of the UNESCO IHP Ecohydrology Demo Sites.

activities.title: Development of Forest-based Blue-Green Network Technologies to Enhance Urban Water Cycle Soundness
activities.priority_area_full: Priority Area 1: Scientific Research and Innovation
activities.output_full: 1.2. Ecohydrology research and innovation at UNESCO designated sites conducted and shared by the scientific community and UNESCO Water Family, communicated to assess the impact of ecohydrological and nature based solutions on water cycles and include such solutions in Integrated Water Resource Management ( and services at all scales and in Sites management.
activities.description:
1. Objectives
A. Advancement of long-term monitoring research on water resources in upstream forest watersheds and stabilization of water supply functions in response to climate change.
B. Evaluation of the hydrological functions and value of urban forests, and development of Nature-based Solutions (NbS) technology to enhance these functions.
C. Strategies to establish Blue-Green Networks for improving urban living environments and support for policy-making related to urban forests.

2. Key Findings
A. Development of Forest Management Technologies for Monitoring Forest Watershed Water Resources and Stabilizing Upstream Water Supply
   (1) Monitoring water cycle characteristics in forest watersheds and identifying influencing factors
   (2) Development of forest watershed management techniques for stabilizing upstream water supply
B. Analysis of Urban Forest Water Cycle Effects and Development of Technologies to Enhance Water Cycle Functions Using Nature-based Solutions (NbS)
   (1) Evaluation of the functions and value of urban forests for water-related disaster mitigation and water environment improvement
   (2) Development of technologies to enhance the water-related functions of urban forests by applying Nature-based Solutions
C. Evaluation of Blue-Green Network Connectivity and Research on Forest-based Water Management Policy Formulation
   (1) Assessment of the current status of Blue-Green Infrastructure and landscape connectivity characteristics
   (2) Research on forest-based water management policy strategies for restoring the soundness of the urban water cycle
activities.key_activity: 1.2.5. Investigation on how the catchment/river basin based ecohydrology concept/nature based solutions can be extrapolated to large scale applications (continental/global scale).
activities.outcomes:
A. Development of Forest Management Technologies for Monitoring Forest Watershed Water Resources and Stabilizing Upstream Water Supply
  - Expansion of monitoring in upstream forest watersheds: Establishment of 50 new forest streamflow gauge stations (70 sites in '24 → 120 sites in '25).
  - Construction of an IoT-based real-time automatic observation system for forest streamflow and development of a data visualization web server
  - Calculation of rating curves (flow equations) for each observation site and acquisition of a watershed-scale spatial information database.
  - Verification of water cycle improvement effects through thinning and establishment of new monitoring sites.
  - Analysis of forest restoration effects based on runoff changes in logged and reforested areas.
B. Analysis of Urban Forest Water Cycle Effects and Development of Technologies to Enhance Water Cycle Functions Using Nature-based Solutions (NbS)
  - Development of an AI-driven water cycle model considering urban forest elements: Deep learning-based GSFLOW.
  - Verification of a dynamic water cycle model for urban watersheds reflecting surface water and groundwater runoff characteristics, and quantification of water cycle effects by element.
  - Assessment of aquatic ecosystem health by section in upstream urban watersheds and identification of indicator species groups (benthic invertebrates).
  - Re-verification of the importance of permeable spaces (urban forests, green spaces, forests, fields, etc.) within urban watersheds using water cycle models.
  - Review of landslide characteristics and trends in urban versus non-urban areas, and the necessity of disaster management in urban forests.
  - Confirmation of water quality improvement and water temperature cooling effects driven by urban forests in upstream urban watersheds.
C. Evaluation of Blue-Green Network Connectivity and Research on Forest-based Water Management Policy Formulation
  - Field survey and typology classification of Blue, Green, and Grey infrastructure in intensive observation areas within upstream urban watersheds.
  - Assessment of habitat quality and network connectivity based on Blue-Green Infrastructure within urban watersheds.
  - Analysis of laws related to forest watersheds upstream of urban streams and comparison of complementary, overlapping, and gap relationships between relevant agencies.
  - Analysis of the operational status and characteristics of legal systems related to the protection of upstream forest watersheds of urban streams by government ministry.
  - Necessity of headwater source protection in the context of Integrated Water Resources Management (IWRM) and comparison of the legal status of relevant ministries.
  - Analysis of recent trends in urban forest creation by the Korea Forest Service and the necessity and current status of governance establishment.

activities.priority_area_full: Priority Area 1: Scientific Research and Innovation
activities.output_full: 1.6. Scientific knowledge, methodologies and tools in addressing water related disasters, such as flood and drought elaborated and/or enhanced towards timely forecasting.
activities.description: The project seeks to support the Kenyan government efforts in averting future disasters and dealing with the aftermath of the 2024 flood events that affected the country from April continuing till June 2024, using a comprehensive, context specific and people centered approach. The project will generate flood exposure maps and identify flood disaster hotspots, which will be used for policy development and settlements’ planning to avoid such losses in the future. A Flood Early Warning System for Tana River Basin will be developed to provide with alerts the communities and avert such devastating disasters in the future. E-learning material will be developed, and human capacities will be enhanced at technical level. All tools and products will be communicated to the public using consultations, related Apps and through community radios in K-Swahili and local languages. Furthermore, communication with NGOs working in the region will be pursued to extent the reach of the project.

activities.outcomes: The project has developed an early flood warning system, characterisation and mapping of aquifer recharge zones in the Tana River Basin, procurement of IoT sensors for hydroclimatic measurements (water level, soil moisture, rainfall) has been done and preparations for installations ongoing, a graphical user interface for flood information dissemination has been developed and training materials for early warning systems developed and available online.

The objective of this study is to develop and demonstrate verification technology for the integrated operation of underground dams and sand storage dams, enhancing water supply resilience under climate change?induced drought conditions.

The study confirms that the integrated management of underground dams and sand storage dams provides an effective governance-level solution for reducing drought risks in water-vulnerable regions, while AI-based inflow prediction enables proactive operational decision-making and integrated quantity–quality assessment supports the long-term sustainability and social acceptance of alternative water sources.

activities.title: Smart Web-based Data Platforms for Integrated Management of Water Quality and Flow Rate
activities.priority_area_full: Priority Area 3: Bridging the data knowledge gap
activities.output_full: 3.1. Development and use of scientific research methods by the scientific community supported to correctly collect, analyze interpret and exchange data.
activities.description:
This project aims to develop a smart web-based data platform for the integrated management of water quality and flow rates. The data platform is designed to efficiently manage data collected from sensor-equipped measuring devices. It is being developed as part of a 3D water quality and flow monitoring technology based on unmanned remote vehicles. To this end, high-resolution three-dimensional water quality and flow data are acquired through spatial scanning of rivers and lakes. The acquired data are then structured into datasets according to predefined protocols—such as vertical profiles or river cross-sections—and transmitted to the platform for intelligent water management.
The project involves establishing standards and protocols for water quality and flow data, developing an integrated data platform with big data analytics capabilities, and conducting field validation at river-based testbeds.
activities.key_activity: 3.1.1. Synthesis on measurements and data, including a synthesis paper; organization of the capitalization of knowledge, results and experience available in the UNESCO Water Family, including the Flagships.
activities.outcomes: Currently in the final year of a 5-year research period, the integrated data platform has been fully developed and is now operational. The system features the following key functions: (1) an interface and automated data transmission between remote monitoring equipment, application servers, and database servers; (2) integration with public data (e.g., water quality, water level, and meteorological networks) to provide reference benchmarks; (3) spatial interpolation and integrated analysis of water quality and flow rates; and (4) database management and visualization for enhanced data utilization.
activities.institution: Korea Institute of Civil Engineering and Building Technology

activities.title: Designate an area for priority management areas for sewerage improvement and conduct urban flood response projects
activities.priority_area_full: Priority Area 1: Scientific Research and Innovation
activities.output_full: 1.6. Scientific knowledge, methodologies and tools in addressing water related disasters, such as flood and drought elaborated and/or enhanced towards timely forecasting.
activities.description:
1. Objectives
Preventing flood by increasing storm-water discharging capabilities in urban areas where storm-water overflow is causing or threatening to cause flood damage

2. Key Findings
The Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment may designate an area where flood damage occurs, or is likely to occur, due to sewage inundation or an area which is likely to worsen the quality of public waters as an area for priority management areas for sewerage improvement (hereinafter referred to as "priority management area"), after consultation with the competent Mayor/Governor. After designating the priority control area, the head of municipalities will conduct a flood preventing activities like i) establishing sewer maintenance measures, and ii) increasing storm-water discharging capacities in accordance with the maintenance measures (such as enlarging the diameter of sewer pipelines, constructing new rainwater pumping stations for expanding discharging capacity, and installing rainfall storage facilities or large-depth rainwater tunnels.).
activities.key_activity: 1.6.1. Research and knowledge generation on the scientific advances in addressing and timely forecasting of water related disasters, such as (flash) floods, (flash) droughts and rainfall induced landslides; and on additional impact of synchronous and/or cascading water related hazards, in partnership with EGU, AGU, IAHS ISEH and ICL - International Consortium on Landslides and IPL - International Programme on Landslides including good practices and lessons learned.
activities.outcomes:
In 2013, 21 areas were designated as Priority Management Areas for Sewerage Improvement, and as of the end of December 2025, 227 areas have been designated. Of the 226 designated areas, construction for increasing storm-water discharging capacity has been completed in 57 areas, construction is ongoing in 45 areas, and design work is underway in 124 areas.
As of 2024, there have been no flooding among the 57 areas, where construction has been completed, within the design rainfall frequency since the expansion of stormwater drainage capacity.

activities.description:
To disseminate Korea’s hydrological survey technologies to the international community, to develop and provide customized, practice-oriented hydrological survey training programs to strengthen the institutional and technical capacities of developing countries, and to support the foundation for sustainable water management.

 - Five international training programs were successfully implemented in cooperation with major domestic educational institutions, including Inha University, the National Institute for Environmental Human Resources Development, the Korea Environmental Preservation Association, and the Human Resources Development Institute of the Korea Rural Community Corporation
 - A total of 61 participants from 14 countries, including Azerbaijan, Cambodia, Ghana, Laos, Nepal, and Viet Nam, took part in the programs, Their practical competencies were enhanced through hydrological survey theory, advanced hydrological survey technologies, VR-based safety training, and field-based practical exercises
 - A two-week internship program was operated for master’s degree trainees who are government officials from Ghana and Kenya, providing tailored, practice-oriented training that reflects the conditions of developing countries, including hydrological surveys, data analysis, and flood response
activities.key_activity: 2.5.3. Capacity building to bridge education policy gaps in water and sustainable development by equipping professionals and technicians with relevant tools and knowledge.
activities.outcomes:
1) Training on “Water Resources and Disaster Management – Advanced Hydrological Survey Technologies
  - content: Introduction to Korea’s water resources survey technologies, VR-based safety training, and field practice on hydrological surveys
  - Participants: 12 students from Azerbaijan
  - Date: 18 April 2025

2) 「35th International Environmental Technology Specialized Training Program」 for Capacity building of international Water Resources Professionals
  - Content: Introduction to Korea’s water resources survey technologies, VR-based safety training, and field practice on hydrological surveys
  - Participants: 10 government officials from 6 countries(Cambodia, Ghana, Laos, Mongolia, Uzbekistan, and Vietnam)
  - Date: 25 April 2025

3) 「36th International Environmental Technology Specialized Training Program」 for Capacity building of international Water Resources Professionals
  - Content: Field-based training including an introduction to hydrological survey equipment and hands-on practice
  - Participants: 12 government officials from 7 countries(Algeria, Ghana, Indonesia, Kenya, Oman, Rwanda, and Sri Lanka)
  - Date: 26 June 2025

4) Overseas Environmental Cooperation Networking Program Internship (Ghana, Kenya)
  - Content: A two-week internship program providing customized training, including lectures on hydrological surveys, data analysis, and flood response
  - Participants: Two water resources–related government officials from two countries (Ghana and Kenya)
  - Date: 21 July 2025 – 1 August 2025

5) Capacity-Building Training on the Development of Flood Early Warning Systems in Nepal
  - Content: Hydrological survey theory, AI-based data quality management, advanced discharge measurement and IRDIMS, and field practice
  - Participants: 25 government officials from the Department of Hydrology and Meteorology of Nepal
  - Date: 15–16 October 2025

activities.title: Development of Flood Damage Reduction and Buffering Methodology Using Nature-based Solutions
activities.priority_area_full: Priority Area 1: Scientific Research and Innovation
activities.output_full: 1.6. Scientific knowledge, methodologies and tools in addressing water related disasters, such as flood and drought elaborated and/or enhanced towards timely forecasting.
activities.description:
1. Objective
The objective of the research project is to develop the implementation methodology for creating and operating flood damage reduction and buffering spaces in the extended floodplains to riparian areas in the inland section by using nature-based technology. The main focus is to improve the resilience to extreme flood damage in Korea due to climate change. 

2. Key Findings
The main findings of this research include the design technology of flood damage mitigation spaces and flood control facilities in the channel and riparian area and the assessment of optimal locations and linked operation methods. Also, nature-based technology to use the extended floodplain of flood buffering zone as a carbon sequestration area is developed in this research.
activities.key_activity: 1.6.1. Research and knowledge generation on the scientific advances in addressing and timely forecasting of water related disasters, such as (flash) floods, (flash) droughts and rainfall induced landslides; and on additional impact of synchronous and/or cascading water related hazards, in partnership with EGU, AGU, IAHS ISEH and ICL - International Consortium on Landslides and IPL - International Programme on Landslides including good practices and lessons learned.
activities.outcomes: This year, we conducted reach-scale experiments to advance methods for estimating vegetation-induced flow resistance in river systems, and subsequently carried out reach-scale experimental validation to support the design of flood-buffering spaces and control structures using offline detention basins. All reach-scale experimental results will be utilized to develop technologies that enable practical design, operation, and maintenance of nature-based flood-buffering spaces and flood management facilities. Finally, we also updated the results of growth-chamber experiments to develop an index estimating carbon uptake by riparian vegetation in waterfront zones where flood-buffering spaces are established.

activities.title: Putrajaya Young Ecologist
activities.priority_area_full: Priority Area 2: Water Education in the Fourth Industrial Revolution including Sustainability
activities.output_full: 2.1. Public s awareness at all levels raised towards better understanding their contribution to the import ant multi functions of water in domestic life, ecosystems and productive development
activities.description:
The Young Ecologist Programme is an educational and training initiative designed to engage school children in ecology, conservation, and environmental science. Its main goal is to develop knowledge, skills, and awareness about ecosystems, biodiversity, and sustainable environmental management.

Putrajaya Young Ecologist program was held on 18 September 2025 at Wetland Park. The programme was divided into two categories — Primary and Secondary Schools. It was attended by 100 primary school students, 50 secondary school students and 10 facilitators from Ekorelawan Club, National University of Malaysia.

The main objective of this programme was to expose students to the career of an ecologist. It also aimed to provide knowledge about the development of urban habitats and ecosystems of Putrajaya Lake and Wetland (Environment & Ecosystem Educational Programme), as well as to instill and nurture a sense of belonging among the community towards Putrajaya Lake and Wetland.
activities.key_activity: 2.1.5. Capacity building of young generation through mass media using easily digestible information on extreme water-related hazards and related technical and ecohydrological solutions.
activities.outcomes:
Output:
A structured environmental education module was developed to introduce school children to freshwater ecosystem science and wetland management. The programme produced a set of hands-on learning activities that combine theory with practical field exposure. Key components implemented included: 

1. Educational briefing module on the function, design and management of Putrajaya Lake and Wetland, covering aspects such as water quality, ecological functions of wetlands, and biodiversity conservation.

2. DIY Mini Floating Wetland activity, where participants constructed small-scale floating wetland models using plants and simple materials to demonstrate how aquatic vegetation can naturally filter pollutants and improve water quality. 

3. Insect sampling and identification activity as part of a basic bioassessment exercise, allowing participants to collect and observe aquatic insects as biological indicators of ecosystem health. 

4. Guided field exposure at the wetland site to help participants relate scientific concepts to the real management practices implemented at Putrajaya Lake and Wetland. 

Outcome / Impact: 
The programme strengthened environmental literacy among participants by providing practical understanding of water ecosystem processes and wetland functions. Participants developed basic scientific inquiry skills such as observation, sampling, and interpretation of ecological indicators. The activity also cultivated appreciation of Putrajaya Lake and Wetland as an integrated water management system and encouraged school children engagement in environmental stewardship and conservation.
activities.partners: Local community, Private Companies (Alam Sekitar Malaysia Sdn Bhd & Selancar Unggul Resources Sdn Bhd) and Higher learning institution (National University of Malaysia, Ekorelawan Club)
activities.stakeholder_group_type: Community Groups (local communities, resident organizations) or Community-Based Organizations (local groups focused on specific water-related issues or projects, indigenous and traditional water management practices)
activities.notes:
The programme is implemented on a continuous basis as an annual initiative. Through this programme, participants are expected to progressively enhance their knowledge, awareness, and appreciation of environmental conservation.

Participants are also encouraged to extend and share the knowledge and practices they acquire with others, including their school communities, friends, and family members. This cascading approach is expected to broaden the programme’s impact and foster a stronger culture of environmental responsibility within the wider community.

activities.title: Studying the dynamics of сryosphere of Central Asia
activities.priority_area_full: Priority Area 1: Scientific Research and Innovation
activities.output_full: 1.1. International scientific cooperation strengthened and fostered to address unsolved problems in hydrology, improving scientific understanding of hydrological cycles across river basins and aquifers.
activities.description:
Organized and successfully completed:
1.	Year-round monitoring of cryosphere dynamics on the basis of three high mountain research stations on the Northern Tien Shan with an annual report on the mass balance of Tuiyksu Glacier to the World Glacier Monitoring Service (Switzerland). 
2.	Targeted financing program «Glacial systems of transboundary basins of Central Asia: status, current and forecast changes, role in ensuring water security of the countries of the region»;
3.	GEF-UNDP-UNESCO project on “Strengthening the resilience of Central Asian countries by enabling regional cooperation to assess glacio-nival systems to develop integrated methods for
sustainable development and adaptation to climate change”.
4.	 UNESCO-Adaptation Fund regional project “Reducing vulnerabilities of populations in the Central Asia region from glacier lake outburst floods in a changing climate”.
activities.key_activity: 1.1.1. Coordination of UNESCO scientific efforts on Unsolved Problems in Hydrology, including hydrogeology/geo hydrology, in partnership with IAHS, IAH and other water related scientific associations, including o rganization of the capitalisation of knowledge, res ults and experience available in the UNESCO Water Family, incl. the Flagships, into published syntheses.
activities.outcomes:
As a result of research, for the first time, we found a clear discrepancy between the results of previous glaciers inventories of the Syrdaria basin and the real ones and substantiated the strategy for solving the problem based on the methodology we proposed for operational monitoring of mountain glacial systems and justified the conclusions that:
- the stability of the average characteristics of the rivers flow in the region under conditions of glaciation degradation is ensured by the participation of ground ice in meltwater runoff and a large proportion of precipitation (more than 50% of the annual amount) formed due to intraregional moisture circulation;
- the incoming part of the water balance of the territory of the region's river flow formation zone has been relatively stable over the past century, and the rapidly growing water shortage in the countries of the region is caused by increase in water demand due to increase in the population and economy needs as well us due to unsatisfactory condition of irrigation systems.
The research results are the basis for the development of the water sector of the economy of Kazakhstan and neighboring countries of Central Asia and basis for agreed decisions on the interstate use of regional water resources.

Le congrès visait principalement à :

Promouvoir le dialogue international sur les grands défis liés à l’eau dans un contexte de changement climatique et de pressions croissantes sur les ressources hydriques.

Partager les innovations scientifiques et technologiques dans les domaines de la gestion des ressources en eau.

Renforcer la coopération internationale entre gouvernements, chercheurs, institutions et acteurs du secteur privé.

Identifier des solutions d’adaptation pour garantir la sécurité hydrique et soutenir les politiques publiques de l’eau

activities.outcomes:
Le congrès s’est conclu par l’adoption de la “Déclaration de Marrakech”, appelant à placer l’eau au cœur des priorités internationales face aux défis climatiques, économiques et sociaux.

Cette déclaration encourage notamment :

l’intégration de l’eau dans les politiques climatiques et de développement,

l’accélération de l’innovation et de la coopération internationale,

et le renforcement des actions pour atteindre l’Objectif de Développement Durable n°6 (eau et assainissement).

activities.title: Strengthening Sustainable Water Resources Management and Ecosystem Services Through Ecohydrology and Nature-Based Solutions
activities.priority_area_full: Priority Area 4: Integrated Water Resources Management under conditions of Global Change
activities.output_full: 4.6. Undertaking and sharing assessment of ecosystem services and environmental flows in ecohydrology pilot sites by the scientific community supported, to improve integrated water resources management.
activities.description: The Asia Pacific Centre for Ecohydrology (APCE), operating under UNESCO in Indonesia, exemplifies a pioneering approach to sustainable water management throughout the Asia-Pacific region. Central to APCE’s mission is the integration of ecohydrology principles, which emphasize the dynamic relationships between water, ecosystems, and human activity. Guided by this framework, the Centre advances capacity-building, innovative technologies, and stakeholder engagement to address pressing water management challenges while aligning with the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals, particularly SDGs 6, 13, 15, and 17. A flagship initiative highlights the enhancement of the Subak irrigation system in Bali, an ancient, community-based agricultural network. By engaging local farmers, government agencies, and environmental organizations, APCE fosters collaboration that merges indigenous knowledge with modern ecohydrological nature-based solutions (NBS). This synthesis promotes the sustainable management of water resources and supports ecosystem services that underpin both biodiversity and cultural heritage. The project underscores the importance of inclusive dialogues and knowledge-sharing as foundational to equitable and effective water governance. For instance, the joint efforts between Tabanan Regency and the University of Muhammadiyah Malang (UMM) have yielded successful organic rice harvests, symbolizing the tangible benefits of aligning traditional practices with NBS. APCE’s presentation at the 10th World Water Forum 2024 in Bali further disseminated these insights, encouraging global adoption of ecohydrological approaches. Ultimately, APCE’s work demonstrates that harmonizing local wisdom with science-based nature solutions enhances resilience, sustainability, and productivity in water resource management — a vital stride toward securing water ecosystems for future generations.
activities.key_activity: 4.6.2. Development/dissemination of case studies from current ecohydrology sites to improve the understanding of water ecosystem human interactions and highlight ecohydrology-NBS synergies.
activities.outcomes:
The activity focused on strengthening sustainable water resources management and ecosystem services in the Subak irrigation system through the application of ecohydrology and nature-based solutions (NBS). The Asia Pacific Centre for Ecohydrology (APCE), under UNESCO’s auspices, implemented a collaborative approach that engaged local farmers, government agencies, and environmental organizations in Bali, Indonesia. This initiative developed and promoted capacity-building programs that integrated local knowledge and ecohydrological principles to enhance water management sustainability within the Subak system.
A key development was the adaptation of nature-based solutions tailored to the unique cultural and ecological context of the Subak irrigation network. These solutions aimed to improve water quality and availability, ecosystem health, and agricultural productivity, especially within community-managed landscapes. The project involved knowledge exchange, stakeholder dialogues, and the use of innovative ecohydrological tools to balance water use with ecosystem conservation.
The outcome of this initiative was significant. The collaboration led to tangible improvements in sustainable agricultural practices, demonstrated by successful organic rice harvests in partnership with Tabanan Regency and the University of Muhammadiyah Malang (UMM). This not only reinforced food security but also preserved the cultural heritage and biodiversity of the region. Additionally, the activity fostered resilience and adaptability in water governance systems, supporting broader sustainable development goals. The initiative therefore contributed valuable models for sustainable water resource management and ecosystem service enhancement through nature-based solutions in the Asia-Pacific region.

activities.title: Putrajaya Lake and Wetland Explorace 2025
activities.priority_area_full: Priority Area 2: Water Education in the Fourth Industrial Revolution including Sustainability
activities.output_full: 2.1. Public s awareness at all levels raised towards better understanding their contribution to the import ant multi functions of water in domestic life, ecosystems and productive development
activities.description:
Putrajaya Lake and Wetland Explorace is part of the Putrajaya Lake and Wetland Ecohydrology Appreciation Programme organized by Perbadanan Putrajaya through the Environment, Lake & Wetland Division, Department of City Planning. The 2025 edition marked the 12th year of the programme since it was first introduced in 2011.

The Putrajaya Lake and Wetland Explorace was held on 4 October 2025, attracting strong participation from various sectors. A total of 102 teams (204 participants) took part in the competition, representing 18 public and private universities (IPTA/IPTS) across Peninsular Malaysia from government agencies, statutory bodies, and private organizations. A total of 84 youth facilitators were involved as part of a Training of Trainers (ToT) initiative, where they were trained and empowered to assist in conducting the tasks effectively. Their involvement strengthened leadership capacity among youth while supporting the smooth implementation of the activities.

The event aims to raise awareness and foster a sense of responsibility towards the protection and conservation of clean water resources. It also seeks to promote environmental awareness among the public and university students, while enhancing understanding of the importance of habitats and the rich biodiversity of flora and fauna within Putrajaya Lake and Wetland.
activities.key_activity: 2.1.5. Capacity building of young generation through mass media using easily digestible information on extreme water-related hazards and related technical and ecohydrological solutions.
activities.outcomes:
Output
Putrajaya Lake and Wetland Explorace successfully engaged participants in hands-on environmental learning. Participants worked in teams to complete exploration tasks and challenges at several checkpoints around the lake and wetlands. Through activities such as identifying plant and bird species, solving environmental quizzes, navigating maps, and participating in eco-awareness tasks like participants gained knowledge about wetland ecosystems, water purification functions, and local biodiversity. The program also strengthened teamwork, communication, and problem-solving skills. Documentation including photos, worksheets, and observation records was collected, together with event reports, participant lists, and activity results as evidence of learning outcomes. 

Outcomes 
Putrajaya Lake and Wetland Explorace produced several positive outcomes for participants and facilitators. The program increased environmental awareness by helping participants understand the important roles of wetlands in flood control, water filtration, and habitat protection. Participants also developed more positive attitudes toward nature and conservation areas, leading to a greater appreciation of natural ecosystems. Through the activities, many participants were encouraged to adopt eco-friendly behaviors such as reducing litter, protecting wildlife, and supporting environmental initiatives. The group-based challenges strengthened teamwork by improving communication, leadership, and problem-solving skills among participants. In addition, the activity promoted eco-tourism and outdoor recreation by encouraging people to visit and value natural areas in Putrajaya while highlighting the importance of sustainable environmental practices. Overall, the program also enhanced community engagement by fostering stronger connections between participants, educators, and environmental organizations involved in conservation efforts.
activities.partners: Government Agency - Local Agenda 21 (LA 21) Putrajaya and Private Sectors - Alam Sekitar Sdn Bhd, Selancar Unggul Resourcess, Mamee Double Decker (M) Sdn Bhd, Berjaya Food Bhd

activities.notes: Youth participants, together with facilitators, play an important role as change agents who can influence positive environmental attitudes and behaviours within their communities. By involving young people, the Explorace programme fosters a long-term appreciation for wetland ecosystems while encouraging participants to share the knowledge they gain with their families, peers, and wider communities, thereby creating a cascading effect that broadens public awareness and ultimately promotes stronger community support for environmental sustainability and conservation efforts.

activities.title: EMPOWERING WOMEN THROUGH WATER MANAGEMENT: NATIONAL WATER AND WOMEN CAMP 2025 IN CONJUNCTION OF UNESCO-IHP 50 YEARS ANNIVERSARY
activities.priority_area_full: Priority Area 2: Water Education in the Fourth Industrial Revolution including Sustainability
activities.output_full: 2.1. Public s awareness at all levels raised towards better understanding their contribution to the import ant multi functions of water in domestic life, ecosystems and productive development
activities.description:
The Malaysian National Committee for the International Hydrological Programme (Malaysia Intergovernmental Hydrological Programme) or known as UNESCO-IHP Malaysia is a collaborative programme entity between government agencies under the auspices of UNESCO which is composed of 39 members consisting of Ministries, Departments, Higher Education Institutions and Non-Governmental Organizations (NGOs) related to water in Malaysia. The programme, which was established since 1975, is managed by the Water Resources Management and Hydrology Division under the Department of Irrigation and Drainage of Malaysia and is currently operating under HTC Kuala Lumpur starting in 2024.
In year 2025, UNESCO-IHP Malaysia, in collaboration with various universities, successfully organized the National Water and Women Camp (KAWK) 2025 across three locations: Sarawak, Penang, and Kedah. This initiative aimed to empower women in water management while promoting Sustainable Development Goal 5 (SDG 5): Gender Equality and Women’s Empowerment.
The first camp was conducted on January 19, 2025, in Kota Samarahan, Sarawak, in collaboration with Universiti Malaysia Sarawak (UNIMAS). A total of 35 participants, including homemakers and students, attended the program. The sessions focused on the importance of water conservation at home and the production of soap using used cooking oil.
The second series was held on February 14, 2025, at Upcycle Park, Seberang Perai, Penang, with the support of Universiti Sains Malaysia (USM). This session saw a significant turnout of 104 participants from Puspanita MBSP and their children. Four modules were conducted, covering water conservation at home, the use of mud balls for water purification, water filtration techniques, and the H2O exercise.
The final series took place on February 21, 2025, at Tasik UniSHAMS, Kedah, in partnership with Universiti Islam Antarabangsa Sultan Abdul Halim Mu'adzam Shah (UniSHAMS), Universiti Utara Malaysia (UUM), and Universiti Sains Malaysia. This session gathered 35 women, comprising students, lecturers, and their children. The modules introduced included water filtration methods, bioindicators, compost fertilizers, and the H2O exercise.
activities.key_activity: 2.1.4. Use of networks and partnerships to increase coverage in mass media and social media, including cooperation with journalists on water topics, using easy-to-understand facts, statistics, infographics, and video clips by public figures, also making use of the Global Water Museums Network (WAMU-NET).
activities.outcomes:
Women’s participation in this initiative played a crucial role in advancing SDG 5 by fostering gender inclusivity in environmental sustainability. By engaging women from diverse backgrounds—including students, homemakers, lecturers, and government personnel—the camp provided them with the knowledge and practical skills to become active agents of water conservation and resource management. Women are essential contributors to sustainable development, and their involvement in decision-making processes, community leadership, and environmental stewardship strengthens collective efforts toward achieving global sustainability goals.
Each camp incorporated hands-on activities to educate women on sustainable water management while fostering community engagement. Participants were encouraged to share their experiences and insights, highlighting their role as change-makers in water sustainability. This platform also provided networking and knowledge exchange opportunities, enabling participants to apply their learnings within their respective communities and professions.

activities.title: 1st International UNESCO Water Watch Program for Young Leaders Camp 2025
activities.priority_area_full: Priority Area 2: Water Education in the Fourth Industrial Revolution including Sustainability
activities.output_full: 2.1. Public s awareness at all levels raised towards better understanding their contribution to the import ant multi functions of water in domestic life, ecosystems and productive development
activities.description:
The 1st International UNESCO Water Watch Program for Young Leaders Camp 2025 was successfully conducted from 20 to 22 May 2025 at Glamping Wetland Putrajaya. With the theme “Guardians of Water, Leaders of Change,” the programme was jointly organised by the National Commission for UNESCO Malaysia (SKUM), UNESCO-International Hydrological Programme (UNESCO-IHP) Malaysia, the Department of Irrigation and Drainage (DID/JPS) Malaysia, the Humid Tropics Centre (HTC), and Putrajaya Corporation (PPj).

The programme brought together 80 local and international participants, accompanied by 20 teachers representing 19 secondary schools from 14 states, as well as representatives from four agencies and 14 universities nationwide.

Throughout the three-day camp, participants were exposed to academic presentations and field activities involving 15 interactive modules covering hydrology, water resources, rivers, and the role of water in human life and the environment. Each module was facilitated by instructors representing the participating agencies, beginning with an introduction to the fundamental roles of their respective organisations.

The modules also incorporated the Integrated Water Resources Management (IWRM) approach. Participants were assessed through various two-way communication methods, including quizzes, multimedia videos, and group presentations evaluated by a panel of judges
activities.key_activity: 2.1.2. Capacity building of educators and policy makers on country level including through workshops, webinars and online distant learning methods, e.g. Massive Open Online Courses (on various water related topics with cross cutting emphasis on youth, women and indigenous communities (also see output 2.3).
activities.outcomes:
To provide participants with comprehensive exposure and in-depth understanding of the current status, strategic opportunities, and complex challenges in national water resource management in line with global sustainability principles.

To enhance critical awareness among participants regarding the importance of sustainable water resource management as a fundamental pillar for human survival and the well-being of future generations, aligned with the United Nations Sustainable Development Goal (SDG 6: Clean Water and Sanitation).

To strengthen participants’ understanding of the mandates, functions, and roles of institutions and agencies involved in water management at national and regional levels, and how collaboration among stakeholders contributes to effective water governance.

activities.title: Total Economic Value Ecosystem Services of Putrajaya Lake and Wetland
activities.priority_area_full: Priority Area 2: Water Education in the Fourth Industrial Revolution including Sustainability
activities.output_full: 2.6. Capacities of decision makers, and water managers and key water sector institutions strengthened allowing them to take advantage of new technologies and resea rch to enhance better decisions, design and implementation of integrated and efficient water policies
activities.description: This study evaluates the Total Economic Value (TEV) of ecosystem services provided by Putrajaya Lake and Putrajaya Wetlands to support sustainable lake and wetland management. Using the TEV framework and the The Economics of Ecosystems and Biodiversity (TEEB) approach, the research identifies ecosystem structures, functions, and benefits, and estimates their economic values through several valuation methods including the Hedonic Price Method (HPM), Discrete Choice Experiment (DCE), Travel Cost Method (TCM), direct pricing, and Benefit Transfer Approach (BTA). The results aim to highlight the economic significance of the lake–wetland ecosystem and provide valuable input for environmental decision-making, including sustainable financing mechanisms, payment for ecosystem services, recreation fee determination, natural resource accounting, damage compensation assessments, and the development of an integrated lake basin management plan.
activities.key_activity: 2.6.2. Building capacity to mainstream research recommendations and relevant technology including nature-based solutions/ecohydrology in decision making for middle/ upper-level civil servants, water managers, and professionals.
activities.outcomes:
Output: 
The study produced an economic valuation of ecosystem services at Putrajaya Lake and Wetlands, including the estimation of the Total Economic Value (TEV) and the identification of key ecosystem service categories contributing to the overall value.  The Total Economic Value (TEV) of ecosystem services provided by the Putrajaya Lake and Wetlands is estimated at approximately RM15.16 billion) reflecting the combined benefits of provisioning, regulating, cultural, and supporting services.  These benefits include water purification, flood regulation, biodiversity conservation, recreation, and educational functions. The supporting services are the necessary services for all other ecosystem services, such as soil formation, nutrient cycling and primary production.

Outcome:
The significant economic value of these ecosystem services further reinforces the international recognition of the lake–wetland system as a UNESCO Ecohydrology Demonstration Site under the UNESCO Intergovernmental Hydrological Programme, where it serves as a practical example of applying ecohydrology principles in integrated urban water and ecosystem management. This status highlights the role of Putrajaya Lake and Wetlands as a living laboratory for sustainable water governance and ecosystem-based management, demonstrating how ecological infrastructure can generate substantial socio-economic and environmental benefits.
activities.stakeholder_group_type: Community Groups (local communities, resident organizations) or Community-Based Organizations (local groups focused on specific water-related issues or projects, indigenous and traditional water management practices)
activities.notes: The findings from this study provide a comprehensive understanding of the economic importance of ecological, recreational, and cultural services generated by the lake–wetland system. Importantly, the estimated values can serve as a practical decision-making tool for policymakers and lake managers in prioritizing conservation investments, improving resource allocation, and supporting sustainable development planning. As a way forward, the results can guide future ecosystem monitoring, strengthen environmental policies, and encourage greater integration of natural capital valuation in long-term management strategies for Putrajaya’s aquatic ecosystems

activities.title: Asian Water Development Outlook 2025 (Key Dimension 5)
activities.priority_area_full: Priority Area 1: Scientific Research and Innovation
activities.output_full: 1.6. Scientific knowledge, methodologies and tools in addressing water related disasters, such as flood and drought elaborated and/or enhanced towards timely forecasting.
activities.description: ICHARM participated in a project to develop climate change models for the fifth key dimension, “Water-Related Disaster Security,” in the Asian Development Bank's “Asian Water Development Outlook (AWDO) 2025.” AWDO provides a detailed analysis of water security conditions in the Asia-Pacific region and summarizes key water challenges facing the region. ICHARM was responsible for analyzing future changes in flood risk and drought risk due to climate change across 50 countries and regions in the Asia-Pacific region. The analysis utilized the CMIP5 data analysis tool implemented on Data Integration and Analysis System (DIAS) to select climate models, perform daily rainfall bias correction, and conduct statistical downscaling. For flood risk, rainfall for 25-year return period was used as the indicator, while 3-month Standardized Precipitation Index (SPI3) was used for drought risk. The analysis period defined the current climate as 1981-2000 and the future climate as 2081-2100, using the RCP4.5 representative concentration pathway scenario. For each selected climate model, the ratio of future climate to current climate was calculated. By averaging across models, the future change rates for floods and droughts were calculated for each country and region. The calculated results were each standardized between 0 and 1 and utilized to calculate scores for each country and region across the entire KD5. The final scores were converted into a five-tier evaluation ranging from “Nascent (lowest performance)” to “Model (highest performance).” The final report was published in December 2025.
activities.key_activity: 1.6.2. Science policy dialogue and capacity building on water management that considers wet and dry extremes (floods and drought), including symposia, workshops, and sessions in related events/fora.
activities.outcomes:
Focusing on rainfall for 25-year return period, extreme rainfall is projected to increase across the Asia-Pacific region by the end of this century (2081–2100). This aligns with trends reported in the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change Sixth Assessment Report. It is expected to intensify particularly in high-latitude regions and the equatorial Pacific, though the latter may be influenced by the dataset used for bias correction. In contrast, smaller increases are projected for Central Asia and West Asia. Short-term drought conditions measured by SPI3 are expected to ease in two-thirds of the countries. However, compared to the projections for extreme rainfall, uncertainty is high regarding the outcomes for drought. Furthermore, for the equatorial Pacific, similar to extreme rainfall, the results show greater variability, likely due to the dataset used for bias correction. The calculated flood change rates and drought change rates were used to compute scores for each country and region across the entire KD5. Comparing these results to the previous 2020 findings shows East Asia and parts of Southeast Asia show steady gains, while Central and West Asia has stalled. South Asia sees sporadic progress, and the Pacific continues to fall behind.
Moving forward, we aim to develop a tool to visualize the future flood and drought change rates obtained in this study on a GIS platform, thereby supporting countries in their consideration of climate change adaptation strategies.

activities.title: Knowledge exchange on flood and drought management between South Sudan and Japan
activities.priority_area_full: Priority Area 1: Scientific Research and Innovation
activities.output_full: 1.6. Scientific knowledge, methodologies and tools in addressing water related disasters, such as flood and drought elaborated and/or enhanced towards timely forecasting.
activities.description: ICHARM provided a training program through a study visit to Japan that shared an overview of the science and technology used for monitoring, forecasting, and warning of floods and droughts, demonstrated comprehensive hydrological forecasting, and presented recommendations for developing flood and drought monitoring and early warning systems (EWS) in South Sudan. During the program, practical case studies from Japan were shared, helping to foster an understanding of the underlying science and technology among experts from five African countries (South Sudan, Comoros, Malawi, Madagascar, and Mozambique) and one regional program (NELSAP: the Nile Equatorial Lakes Subsidiary Action Program under the Nile Basin Initiative). As a result, prioritized future steps were proposed to mitigate flood and drought damage in South Sudan.
activities.key_activity: 1.6.2. Science policy dialogue and capacity building on water management that considers wet and dry extremes (floods and drought), including symposia, workshops, and sessions in related events/fora.
activities.outcomes: ICHARM shared examples of scientific methodologies for monitoring and predicting floods and droughts in South Sudan. For floods, the following approaches were introduced: (1) real-time precipitation information with spatiotemporal continuity; (2) local precipitation forecasts using global-scale weather prediction data; and (3) modelling capable of seamlessly simulating river hydrology from low to high water levels. For droughts, the following methodologies were introduced: (1) land surface-vegetation coupled satellite data assimilation techniques; (2) monitoring and forecasting of agricultural drought; and (3) estimation of irrigation water requirements for drought risk mitigation. As a result of the activities, three priority items were proposed as future steps in South Sudan: (1) to demonstrate the usefulness of EWS for society; (2) to quantitatively assess the impacts of climate change on water-related disasters and water use; and (3) to combine structural and non-structural measures to mitigate flood and drought damage based on the information provided by EWS, as well as to formulate adaptation measures based on the climate change impact assessment.

activities.title: The impact of ritual practices on macroinvertebrates in the Bojanala Platinum District, North West Province
activities.priority_area_full: Priority Area 1: Scientific Research and Innovation
activities.output_full: 1.8. Development and sharing of knowledge and innovative solutions on impr oving water quality and reducing water pollution by the scientific community supported and communicated to support science based decision making, improve knowledge, services and reduce health related risks.
activities.description: A trend of sacred ritual practices is increasingly observed across water catchments in South Africa. These human activities may contribute to pollution of natural water bodies, potentially causing a loss of aquatic biodiversity, disrupting ecosystems, diminishing recreational activities and spoiling the sacred natural space. Barnardsvlei, situated along the Sterkstroom River before its water flows into the Buffelspoort Dam, is a well-known site for sacred ritual practices. We employed the South African Scoring System (SASS) version 5 and physicochemical parameters to assess water quality and aquatic habitats. Observations were uploaded to the iNaturalist application for validation. The macroinvertebrates recorded included seven orders: Hemiptera, Coleoptera, Diptera, Odonata, Ephemeroptera, Trichoptera, and Gastropoda, collected from two biotopes, vegetation (SS2) and gravel, sand and mud (SS3). Thirteen biomonitoring events were conducted. In the wet season, samples yielded an abundance of 152, with SS2 scoring 57 individuals, obtaining an Average Score Per Taxon (ASPT) of 3,2 and SS3 scoring 95 (ASPT of 3,6). Similarly, an abundance of 141 was captured during the dry season. The ASPT for SS2 dropped to 2,5 (31 total abundance), while for SS3 it was 3,83 (110 total abundance). The results reflect a poor ecological condition since pollution tolerant species were dominant. Of the 14 families recorded, Gyrinidae (Coleoptera) was the most dominant at SS2, with counts of 86 in the wet season and 107 in the dry season. At the same time, Chironomidae (Diptera) were fewer (<21 individuals) in both seasons at SS2. Also, Heptageniidae (Ephemeroptera) and Coenagrionidae (Odonata) were scarce (<11 individuals) in both seasons at SS2. As seconded by Simpson’s (1-D) index of 0,8094 and 0,8117 for SS2 and SS3, respectively. These preliminary findings suggest that ritual practices at Barnardsvlei may require interventions to safeguard the water quality and the health of users.
