activities.title: Nature-based solutions garden on Arcadia corner
activities.priority_area_full: Priority Area 4: Integrated Water Resources Management under conditions of Global Change
activities.output_full: 4.1. Conducting and sharing of research on inclusive and participatory approaches by the scientific community, to ensu re open, active, meaningful gender responsive engagement of youth, local and indigenous communities supported to enable all stakeholders to be part of the water management process.
activities.description: Urban areas, especially Central Business Districts (CBDs), face increased temperatures and flash floods due to limited natural features and extensive hard surfaces. To address these challenges, students and volunteers at Tshwane University of Technology (TUT), Arcadia Campus, created a nature-based solutions garden on a degraded building site. The project aimed to restore the landscape, manage stormwater, and enhance urban resilience. Four bioretention cells were excavated to trap and filter stormwater runoff from a major arterial road entering the CBD. Instead of flowing directly into the Apies River and raising downstream flood risks, part of the runoff was retained within the garden. Vetiver grass, with roots reaching up to two meters, was planted to stabilize soil and prevent erosion, while indigenous thorn trees were introduced to enrich soil through nitrogen fixation. A hillock made from construction rubble and covered with nutrient-rich soil supports drought-resistant plants such as aloes, euphorbia, and mother-in-law’s tongue. These species conserve water and withstand heat stress, creating a resilient microhabitat. Flowering shrubs and grasses attract pollinators, enhancing biodiversity and ecosystem services. Implemented between October and December 2023, the project received support from the Wildlife and Environment Society of South Africa (WESSA), which donated plants, compost, and tools. Linked to the 16 Days of Activism Against Gender-Based Violence campaign, the garden integrates social awareness with environmental restoration. activities.title: Rehabilitation of The Apies River in Pretoria, South Africa
activities.priority_area_full: Priority Area 4: Integrated Water Resources Management under conditions of Global Change
activities.output_full: 4.5. Understanding and knowledge on pollutants sources, fate and transp ort in freshwater systems, including surface waters (rivers, lakes, wetlands) and groundwater improved by the scientific community and UNESCO Water Family to prevent and reduce water pollution and underpin water resources management strategies.
activities.description: The adoption of the Apies River since 2023 to date stretches from GroenKloof Nature Reserve to inlet into Bon Accord Dam. The activities involved is instream river and riparian zone clean-ups. It also involves monitoring water quality at 5 sites using citizen science tools. It also includes investigation of possible pollution sources in the catchment and reports to the City of Tshwane municipality for fixing, most of which are sewage manholes that overflow. It involved the cleaning of stormwater drains. It also includes awareness campaigns to the community.
activities.key_activity: 4.5.5. Identification and promotion of best practices and appropriate solutions Including ecohydrological nature-based solutions to reduce surface and groundwater pollution; a compendium of such solutions and technologies.
activities.outcomes: The adoption of this stretch of River has resulted in the improvement of water quality two of the sites are now used for demonstration on macroinvertebrates community as the ecological health state has been improving with all these different initiatives. The cleaning of stormwater drains by the community has increased as well. The bad smell from the low water bridge at one of the sites has decreased as the water is no longer stagnant. The number of people joining in the activities more especially the clean-ups and water quality monitoring has increased to having schools coming in to assist.

activities.title: Integrating Traditional Knowledge and Citizen Science for the Protection of Sacred Freshwater Sites
activities.priority_area_full: Priority Area 5: Water Governance based on Science Mitigation, Adaptation and Resilience
activities.output_full: 5.1. Awareness raising of decision makers at all levels on the importance of science based water governance by the UNESCO Water Family supported, to enhance the overall resi lience of communities to effects of global change.
activities.description: The activity is an approach of including the faith-based community (Traditional Healers and traditional churches) into water resources management as they use these water resources most of the time in their practices. They are equipped with the scientific knowledge pertaining to water quality and the health implications of using natural water resources without testing the quality of the resources. The activities include awareness campaigns, co-learning, water quality monitoring using citizen science tools, health and safety measured and solid waste removal.
activities.key_activity: 5.1.2. Active participation and engagement in international and regional campaigns/processes to promote the role of science-based water governance in resilience against global changes.
activities.outcomes: Awareness campaigns have been conducted since 2022 specifically for the faith-based community and the materials used to share knowledge have been prepared specifically to suit their needs as the users of these raw water resources. Monitoring water quality using citizen science tools has been conducted at the sites they use for their practices which include, healing (bathing), purging and others which all use these resources through ingestion of full body contact. We have seen a well aware community of practice that used these water resources with caution and also monitoring while they clean-up these sacred sites. Through their influence in the society there are environmental improvements in the catchments.

activities.title: Citizen Science in the school environment
activities.priority_area_full: Priority Area 2: Water Education in the Fourth Industrial Revolution including Sustainability
activities.output_full: 2.3. Teaching and learning materials on water related matters f or formal, non formal and informal education at all levels elaborated towards a better understanding of the importance of water in lives and communities.
activities.description: The approach involves the inclusion of citizens science knowledge to the young school children. This is done mostly on environmental recognized international and nations days. The kids range from early development stage to grade 12 school learners. The learners are equipped with basic water quality monitoring onsite (school grounds) by bringing the samples to the school or in the field where they become part of the process from basic catchment understanding and how the catchment links with the water resources. They observe the collection of the sample in the water resource; they analyze and interpret the sample and when possible, take action (investigate possible pollution sources and clean-up campaigns).
activities.key_activity: 2.3.1. Compilation, harmonization, and dissemination, including to university libraries and for early, primary, and secondary education of UNESCO Water Family-based training materials and others related to importance of the interactions of water in lives, communities and ecosystem processes.
activities.outcomes: The initiative has led the  Education iDepartment ofn allowing citizen science as one of the supporting tools as it is an out of the classroom experience. The initiative has led to schools supporting the environmental days and thus for us sharing the knowledge of environmental protection to the young generation. We have seen some schools also using citizen science for assignments which we go into the field with them for the hands-on experience. We have also been invited to schools to share the knowledge with the actual sample brought to the school. We have also seen more ecological clubs being included in the schools.

activities.output_full: 1.7. Scientific studies, thematic workshops, and science-based support to policy makers and managers on “Water in the Anthropocene” (e.g. Water Management in Coastal Areas; Water and Land Management in Low Lying River Deltas; Aqui fer Systems; Water management in Urban Environments; Management of Hydrosphere-Cryosphere-Climate Change Nexus).

activities.stakeholder_group_type: Community Groups (local communities, resident organizations) or Community-Based Organizations (local groups focused on specific water-related issues or projects, indigenous and traditional water management practices)
activities.notes:
In 2025, the Manglaralto River–Aquifer System consolidated its recognition as a UNESCO Ecohydrology Demonstration Site, strengthening coordination among academia, the local community, and national and international institutions. This designation validated the technical and social work carried out since 2006 and positioned the site as a regional benchmark for the application of nature-based solutions for water management in semi-arid environments.
The activities carried out during the year demonstrate effective integration of research, outreach, and environmental education. Scientific and academic events facilitated the dissemination of results, knowledge exchange, and the projection of the community-based management model to other contexts in Latin America and the Caribbean. At the local level, workshops, awareness campaigns, and educational tools enhanced social appropriation of knowledge and reinforced shared responsibility in water resource management. Monthly aquifer monitoring and associated research initiatives generated key technical data to support decision-making processes, particularly regarding saline intrusion dynamics and climate variability. The research projects and scientific publications produced in 2025 reflect sustained progress in applied knowledge generation, with both academic and territorial impact.
Overall, the results indicate that participatory management of the Manglaralto River–Aquifer System constitutes a viable strategy to strengthen water security, advance environmental education, and contribute to the Sustainable Development Goals, particularly SDG 6. Future efforts should prioritise long-term monitoring, expanded international cooperation, and the consolidation of financial mechanisms to ensure the Demonstration Site's sustainability.

activities.title: Training Workshop on Water Information Network Systems (WINS), for IHP National Committees in West Africa;
activities.priority_area_full: Priority Area 3: Bridging the data knowledge gap
activities.output_full: 3.3. Comparing and validating open access data on water quantity, quality and use and their sharing by the scientific community supported for sustainable water management.
activities.description:
The 2-day workshop was organized to build the capacity of the National IHP Committee Chairs/Focal Points on sustainable management of water resources and in using Water Information Network System (WINS) thereby contributing to the IHP-IX Strategic Plan, for achieving the SDG 6.
The specific objectives of the Workshop are to:
i) build capacity of the NCs on areas of weakness as identified in the 2021 baseline study; 
ii) expose the IHP Chair/Focal Points to WINS; 
iii) adopt a concept note for project(s) in the region in taking forward the recommendations of the baseline study.
Participants for the Workshop comprised mainly Chairs and Deputies of the IHP National Committees from eight (8) West African countries namely Benin, Cote d’Ivoire, Ghana, Guinea, Liberia, Nigeria, Sierra Leone and Togo. In addition, other participants were drawn from UNESCO Abuja Regional Office, the RC-IRBM and National Water Resources Institute (NWRI) Kaduna Nigeria. A total of twenty-five (25) participants attended the workshop.
The methodology adopted for delivering the training focused on knowledge sharing using presentations, interactive discussions, case studies, provision of question-and-answer sessions and hands-on activities on practical application of the WINS. The training also included a session for development of project idea(s) for the region for immediate implementation by the participants as an output of the workshop activities

activities.title: REGIONAL WORKSHOP ON GOVERNANCE MECHANISM FOR COOPERATION ON CONJUNCTIVE WATER RESOURCES MANAGEMENT IN THE NB-ITTAS REGION
activities.priority_area_full: Priority Area 4: Integrated Water Resources Management under conditions of Global Change
activities.output_full: 4.9. Implementing integrated water resources management at all levels, through transboundary cooperation as appropriate by Member States, supported, in coordination with UN Water and UNECE, to achieve SDG target 6.5.
activities.description:
The Regional Workshop on Governance Mechanism for Cooperation on Conjunctive Water Resources Management in the NB-ITTAS Region was held from December 10th to 11th, 2025 in Abuja, Nigeria. It was organized by UNESCO in partnership with the Regional Centre for Integrated River Basin Management (RC-IRBM) and the workshop served as a concluding activity for Component 4 of the GEF-Project (2019–2025). The project focuses on improving knowledge-based management and governance of the Niger River Basin and the Iullemeden-Taoudeni/Tanezrouft Aquifer System (ITTAS). The primary goal was to finalize a flexible governance framework to support Conjunctive Water Management (CWM), the coordinated management of surface and groundwater as a single resource. Key objectives included:
1.	Sharing global and regional best practices in integrated water management.
2.	Reviewing and refining a draft flexible governance framework based on shared problems rather than traditional basin-wide treaties.
3.	Strengthening political and technical commitment to regional coordination.
4.	Fostering institutional readiness for sustained implementation beyond the project’s 2025 lifespan.
The workshop adopted a hybrid format, bringing together approximately 40 participants. Representation included:
•	National Focal Points for NB-ITTAS Project and OSS from nine countries, namely: Benin, Burkina Faso, Cameroon, Côte d’Ivoire, Guinea, Mali, Niger, Nigeria, and Chad (Algeria and Mauritania were not represented).
•	Key Institutions such as: UNESCO, NBA, AIDA, Sahara and Sahel Observatory (OSS), UNESCO-IHP, and various national water ministries.
activities.key_activity: 4.9.5. Providing support and capacity building to countries, including through knowledge generation, compilation and publication of state and trends on wat er cooperation, including recommendations, guidelines, and good practices and using monitoring and using integrated water resources management through transboundary cooperation, when applicable, as a basis to foster cooperation.
activities.outcomes:
The workshop concluded with the following results:
•	A formal affirmation of the need for CWM and a call for all partners and countries to support its implementation.
•	Identification of good practices and challenges (e.g., data gaps, pollution, and climate variability) across the 11-country region.
•	Agreement on the necessity of a second phase of the project to deepen the gains made since 2019 and ensure financial sustainability.
•	Policy Path: All issues related to the political or legal governance of the basin will be reported back to national leadership and further deliberations and decisions to be made through the Niger Basin Authority (NBA).

activities.title: Participatory Ecosystem Services Shared Value Assessment of Putrajaya Lake and Wetland
activities.priority_area_full: Priority Area 2: Water Education in the Fourth Industrial Revolution including Sustainability
activities.output_full: 2.6. Capacities of decision makers, and water managers and key water sector institutions strengthened allowing them to take advantage of new technologies and resea rch to enhance better decisions, design and implementation of integrated and efficient water policies
activities.description:
The Participatory Ecosystem Services Shared Value Assessment of Putrajaya Lake and Wetland was conducted to assess community and stakeholder perceptions while strengthening communication and collaboration among stakeholders in managing the lake and river system.
The study aims to develop a comprehensive understanding of stakeholder views and to identify the key ecosystem services provided by the Putrajaya Lake and Wetland. Using participatory approaches such as surveys, interviews, and stakeholder workshops, the research collected data on the ecological, social, and economic values associated with the lake and wetland ecosystem.
Two focus group discussion sessions were held on 19 February 2025 in conjunction with the International Colloquium: Towards Sustainable Lake Basin Management: Strengthening Community Involvement. The sessions served as a platform for stakeholders to share perspectives, experiences, and expectations related to the sustainable management of the lake and wetland.
More than 40 agencies representing government agencies, community groups, environmental organizations, recreational users, and Putrajaya staff contributed to the discussions. Their participation provided valuable insights, inputs, and shared aspirations for ensuring that Putrajaya Lake and Wetland continue to be effectively managed and capable of meeting environmental, social, and community needs in the future.
activities.key_activity: 2.6.2. Building capacity to mainstream research recommendations and relevant technology including nature-based solutions/ecohydrology in decision making for middle/ upper-level civil servants, water managers, and professionals.
activities.outcomes:
Output
The study found that community awareness of basin threats is relatively low. However, communities generally recognize the Federal, State, and Local Governments as key agencies that have taken relevant actions in basin governance. The findings also highlight the need for stronger participation from private companies and premises to support basin management. In addition, the governance pillars requiring the most improvement are policy, followed by financing and institutional strengthening, to ensure more effective and sustainable basin management.
Outcome
The study contributes to improved environmental governance by strengthening communication and collaboration among stakeholders involved in the management of the Putrajaya Lake and Wetland ecosystem. It promotes more inclusive and transparent decision-making while increasing public awareness of the importance of ecosystem services and community stewardship. The findings also provide evidence-based insights to support future policies, planning, and conservation initiatives. Overall, the study supports the long-term sustainable management and ecological resilience of the Putrajaya Lake and Wetland by balancing environmental protection, recreational use, and urban development.
activities.partners: National Water Research Institute (NAHRIM)
activities.stakeholder_group_type: Community Groups (local communities, resident organizations) or Community-Based Organizations (local groups focused on specific water-related issues or projects, indigenous and traditional water management practices)
activities.notes: The study highlights several management measures to further strengthen the sustainability of Putrajaya Lake and Wetland. These include improving park facilities, implementing staged wetland restoration with appropriate control measures, and strengthening existing by-laws. Enhanced enforcement on grey water discharge from commercial premises is also essential to protect water quality. In addition, increasing public awareness and organizing joint community programs can encourage greater community participation. Support from private sectors and premises surrounding the lake through contributions and funding is also encouraged. Overall, the research offers practical policy recommendations and management strategies to support integrated lake and river basin management by the Perbadanan Putrajaya.

activities.title: The Denmark Strategic Sector Cooperation (SSC) Initiative
activities.priority_area_full: Priority Area 1: Scientific Research and Innovation
activities.output_full: 1.3. Research on uncertainty in climatic scenarios, hydrological projections and water use scenarios conducted and recommendations communicated to decision makers and the general public to elaborate adaptive water management strategies
activities.description: Denmark SSC Initiative provides Danish development funding for partnerships between Danish Public Authorities and their counterparts in strategically important developing countries and growth economies to work together to improve the framework conditions for furthering sustainable development in various sectors such as Environmental Protection Agency, Energy Agency and Veterinary and food Administration. A Strategic Sector Cooperation (SSC) between Denmark and Kenya on water was initiated. As part of the SSC Water Kenya (2025-2027), output includes the development of an initial hydrogeological model as a demonstration project. The hydrogeological model is expected to form the basis for a subsequently hydrological model, which will enable water particle tracking, estimation of sustainable groundwater extraction and identification of recharge areas.
activities.key_activity: 1.3.2. Research and preparation of state-of-the-art publications on uncertainty in climatic scenarios, hydrological projections and water use scenarios and intersectoral consultations among research teams (including publication and dissemination of Water Outlook).
activities.outcomes:
As part of the SSC Water Kenya (2025-2027) the output includes the development of an initial hydrogeological model as a demonstration project. Central to this output is a robust capacity-building and training component designed to empower local water authorities through hands-on technical workshops and collaborative modeling sessions. The hydrogeological model is expected to form the basis for a subsequent hydrological model, which will enable:
•	Water particle tracking for pollution pathway analysis.
•	Estimation of sustainable groundwater extraction limits.
•	Identification of critical recharge areas for protection.
By embedding training into the development process, the project ensures that Kenyan water professionals possess the skills to update, manage, and utilize these models for long-term, data-driven decision-making.

activities.title: Establishing Cooperation System and Analysing International Trends for Sustainable Cities focusing on Ecohydrology
activities.priority_area_full: Priority Area 1: Scientific Research and Innovation
activities.output_full: 1.2. Ecohydrology research and innovation at UNESCO designated sites conducted and shared by the scientific community and UNESCO Water Family, communicated to assess the impact of ecohydrological and nature based solutions on water cycles and include such solutions in Integrated Water Resource Management ( and services at all scales and in Sites management.
activities.description: The study aims to examine the concept of ‘ecohydrology’, introduce the UNESCO Ecohydrology Demosite in the Republic of Korea, and propose a governance structure for a multidisciplinary and multisectoral basin management to disseminate and further improve its achievements.
activities.key_activity: 1.2.1. Development and operationalization of a world leading network/hub for transdisciplinary ecohydrological research, education and dialogue on ecohydrology and nature-based solutions for enhancement of WBRS+CE catchment sustainability potential (biodiversity, resilience to anthropogenic climate change, ecosystem services and culture and education) and promotion of Ecohydrology Web Platform (http://ecohydrology ihp.org/demosites/).
activities.outcomes:
-UNESCO regional networks and ecohydrological best practices investigated
-Ecohydrological approach in Korean basin management defined
-First two Demosites introduced (Feb ’24) thanks to close collaboration with the local govs
-A multisectoral governance framework proposed

activities.title: Brainstorming Session: International Year of Glaciers' Preservation, 2025 and Sustainable Mountain Development, 2023-2027
activities.priority_area_full: Priority Area 4: Integrated Water Resources Management under conditions of Global Change
activities.output_full: 4.7. Undertaking assessments and developing and sharing of methods to monitor changes in the cryosphere system (glacier, and permafrost), runoff formation from melting glaciers erosion and sediment transport, glacier fed reservoirs such as mountain lakes, and aquifers, by the scientific community supported for improved understanding of their potential use to inform decision makers at all levels
activities.description: Brainstorming session that was organised as a contribution to the roadmap of the International Year of Glaciers' Preservation, 2025. The session provided a platform for stakeholders to brainstorm, collaborate, and exchange ideas to contribute to the planning and implementation of the International Year.
activities.key_activity: 4.7.3. Focused research and knowledge generation and dissemination, including International symposium on the scientific understanding on current and future water availability and the risks from highly glacierized basins; IHP position paper to guide forthcoming research.
activities.outcomes: Defined pathways for implementing the International Year of Glacier Preservation 2025. Presentation of a concept note for collaborative input. 102 participants from 16 countries attended, offering diverse perspectives. The concept note outlined objectives, activities, and financial support. Proposed activities include a global campaign and an international conference. The conference aims to share knowledge and promote action. Emphasized dialogue to foster collaboration and solutions. Highlighted research, workshops, advocacy, and partnerships.

activities.title: The first international drought symposium and workshop
activities.priority_area_full: Priority Area 1: Scientific Research and Innovation
activities.output_full: 1.6. Scientific knowledge, methodologies and tools in addressing water related disasters, such as flood and drought elaborated and/or enhanced towards timely forecasting.
activities.description:
This symposium and workshop aimed to help participants understand the causes of drought, ways to mitigate its effects and monitor drought events.

Topics that are covered:

- Understanding drought and its impact on the environment
- Drought analysis advancements using drought indices
- Drought under changing climate and drought risk assessment
- Early warning systems for drought risk reduction
- Nature-based solutions (strategies for conserving water during a drought)
- Drought monitoring via citizen of science and internet of things (IoT) approach
- Hands on exercise

The workshop featured expert speakers and interactive sessions, allowing participants to learn and share their experiences with others.
activities.key_activity: 1.6.2. Science policy dialogue and capacity building on water management that considers wet and dry extremes (floods and drought), including symposia, workshops, and sessions in related events/fora.
activities.outcomes: More than 100 scholars, students, researchers and policy makers exchanged ideas, knowledge and experiences on drought, nature-based solutions and internet of things (IoT sensors/technologies). 30 persons followed the hands on workshop.

activities.title: Southern Iran Coastal Climate Park with Integrated Watershed Management Approach
activities.priority_area_full: Priority Area 5: Water Governance based on Science Mitigation, Adaptation and Resilience
activities.output_full: 5.1. Awareness raising of decision makers at all levels on the importance of science based water governance by the UNESCO Water Family supported, to enhance the overall resi lience of communities to effects of global change.
activities.description:
This plan has been designed considering the specific conditions of the coastal areas in southern Iran (Hormozgan, Bushehr, Sistan and Baluchestan, and Khuzestan provinces) and emphasizes integrated watershed management as a key solution for addressing climate change. This approach includes watershed management activities, groundwater management, development of vegetation cover, capacity building for local communities, collaboration among executive agencies, and support for research related to reducing greenhouse gas emissions, adaptation, and resilience.

General Objectives of the Plan:

    To protect and restore coastal ecosystems through integrated watershed management.
    To reduce risks arising from climate change, such as drought, flash floods, and soil erosion.
    To develop vegetation cover to increase carbon sequestration, reduce erosion, and improve soil quality.
    To build capacity and empower local communities for active participation in natural resource management and climate change adaptation.
    To collaborate among executive agencies for the successful implementation of the plan and to create coordination among different sectors.
    To support research related to reducing greenhouse gas emissions, adaptation, and resilience to climate change.
    To attract sustainable tourism and create economic opportunities for local communities.
activities.key_activity: 5.1.1. Organizing, co-organizing sessions in intergovernmental meetings, UN platforms and processes, and major international and regional events with relevant tailored messages and science-based governance recommendations.
activities.outcomes:
Main Components of the Plan:

    Integrated Watershed Management
        Planning for the development and expansion of integrated watershed management patterns in coastal areas: to reduce surface runoff and increase water infiltration into the ground, based on the framework document of integrated watershed management and guidelines for participation and empowerment of local communities and coordination among executive agencies.
        Implementation of sustainable agricultural practices.
        Management of surface runoff: using drainage systems and flood control channels.
        Rehabilitation of qanats and wells: to improve access to water in dry and semi-dry areas.
        Application of modern groundwater management methods: such as injecting water into underground layers.

    Vegetation Development
        Planting native and drought-resistant plants: such as tamarisk, acacia, and prosopis to stabilize soil and reduce erosion.
        Restoration of mangrove forests: for coastal protection and biodiversity enhancement.
        Establishment of green belts: to reduce the effects of dust storms and improve air quality.
        Sustainable management of pastures.
        Management of critical wind erosion sites.

    Capacity Building and Empowerment of Local Communities
        Training local communities: conducting workshops on integrated watershed management and sustainable natural resource management.
        Establishing local organizations: forming local groups to participate in the implementation and oversight of projects.
        Economic empowerment: creating job opportunities in areas related to parks, such as sustainable tourism, sustainable agriculture, and handicrafts.

    Collaboration Among Executive Agencies
        Inter-sectoral coordination: creating joint committees among executive agencies such as the Ministry of Jihad Agriculture, Ministry of Energy, Department of Environment, and Cultural Heritage Organization, led by the Provincial Governor and the planning and budgeting organizations of the province.
        Budget and resource allocation: attracting financial and technical support from executive agencies for project implementation.
        Monitoring and evaluation: establishing monitoring systems to assess project performance and provide periodic reports using participatory monitoring models.

    Support for Relevant Research on Emission Reduction and Adaptation
        Establishing research centers: to study the impacts of climate change on water, soil, and coastal ecosystems.
        Research projects: supporting research projects on reducing greenhouse gas emissions, developing eco-friendly technologies, and increasing the resilience of local communities.
        Collaboration with universities and research institutions: creating a network of researchers and specialists for developing innovative solutions to combat climate change.
        Implementation of pilot projects: testing and executing new solutions on a small scale to reduce emissions and enhance resilience.

    Educational and Demonstration Area
        Establishing educational centers for local communities and visitors about the importance of integrated watershed management.
        Showcasing successful watershed management projects in various regions of Iran.
        Using models and interactive exhibits to explain watershed management processes.

    Water Management Systems
        Highlighting indigenous and local patterns of water resource extraction and management in coastal areas.
        Creating systems for collecting and treating rainwater to alleviate pressure on freshwater resources.
        Utilizing natural methods such as artificial wetlands for wastewater treatment.
        Implementing seawater desalination projects using renewable energy.

    Attracting Sustainable Tourism
        Developing walking and cycling paths for visitors.
        Offering educational tours about coastal ecosystems and watershed m

activities.title: Hydrometric experiences for extreme events
activities.priority_area_full: Priority Area 3: Bridging the data knowledge gap
activities.output_full: 3.4. Capacity of scientific community strengthened to develop, share and apply scientific tools for data processing (like data assimilation and visualization methods, quality assurance protocols to connect existing databases and outreach protocols).
activities.description: In LAC, there is a lack of validated river flow and velocity data to inform decision makers and improve early warning systems for extreme events. The webinar "Hydrometric Experiences for Extreme Events" explored the implementation of new hydrometric technologies in Latin America and the Caribbean (LAC). Dr. Antoine Patalano presented the use of LSPIV to monitor rivers, and Dr. Waldo Lavado Casimiro presented on experiences in hydrometry in Peru. The seminar promoted the exchange of hydrometric experiences and case studies to strengthen professional capacities in the region. The focus on innovative technologies aims to improve the availability and accuracy of hydrometric data, crucial for water management and water security.
activities.key_activity: 3.4.2. Capacity development of stakeholders in public and private sectors, and civil society in hydrological data collection, validation, interpretation and sharing as well as data entry, storage and subsequent access processes.
activities.partners: IHP-LAC working group on Hydrogeomorphology of the Amazon Andean Basin (HIDRICAA), WMM, TEHLA

activities.title:
JRS Biodiversity Foundation funded project on Groundwater Dependent
Ecosystems research in the Khakhea Bray Dolomite Aquifer.
activities.priority_area_full: Priority Area 1: Scientific Research and Innovation
activities.output_full: 1.10. Conducting and sharing of research on integrating citizen science in the hydrological discipline by the scient ific community and other stakeholders supported, to improve understanding of the water cycle enabling science based decision making
activities.description:
The aim of the project was to characterise the Groundwater Dependent Ecosystems (GDEs) in the
Khakhea/Bray Transboundary Aquifer shared between Botswana and South Africa and develop a database using an integrate approach that included Biodiversity/Ecology, Remote Sensing/GIS,
Geohydrology and GESI. The GDE database that produced through the project was linked to the SADC Groundwater Information Portal (SADC-GIP).
activities.key_activity: 1.10.1. Citizen science pilot studies in different regions for water resources monitoring and crowdsourced assessments by local stakeholders, including validation of data quality to ensure adequate accuracy.
activities.outcomes:
Characterisation of the Groundwater Dependent Ecosystems in the Khakhea-Bray Transboundary Aquifer.
Groundwater related Biodiversity/Ecology, Remote Sensing/GIS, Geohydrology and GESI data.
